title.rendered: iPhone Duo: Everything You Need to Know About Apple’s First Foldable iPhone

content.rendered:
Apple introduced iPhone Duo during its September 9 event, making it the company’s first foldable iPhone. The official iPhone Duo product page confirms a 7.6-inch inner display, a 5.4-inch outer screen, and Touch ID in the side button. In the U.S., preorders begin October 16 at 5:00 a.m. PT, with availability starting October 23.

Apple’s pages also draw a useful boundary. The phone uses a two-camera rear system and Touch ID. The battery and performance numbers are Apple’s own test claims.

The same A20 Pro chip powers iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, but those phones use a conventional design and a three-camera Pro system.

Two OLED displays in a foldable design

iPhone Duo has a 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR all-screen OLED folding display on the inside and a 5.4-inch Super Retina XDR all-screen OLED display on the outside. The inner panel has a nano-texture finish and wide-angle OLEDs.

Both screens include Dynamic Island, Always-On display, and ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. Apple lists 1000 nits of typical max brightness, 1600 nits of HDR peak brightness, and 3000 nits of outdoor peak brightness, with a 1-nit minimum brightness.

The official dimensions are:

  • Open: 6.48 inches wide, 4.64 inches high, and 0.21 inches thick.
  • Folded: 3.31 inches wide, 4.64 inches high, and 0.44 inches thick.
  • Weight: 8.96 ounces, or 254 grams.

Apple says the two screens keep a consistent aspect ratio, so content can move between the inner and outer displays without changing its basic shape. It also says the inner display uses multiple thin layers and optically clear adhesives that let the layers glide as the phone folds. The page describes Apple’s foldable display design, but it does not establish how the display will hold up in everyday use.

Titanium, Ceramic Shield, and Touch ID

The frame and hinge cover use Grade 5 titanium. Apple’s technical specifications list Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, Ceramic Shield on the back, and a scratch-resistant coating on the inner display. The phone has an IP68 rating for water and dust resistance, tested to a maximum depth of 6 meters for up to 30 minutes under IEC standard 60529.

iPhone Duo comes in Night Sky and Star White. It uses Touch ID instead of Face ID, with the fingerprint sensor built into the side button. Apple says the same sensor works whether the phone is open or folded.

iOS 27 adds more room for apps

iPhone Duo ships with iOS 27, which Apple has adapted for the two-screen design. In landscape mode, Split View lets you use two apps side by side on the inner display. In portrait mode, the wider layout gives you more room for the keyboard and browsing, while a video can stay pinned at the top as you use another app.

The phone can also sit at different angles. Apple shows it standing in StandBy mode as a clock, photo frame, or widget display. It can sit in a seated position for watching a show or following a workout, and it can stand on its own for hands-free video calls. When closed, the outer display is meant for quick, one-handed use.

The larger canvas also supports Apple Pencil (USB-C), although Apple says that support is coming later this year. For broader software context, see what changed in iOS 27 compared with iOS 26.

A20 Pro and Apple Intelligence

The A20 Pro chip has a 6-core CPU, a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says the Neural Engine is designed for intensive AI workloads and pairs the chip with a vapor chamber thermal management system. Those are Apple’s hardware and performance claims, not independent benchmark or thermal results.

For the chip’s core design, Apple comparisons, and cooling system, see our A20 Pro guide.

Apple Intelligence powers Siri AI on iPhone Duo. Apple describes a more conversational assistant with personal context, broad world knowledge, Camera-based help, intelligent photo editing, and productivity features inside apps. The product page says Siri AI is rolling out in English, and Apple notes that feature availability can vary. The new Apple Intelligence features in iOS 27 provide a wider look at the software update, but the final availability still depends on Apple’s language and regional limits.

Two 48MP rear cameras, with 2x optical-quality zoom

The rear camera system has two listed cameras:

  • 48MP Fusion Main camera with a 26mm focal length, f/1.6 aperture, sensor-shift optical image stabilisation, and support for 24MP and 48MP photos.
  • 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide camera with a 13mm focal length, f/2.2 aperture, and a 120-degree field of view.

Apple lists 2x optical-quality zoom in, 2x optical zoom out, a 4x optical-quality zoom range, and digital zoom up to 10x. Its technical specifications also mention a 12MP optical-quality 2x Telephoto output under the Fusion Main camera. Apple does not list a separate telephoto lens for iPhone Duo, so that 2x mode should not be described as a third rear camera.

The outer camera is a 12MP Centre Stage camera. The inner display has an under-display FaceTime camera that records 1080p video. Apple also lists Smart Take, Duo Preview, Kid Cue, Duo FaceTime, Dual Capture, and Centre Stage for photos and video calls. The current iPhone Duo pages do not give it the separate Pro camera system listed for Apple’s Pro models.

USB-C, MagSafe, Qi2, and eSIM

iPhone Duo has a USB-C connector for charging, DisplayPort output, and USB 3 data transfer at up to 10Gb/s. Its wireless charging system supports MagSafe up to 25W and Qi2 up to 25W.

Apple’s technical specifications list the N1 wireless networking chip, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and the C2 cellular modem. The phone is eSIM-only and supports two active eSIMs while storing eight or more eSIMs. It does not support a physical SIM card.

Battery and charging claims

iPhone Duo uses two built-in rechargeable lithium-ion batteries. Apple claims up to 24 hours of typical use, up to 44 hours of video playback when using the outer display, and up to 31 hours when using the inner display. For streamed video, Apple lists up to 37 hours on the outer display and up to 26 hours on the inner display.

With a 60W-capable adapter or higher and a USB-C cable, Apple says the phone can reach 50% charge in around 20 minutes. With a 35W adapter or higher and a MagSafe Charger, it says 50% takes around 30 minutes. The adapters and MagSafe Charger are sold separately. These figures are Apple’s test claims, not real-world battery results.

U.S. price and availability

Apple’s U.S. Store page lists four storage options for iPhone Duo:

U.S. preorders start Friday, October 16, at 5:00 a.m. PT on Apple’s website and in the Apple Store app. iPhone Duo will be available from October 23 at Apple and through select carriers and partner stores.

content.rendered:
Apple has officially unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at its “Surprise and Shine” event, with both new Pro models arriving with iOS 27. First announced at WWDC 2026, Apple’s latest iPhone software is set to roll out as a free update on September 14. In a surprise move, no iPhones are losing support this year.

If you’re wondering whether your existing iPhone will get the new software, here’s the full list of iOS 27-compatible devices.

iOS 27 supported devices

Apple has confirmed that iOS 27 supports every iPhone capable of running iOS 26, along with the newly launched iPhone lineup.

  • iPhone Duo
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro
  • iPhone 17, iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 17e
  • iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 15, iPhone 15 Plus, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 14, iPhone 14 Plus, iPhone 14 Pro, iPhone 14 Pro Max
  • iPhone 13, iPhone 13 mini, iPhone 13 Pro, iPhone 13 Pro Max
  • iPhone 12, iPhone 12 mini, iPhone 12 Pro, iPhone 12 Pro Max
  • iPhone SE (2nd generation) and newer
  • iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro, iPhone 11 Pro Max

Apple isn’t ending support for any iPhone

The biggest surprise isn’t a new device gaining support. It’s the fact that Apple didn’t remove any.

As a result, the devices many expected to lose support remain compatible with iOS 27.

  • iPhone 11
  • iPhone 11 Pro
  • iPhone 11 Pro Max
  • iPhone SE (2nd generation)

That means the iPhone 11 lineup has now received another year of major iOS support, extending its software lifespan beyond many earlier expectations.

For users still holding onto these devices, iOS 27 extends their run of major software updates by another year.

Will every iPhone get every iOS 27 feature?

The compatibility list may be unchanged, but Apple’s hardware requirements for certain features aren’t. Apple Intelligence, for instance, continues to require an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, or a newer model. That means devices like the iPhone 11 and iPhone 12 series can install iOS 27 but won’t get Apple Intelligence features.

iOS 27 release timeline

Apple released the first developer beta of iOS 27 immediately after the WWDC 2026 keynote.

Another year for the iPhone 11…

With iOS 27, Apple continues its long-standing software support streak by keeping every iPhone supported by iOS 26 on the compatibility list. While some of the newest features remain limited to newer hardware, iPhone 11 users get at least one more year of major iOS updates.

Is your iPhone getting iOS 27? Let us know which model you’re using and whether you plan to install the update in the comments below.

title.rendered: iOS 27 features: Everything Apple announced at WWDC 2026

content.rendered:
iOS 27 is here, and Apple is putting Apple Intelligence at the center of the update. From a rebuilt Siri and AI-powered Shortcuts to new tools in Photos and Safari, the latest iPhone software brings changes to many of the apps people use every day.

The headline addition is Siri AI, a completely rebuilt version of Siri that can understand your personal context, hold natural conversations, and help you complete tasks across apps. But that’s only part of the story. Apple has also upgraded Safari, Photos, Shortcuts, Passwords, Messages, and several other apps while making the entire operating system faster and more responsive.

If you’ve been waiting for Apple Intelligence to move beyond demos and become part of everyday iPhone use, iOS 27 is Apple’s biggest step yet.

Here’s everything new in iOS 27, along with its release date and supported devices.

Table of Contents
  • Siri AI brings conversations, Visual Intelligence, and personal context
  • Safari can organize tabs and monitor websites for you
  • Liquid Glass gets more customization
  • Photos get Spatial Reframing, Extended, and better Clean Up
  • Shortcuts can create automations from natural language
  • Wallet App updates
  • Passwords can automatically update weak passwords
  • Apple Intelligence expands across core apps
  • iOS 27 is faster across the board
  • New parental controls and child safety tools
  • Shared Albums get Android and Windows support
  • iOS 27 compatible devices
  • iOS 27 release date
  • Is iOS 27 worth the upgrade?

Siri AI brings conversations, Visual Intelligence, and personal context

Apple spent years promising a smarter Siri. With iOS 27, it has finally arrived.

Siri AI is a completely rebuilt assistant powered by Apple Intelligence. It can understand information from across your apps, maintain natural conversations, and help complete tasks that previously required jumping between multiple apps.

For example, you can ask Siri where a friend recently moved, find photos from a specific trip, create reminders based on information from the web, or draft a message using details from previous conversations.

Apple has also introduced a dedicated Siri app that stores your conversation history and syncs it across supported Apple devices through iCloud.

Other Siri improvements include:

  • More natural and expressive voices
  • Improved dictation accuracy
  • Visual Intelligence integration
  • Richer conversational responses
  • Better app awareness and task completion

Safari can organize tabs and monitor websites for you

If you’re someone who constantly ends up with dozens of open tabs, Safari finally has a solution.

iOS 27 introduces automatic tab organization powered by Apple Intelligence. Safari can analyze your open tabs, identify related pages, and group them into topics automatically.

For example, if you’re planning a vacation, Safari can place hotel bookings, restaurant research, airline pages, and travel guides into the same group without any manual effort.

Apple is also introducing a new feature called Notify Me.

Instead of repeatedly checking a website for updates, you can ask Safari to watch the page for you. When something changes, such as tickets becoming available or a product returning to stock, Safari sends you a notification.

Safari also gains a feature called Describe an Extension. You can simply describe what you want a website to do, and Safari can create a custom extension that modifies the page accordingly.

Liquid Glass gets more customization

After introducing Liquid Glass last year, Apple is giving users more control over the look of the interface.

A new transparency slider allows you to adjust the appearance of Liquid Glass elements across the system. You can choose a cleaner, more transparent appearance or a stronger tinted effect depending on your preference.

Photos get Spatial Reframing, Extended, and better Clean Up

The Photos app receives three major Apple Intelligence upgrades.

  • Clean Up: Apple has improved the existing Clean Up tool, making it better at removing distracting objects while generating more natural-looking replacements.
  • Extend: The new Extend tool lets you expand the edges of an image, giving you more room for cropping, social media posts, or creative projects.
  • Spatial Reframing: This tool allows you to adjust the camera perspective after the photo has already been taken. You can move subjects into better positions, improve symmetry, and correct framing issues without needing to retake the picture.

Apple uses AI to generate the missing parts naturally, helping edits look more realistic.

Shortcuts can create automations from natural language

The Shortcuts app has always been powerful, but many users found it intimidating. Apple is solving that problem with Apple Intelligence.
Instead of manually building an automation step by step, you can simply describe what you want in plain English.

For example, you can type:

“When I leave work, text my partner that I’m on my way home and include my ETA.”

Shortcuts automatically creates the automation, adds the necessary actions, and even allows you to refine it further using natural language.

For many users, this could be the first time Shortcuts feels approachable.

Wallet App updates

Apple is adding a couple of new features to the Wallet app in iOS 27.

The first is support for digitizing physical passes. Instead of carrying certain paper-based passes, users can add supported versions to Wallet and access them directly from their iPhone.

Apple is also making it easier to split expenses. When paying with Apple Pay, users can divide a bill and settle balances using Apple Cash without switching between multiple apps.

Passwords can automatically update weak passwords

Managing passwords is important, but updating dozens of accounts can be a hassle.

With iOS 27, the Passwords app can automatically update eligible accounts to stronger passwords.

Using Apple Intelligence and Safari together, your iPhone can navigate supported websites, sign in securely, and replace weak credentials with stronger alternatives.

The result is better security with much less effort.

Apple Intelligence expands across core apps

Apple Intelligence is now deeply integrated across the apps many people use every day.

  • In Messages, your iPhone can suggest actions based on conversations, create reminders, and help locate photos mentioned in chats.
  • Mail offers smarter suggestions based on the contents of incoming messages.
  • Calendar can create events simply by understanding natural language.
  • The Phone app gains a feature called Call Context, which can automatically surface useful information before a call. For example, if you’re calling an airline, your iPhone may display the confirmation code it found in Mail so you don’t have to search for it manually.

iOS 27 is faster across the board

Apple also spent time improving performance throughout the operating system.

According to Apple:

  • Apps launch up to 30% faster
  • New photos appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster
  • AirDrop transfers are up to 80% faster
  • Network transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular are more reliable
  • Search results appear faster across Spotlight, Mail, and Photos

Another notable change is an upgraded CPU scheduler for older iPhones. Apple says the improvements extend all the way back to the iPhone 11, helping the devices manage system resources more efficiently.

New parental controls and child safety tools

Families aren’t being left out of this update. iOS 27 introduces Ask to Browse for website approvals, expands Communication Safety to include violent content, and refreshes Screen Time with new controls for managing app access throughout the day.

Shared Albums get Android and Windows support

If you’ve ever created a Shared Album only to realize that some friends or family members couldn’t participate because they use Android or Windows devices, iOS 27 removes that limitation. Apple now lets Android and Windows users join Shared Albums and add their own photos and videos.

Apple is also removing another long-standing limitation. Shared Albums now support full-resolution photos and videos, so the memories you share won’t lose quality in the process.

Must read: How to create a Shared Album on iPhone

iOS 27 compatible devices

Apple is keeping the same compatibility list as iOS 26, meaning every supported iPhone from the iPhone 11 lineup onward can run iOS 27. Moreover, the newly launched iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo will arrive with iOS 27.

However, some Apple Intelligence features will remain limited to newer iPhone models.

iOS 27 release date

Apple unveiled iOS 27 during its WWDC 2026 keynote on June 8, 2026, and the developer beta launched immediately, while the public beta arrived in July 2026.

Apple has scheduled the release of the final version of iOS 27 to all users starting from September 14, alongside its new iPhone lineup.

Is iOS 27 worth the upgrade?

iOS 27 isn’t defined by a single headline feature. Instead, Apple has woven Apple Intelligence throughout the operating system, from Siri and Safari to Photos, Shortcuts, and Passwords. If these features work as advertised, iOS 27 could end up feeling less like a traditional software update and more like a smarter version of the iPhone people already use every day.

Which iOS 27 feature are you most excited to try first? Let us know in the comments below.

  • iOS 27 Reminders App Features

His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. title.rendered: GTA 6 global release times: When does it launch in your region?

content.rendered:
If you’re planning to jump into GTA 6 as soon as possible, you’ll want to pay close attention to its release date and time. Why is that the case? Well, the game won’t have a global release on November 19, 2026. What Rockstar Games is planning this time around is a midnight release in every region.

This means gamers in countries such as New Zealand could get their hands on the game much earlier than those in Central America and Mexico. So, if you’re wondering when exactly GTA 6 will be available in your region, there’s no need to worry, as we’ve got you covered. Let’s take a look at GTA 6 global release times and dates.

GTA 6 launch times by region

As we’ve mentioned before, the GTA 6 release time will depend on your region, with the game becoming available at 12:00 AM local time. Both Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation players will be able to jump into the game at the same time in each region.

If you want to play GTA 6 as early as possible, Xbox players can change their console’s time zone to New Zealand through settings. However, this is a bit complicated on PlayStation as it requires purchasing the game on a new account.

With that in mind, here’s a complete breakdown of GTA 6 global release date and time, starting with the first region to get the game and ending with the last. –

GTA 6 PS5 edition controllers can now be pre-ordered

The GTA 6 pre-orders are now live for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series/X consoles. There are two separate editions to choose from, each with its own perks and cosmetics that you’ll be able to obtain once the game becomes playable on November 19, 2026. However, if you’re a die-hard fan of the franchise and want to get something extra, you can also pick up the exclusive GTA 6 PS5 edition controllers.

In a recent State of Play event, Sony revealed a brand-new DualSense controller based on GTA 6. Available in both black and white variants for $84.99, the controllers fully embody the aesthetic of Leonida, with palm trees on the handles and a giant “VI” logo across the touchpad.

These might seem a bit pricey, but they’re a must-have for collectors and fans. If you want to get your hands on this controller before launch, the GTA 6-themed DualSense controllers are available to pre-order through Sony and major retailers.

Conclusion

Many expected GTA 6 to have a simultaneous global launch, but as we’ve now learned, Rockstar is instead going with a midnight release in each specific region. This does mean that some players will be able to access the game much earlier than others, but there are ways to bypass this limitation depending on which console you’re playing on.

title.rendered: Is GTA 6 coming to PC earlier than expected? Here’s what we know

content.rendered:
Rockstar Games has been keeping fans busy with tons of GTA 6 screenshots and gameplay details, but one thing that’s still unanswered is the PC release date. The game is all set to make its debut on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19, 2026. However, the developer hasn’t uttered a word about a PC release. In the past, Rockstar has taken a year or more to bring its games to PC.

However, things might be a bit different this time around, thanks to a PS5 emulator called KyTyPS5. Although it’s still in development, the emulator might allow PC players to jump onto GTA 6 right after its console release. So, let’s take a look at what we’re talking about

PC Emulators might allow players to run GTA 6

Over the last couple of months, the KyTyPS5 emulator has gained a lot of attention in the gaming community as its developers have continued to make rapid progress. Not too long ago, the emulator was just capable of running simple 3D games. However, the PS5 emulator has reached another level, as it’s now capable of running GTA 5.

Over on X, BrutalSam has shared a video showing GTA 5 running through the KyTyPS5 emulator. It features the game’s prologue of the North Yankton mission running between 40-60 FPS. Of course, the emulator isn’t running the game perfectly. You can see tons of glitches, missing text, weird textures, and crashes. However, it’s still an achievement for the PS5 emulation scene, as even a AAA title like GTA 5 is now playable. The system that’s being used by the emulator is packed with an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT and an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D CPU.

Grand Theft Auto PS5 version PPSA04264 running on PS5 emulator KyTyPS5 forks.

(some of the builds are forks, some are local builds)
(Yes, GTA 5 is on PC, we know that, the point is the progress for big 3D games).

for updates: https://t.co/Hz6VoBrtHh
credit to ihc160/Komary pic.twitter.com/en1iKatnmT

— BrutalSam (@BrutalSam_) September 6, 2026

As we’ve already said before, the GTA 6 PC release date is still unknown. However, if PS5 emulators like KyTyPS5 are able to continue progressing at this pace and become powerful enough to run AAA games, there’s a good chance that GTA 6 could also be playable on PC with the help of emulation. However, this won’t be an easy job. Through the GTA 6 leaks and extended gameplay, it’s quite evident that this game is extremely detailed and graphically demanding to run.

The development team behind the KyTyPS5 emulator would need to do a lot of work before it can even think about running a game as heavy as GTA 6. Also, let’s not forget the fact that anyone who even wants to emulate Rockstar’s next magnum opus would need a high-end gaming PC. It’s going to be interesting to see in the coming months just how far the KyTyps5 emulator progresses, and whether it will allow players to experience GTA 6 on PC before an official port drops.

Rockstar Games could move up the GTA 6 PC release date

It’s heavily speculated that the GTA 6 PC version would debut sometime in late 2027 or early 2028. This comes from the fact that Rockstar has a history of delaying its game releases on PC. While there’s a good chance that the PS5 emulation projects could make the game playable on PC much sooner after launch, it now seems like even Rockstar’s official port could arrive sooner than we expected.

In a recent episode of the VGC podcast, reputable insider Andy Robinson suggested Rockstar might “push up the PC version” of GTA 6. According to him, there’s a lot of chatter in the industry surrounding the possibility of this happening, considering the current state of the hardware market. However, it’s crucial to note that Robinson hasn’t said this is a confirmed report.

The AI trend has hit the hardware market quite hard in the last couple of years. For instance, DRAM prices have reached new highs that have led to increased prices for phones, PCs, and even consoles. If that wasn’t bad enough, PS5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles are facing supply issues thanks to the hype around GTA 6, which will only get even bigger as the game’s launch approaches.

Considering these factors, it makes sense for Rockstar to fast-track development on the GTA 6 PC version. It would allow the game to reach even larger audiences, including those who can’t get their hands on consoles. It’s also worth keeping in mind that the PC gaming market has grown considerably since the developer’s last release in 2018, which has made it a much larger audience that can’t be overlooked. Let’s hope Rockstar soon provides us with more clarity on the GTA 6 PC release date.

  • Why GTA 6 needs a first-person mode

title.rendered: I stopped organizing my photos: Gemini Spark finally does it for me

content.rendered:
My Google Photos library is a mess, and I’m pretty sure I’m not alone in this. We all have thousands of photos, including vacation pictures, family memories, screenshots, duplicate shots, and random images we probably no longer need. I’ve always planned to organize them properly, but honestly, who has the time?

That’s why Gemini Spark caught my attention. Instead of manually sorting photos, creating albums, finding the best shots, and editing images one by one, I can simply tell Gemini what I want done. It can handle multiple photo-related tasks as part of a single workflow.

And honestly, this feels like one of the first genuinely useful AI agents for everyday users. Here’s how to use Gemini Spark with Google Photos.

What is Gemini Spark, and why does it matter for Google Photos?

Gemini Spark is Google’s agent-style AI experience designed to handle tasks and workflows rather than simply answer questions. The difference is important.

Usually, you may ask, “Find my photos from my trip,” and Gemini gives you an answer. But a Gemini Spark workflow can look more like this: “Find the best 15 photos from my trip, enhance the beach photos, create a shared album, and draft an email with the album link.“

Instead of helping me perform each step, Gemini Spark can connect those steps into one workflow. That’s exactly what makes its Google Photos integration more interesting.

Google says Spark can combine actions such as searching and curating photos, editing images, creating albums, sharing them through connected apps, extracting text from images, and scheduling recurring workflows. Overall, it makes turning a giant pile of memories into something useful effortless.

Why I stopped organizing photos manually

I used to think organizing photos was one of those small digital habits I should develop. For example, create albums after every trip, delete blurry photos, separate screenshots from camera pictures, pick the best images, rename important albums, etc.

The problem? Every single one of those tasks sounds easy on its own. Together, they become an exhausting digital chore.

Let’s say you return from a week-long vacation with 800 photos and videos.

Before Gemini Spark, organizing them properly would mean:

  1. Opening Google Photos
  2. Searching through hundreds of images
  3. Identifying duplicates
  4. Choosing the best shots
  5. Editing selected photos
  6. Creating an album
  7. Naming the album
  8. Adding photos
  9. Creating a shareable link
  10. Sending it to friends or family

All of these tasks seem boring and daunting.

Gemini Spark could finally change that by taking a natural-language request and turning it into an actual workflow instead of giving me another feature I have to learn.

The Gemini feature I use most: Finding my best photos automatically

If I had to pick the feature I’m most excited about, it wouldn’t be AI photo editing. It would be finding my best photos and videos.

Gemini Spark can search and curate photos and videos based on subjects, locations, dates, or events. It can also identify the best shots and filter duplicates. This sounds simple, but I think it solves one of the biggest problems with smartphone photography.

We take too many photos and end up with dozens of versions of essentially the same moment. And choosing the good photos afterward looks like a serious manual task. Because they get buried between screenshots, duplicates, accidental photos, and blurry shots.

That’s where I see Spark becoming genuinely useful.

You can give it prompts like:

  • Find the best photos from my birthday celebration last month and remove obvious duplicates from the selection.
  • Find my best landscape photos from 2026.
  • Pick the 20 best family photos from our vacation.

Gemini Spark can also create and organize albums

Creating photo albums is another task I always intend to do and almost never finish.

Gemini Spark can create new private or shared albums and save curated photos into them. This opens up some genuinely useful possibilities.

For example:

  • Create an album with the best photos from my London trip.
  • Find all photos from my sister’s wedding and organize them into an album.
  • Create a private album with my favorite food photos from this year.

The feature becomes more interesting when I combine organization with other actions.

Instead of simply saying, “Create a vacation album,” I could theoretically create a full workflow: “Find the best 50 photos from my recent vacation, enhance the landscape photos, create an album called Summer Escape 2026, and make it ready to share.“

That’s the point at which Gemini Spark starts to feel less like an AI chatbot and more like a digital assistant.

Google also says new albums created by Spark are private by default, which is reassuring. Gemini asks for permission before sharing an album.

The interesting part: Gemini can handle multi-step photo tasks

This is where I think people might underestimate the Google Photos integration. AI search, AI editing, and automatic album creation are useful. But multi-step workflows are where everything starts becoming significantly more powerful.

I tried this feature using these steps:

  1. Launch the Gemini mobile app or go to gemini.google.com.
  2. Tap the Menu icon at the top and select Spark.
  3. In the text box, enter this prompt: Find the best 15 photos from a trip, enhance specific images, add them to a shared album, and draft an email containing the link.
  4. Tap the Submit button.

That workflow crosses several traditionally separate tasks: Google Photos → Image selection → Photo editing → Album creation → Sharing → Gmail.

Normally, I would need to manually jump between multiple screens and apps. Gemini Spark connects them.

Here’s another example I find genuinely interesting: Find the concert schedule in a photo and cross-reference it with my Google Calendar to determine which date I’m available.

Google specifically highlights workflows where information extracted from images can be used across connected apps.

I didn’t expect scheduled photo organization to be so useful

Gemini Spark can run recurring workflows for Google Photos in the background. For example, you can ask Gemini to automatically create monthly highlight albums or sort photos of receipts.

This is probably the feature I’d experiment with the most. Photo organization fails when it becomes a one-time project. Within a few months, it would become messy again. Recurring automation solves that problem differently.

For example:

  • Every Sunday, find my best photos from the previous week and add them to a weekly highlights album.
  • At the end of every month, create an album containing my favorite family photos.
  • Every week, find photos of receipts and organize them separately.

That last example might sound boring, but I actually think it’s incredibly practical.

My Google Photos library often doubles as temporary storage for things like receipts, bills, product labels, event posters, travel confirmations, and restaurant menus. I take photos because it’s faster than writing things down. Then those images disappear into my library. Scheduled automation could finally give those forgotten images a purpose.

Photo editing becomes part of the workflow instead of a separate task

One thing I particularly like about the Gemini Spark approach is that editing doesn’t have to be a separate destination anymore.

Normally, my workflow involves finding a photo, opening the editor, adjusting the image, saving, going back, and repeating.

With Gemini Spark, editing can become one step inside a larger workflow. It can enhance images, apply quick fixes, create stylized images, and generate collages or other visual creations. Importantly, edits are made to a new copy rather than overwriting the original image.

That last part matters a lot to me. I love experimenting with photo editing, but I don’t want an AI agent permanently modifying my original memories.

Imagine this request: Find my best beach photos from last month, brighten the underexposed ones, and add the edited versions to a new album.

That’s far more useful to me than opening an AI editor and individually experimenting with every image.

Things I would actually automate with Gemini Spark

I can think of dozens of theoretically impressive things Gemini Spark could do with Google Photos.

But these are the automations I would actually use.

1. Weekly photo highlights

I would set up something like: Every Sunday, find the best photos and videos I captured that week and create a private weekly highlights album.

This would essentially create a visual diary without me having to maintain one.

2. Travel albums automatically

After returning from a trip, you may create a workflow such as: Find the best photos from my recent trip, filter duplicates, enhance the landscape shots, and organize everything into an album.

Honestly, this alone could save hours.

3. Screenshot cleanup

My photo library is full of screenshots I needed once and never looked at again.

I would love to experiment with finding screenshots containing receipts, booking information, and important documents and organizing them separately.

Google says Spark can extract text from images and use that information in broader workflows, which makes this type of automation particularly interesting.

4. Monthly family albums

This might be one of the most meaningful uses.

Enter this prompt: At the end of every month, find the best family photos and create a monthly memories album.

Instead of discovering random memories years later, you would have an automatically generated, organized timeline.

5. Food photo collections

I know this sounds incredibly specific, but I take far too many photos of food. Google’s example of automatically creating a weekly food-photo collage is actually one of the more fun use cases.

Something like: Every weekend, find my best food photos, create a collage, and add them to a weekly album.

6. Event sharing

This is where multi-step automation becomes genuinely convenient.

Find the best photos from yesterday’s party, create a shared album, and prepare the link to send to everyone.

I wouldn’t necessarily trust an AI to send something automatically without reviewing it. But letting it do everything up to the final confirmation? That’s exactly the kind of automation I want.

Privacy concern: Giving AI complete control of your memories

Here’s where my excitement about Gemini Spark becomes more complicated.

Your Google Photos library might be the most personal digital archive you own. It contains things you intentionally saved or completely forgot were there, including family moments, screenshots, documents, locations, events, and potentially sensitive information captured in photos.

So while I find Gemini Spark’s capabilities exciting, I don’t think users should casually connect an AI agent to their entire photo history without understanding what they’re allowing.

Thankfully, Google has built some guardrails into the workflow. Original photos remain untouched during editing because Spark creates a copy, newly created albums are private by default, and Gemini asks for confirmation before actions such as sharing albums or sending emails.

Who can use Gemini Spark with Google Photos?

This is the part that will disappoint a lot of people.

Right now, Google Photos integration in Gemini Spark is rolling out gradually, so not everyone will see it immediately. Moreover, users need to meet specific requirements such as:

  • Be 18 years or older
  • Be located in the United States, subject to regional availability restrictions
  • Be eligible to use Gemini Spark with Google AI Pro or Ultra subscriptions
  • Toggle on Google Photos in the Gemini app through Settings > Personal Intelligence > Connected apps > Turn on Google Photos
  • Use the feature in English
  • Access it through the Gemini mobile app or Gemini on the web

The availability limitation is frustrating, especially since this feels like a feature that could be useful to almost anyone with a large Google Photos library. But given how much personal data and automation is involved, I also understand why Google may be rolling it out gradually.

Gemini Spark makes managing Google Photos easier!

I’ve used plenty of AI features that felt impressive for five minutes and then quietly disappeared from my workflow. This one feels different.

Not because Gemini Spark can magically edit photos, create albums, or search through my Google Photos library. Those are useful features individually, but they’re not the real story. The best part is that Gemini Spark can connect them. You can describe an outcome instead of manually executing every step required to reach it.

Would you trust Gemini Spark to organize your entire Google Photos library, or would you rather keep control of your memories yourself? Let me know in the comments.

  • I asked Gemini to find Android apps instead of searching the Play Store
  • I connected WhatsApp to Gemini

title.rendered: WhatsApp is doubling music clip length for Status updates to 30 seconds

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is rolling out longer music clips for Status updates. The limit is increasing from 15 seconds to 30 seconds, giving users more room to share a useful part of a song instead of cutting it off too quickly.

WABetaInfo reports that the change is rolling out on Android and iPhone. It is a gradual, account-side update, so installing the latest WhatsApp version does not guarantee that the new limit will appear immediately.

The music picker now goes up to 30 seconds

WhatsApp is adding a clip-duration picker to the music editor. After choosing a song, users can select a duration of up to 30 seconds or choose a shorter option when a smaller snippet fits the Status better.

The longer limit works when adding music to a photo Status and when sharing a music-only Status. WhatsApp first introduced music in Status updates through its music catalog, and its official announcement originally described shorter music clips for photo updates.

The basic flow stays the same:

  1. Create a photo or music-only Status.
  2. Tap the music note and choose a song.
  3. Open the duration picker and select up to 30 seconds.
  4. Choose the part of the song you want, then share the Status.

The rollout is still gradual

WABetaInfo says the feature is appearing for some users on Android and iOS. The compatible versions it identified are WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.36.1 and WhatsApp for iOS 26.35.72, but the update is controlled on WhatsApp’s servers and may not reach every account at once.

If you do not see the 30-second option, keep WhatsApp updated and check again later. The current WhatsApp Status guide for iPhone explains the existing music flow, while the latest WhatsApp tips for iPhone covers other Status tools and app features.

The change is small, but 30 seconds is enough to include a longer chorus, intro, or verse without turning a Status update into a full music stream. WhatsApp has not said when the rollout will reach every user.

title.rendered: Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo reportedly starts at $2,000

content.rendered:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone may have a name, a starting price, and a launch window. In a late post on X, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple plans to call the device iPhone Duo, with a $2,000 starting price for 256GB of storage.

The report says higher-capacity versions could reach roughly $3,000. Apple has not confirmed the phone, its name, or any of these prices.

iPhone Duo could start with 256GB

The reported $2,000 price would apply to the entry-level model. Gurman says storage could go as high as 2TB, pushing the most expensive version to around $3,000. Apple is reportedly absorbing some of the extra memory cost to keep the base model near the $2,000 mark while passing more of that cost to buyers who want additional storage.

That would still make the iPhone Duo one of Apple’s most expensive mainstream products. Earlier reports had placed the foldable above $2,000, with some estimates reaching $2,500 before the latest pricing detail.

The foldable may arrive after the iPhone 18 Pro

Gurman says the iPhone Duo could go on sale as early as October, rather than launching alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. Apple is expected to unveil its fall iPhone lineup at the September 9 “Surprise and shine” event, but the company has not named the foldable on its event page.

The delayed sale date would give Apple more time to prepare a new foldable product category. Previous reports have also pointed to production challenges, although Apple has not explained a launch schedule.

Other reported iPhone Duo details

The same report points to a new A20 Pro chip, Apple’s C2 modem, dual 48-megapixel rear cameras, a 12-megapixel front camera, a magnetic hinge, and Apple Pencil support. The phone may come in white and dark blue.

Those details remain unconfirmed, but the name is now more credible than the “iPhone Ultra” label used in earlier reports. People who reportedly handled Apple’s foldable liked its pocketable design and larger-screen software, as described in earlier foldable iPhone coverage. Apple’s broader foldable iPhone guide collects the older design and display rumors, but it does not make them official.

Apple’s September event may settle the product name and core specifications. Until then, the $2,000 starting price and October availability are still reported details, not confirmed Apple specifications.

title.rendered: How to get the Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Sprites can completely shake up your gameplay in Fortnite, and the one you undoubtedly need to get your hands on is the Mega Man Sprite. This is a Rare-tier sprite introduced with the Fortnite v42.10 update, and it’s useful for players who are looking to move around the map quickly.

However, locating a Mega Man Sprite can prove to be difficult if you don’t know where to search. But you don’t have to worry, as we’ve got you covered. Let’s take a look at how you can easily find and obtain the Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite.

Here’s how to get the Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite

If you’re trying to hunt for the Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite, the best way to obtain it is through a Blue Cheat Code. Since the Mega Man Sprite is a Rare-tier item, the Blue Cheat Code gives you the maximum chance of obtaining it.

The issue is that the Blue Cheat Codes appear randomly on the Fortnite Override map. From our experience, though, Heatwave Harbor, Cluster Coast, and Shaken Sanctuary seem to be some of the better locations to check when you’re looking for the Cheat Code.

You can also make your search for the sprite easier in the Battle Royale by purchasing a Cheat Code Locator for 1,500 Sprite Dust at the in-game extraction sites. Once you’ve got your hands on it, the item will point you towards the closest Cheat Code, which means you won’t have to search the entire map. After finding one, you need to enter four button inputs to unlock the Rare Cheat Code.

If you’re still not able to find a Blue Cheat Code, you can search Rare Chests and regular Chests. Both of these have a chance of containing the Sprite, but keep in mind that the odds are low. You can also obtain the Mega Man Sprite from another player, either a friend or an opponent, if they already have one in their inventory.

Is Mega Man Sprite useful in Fortnite?

Now that you know how to get the Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite, the next question is whether it’s actually worth going out of your way to find it. Before we tell you that, it’s crucial to understand what makes this Sprite useful.

Equipping the Mega Man Sprite will give you improved sliding capability and allow you to make moves across the island with less friction. This means you will be able to maintain your momentum more easily and cover greater distances while sliding, regardless of the environment you’re moving across.

This perk might seem simple on paper. However, from our experience, we’ve found it quite useful for rotating around the map, escaping a sketchy situation, or repositioning yourself during a match. It makes your overall movement much smoother, which is quite valuable in a fast-paced game like Fortnite. So, if you come across one during a match, it’s definitely worth picking up.

FAQs

What does Mega Man Sprite do in Fortnite?

The Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite enhances your mobility by reducing friction while sliding across the map.

Can you level up Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite?

You can level up the Mega Man Sprite by equipping it and earning XP through activities such as opening containers, getting eliminations, and collecting other Sprites.

What’s the best way to get Mega Man Sprite in Fortnite?

The best way to obtain the Mega Man Sprite is through Blue Cheat Codes, which can be found across the map.

title.rendered: I thought shutting down my Windows 11 PC meant it was off; turns out I was wrong

I always assumed that clicking Shut Down on my Windows 11 PC would turn it off completely. And the next time I pressed the power button, Windows was starting from scratch. But that isn’t always true.

Depending on your settings, Windows may quietly save part of its system state so it can boot faster the next time you turn it on. That also explains why restarting my PC has fixed problems that shutting it down couldn’t. If this sounds surprising to you, keep reading.

Here’s what I learned about what really happens when you shut down a Windows 11 PC, why Restart and Shut Down are not the same thing, and whether disabling Windows Fast Startup is actually worth it.

What actually happens when you click Shut down?

Before learning about Fast Startup, I assumed shutting down a PC followed a straightforward sequence.

Windows would close my apps, stop background processes, unload drivers, clear everything from memory, and completely power down. The next time I pressed the power button, Windows would start from scratch.

That’s how most people probably imagine a shutdown works. But with Fast Startup enabled, Windows 11 can take a different approach.

When you click Shut Down, Windows closes your applications and signs you out of your user session. However, instead of completely discarding the Windows system session, it saves important system information to a file on the storage drive.

So, essentially, the PC is physically powered down, but Windows hasn’t forgotten everything from the previous session. That’s the part that surprised me.

The feature behind it all is Windows Fast Startup

The reason Windows behaves this way is Fast Startup, often referred to as hybrid boot. With this feature, Windows tries to give you the feeling of shutting down your PC while still retaining some of the speed benefits of hibernation.

Here’s roughly what happens:

  • Windows closes your open applications.
  • Your user session is ended.
  • It hibernates the core operating system kernel and the loaded hardware drivers.
  • A snapshot of the Windows kernel session is saved to the storage hard drive.
  • Your PC powers off.
  • The next time you start it, Windows reloads that saved system state.

The result is a faster boot.

On paper, I understand why this feature exists. Nobody enjoys sitting around waiting for a computer to start. Faster boot times were especially valuable when Windows PCs commonly relied on slow mechanical hard drives.

But here’s my issue with Fast Startup. Most people don’t know it exists. Whenever my PC is acting strangely, Bluetooth has stopped working, the Wi-Fi adapter is misbehaving, or a USB device refuses to cooperate, I shut it down, turn it back on, and expect everything to start fresh.

But Windows may have preserved part of the system state. That means the problem you were trying to eliminate might survive the shutdown.

I realized “Shut Down” and “Restart” are not the same thing

This was the biggest thing I learned. I used to treat Restart and Shut Down almost interchangeably, not realizing there was a meaningful difference beyond convenience.

When you choose Restart in Windows 11, Windows performs a more complete shutdown process before starting again. It doesn’t rely on Fast Startup in the same way as a normal shutdown.

That means Restart is much better when Windows needs a genuine fresh start.

Here’s how the different power options work:

This is why, when Windows is behaving strangely, restarting forces the operating system to go through a cleaner initialization process. Drivers reload, services restart, and thus temporary system issues are more likely to disappear.

Why this can actually cause problems

Fast Startup isn’t a bad feature, and for many people, it works exactly as intended. The problem is that a faster startup and a completely fresh system aren’t the same thing.

When Windows saves part of its system state instead of fully clearing it during shutdown, some issues can persist. When dealing with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, USB devices, audio problems, graphics drivers, or other strange hardware behavior, I shut down my PC expecting a fresh start—only to turn it back on and find the exact same problem waiting for me.

That’s where a complete shutdown becomes important.

When you make Windows 11 fully shut down, it:

  • Gives Windows a genuinely fresh start to avoid software or driver conflicts
  • Stops laptops from consuming unnecessary power
  • Helps in troubleshooting persistent problems and installing system updates properly
  • Is ideal when leaving a PC unused for a longer period.

I think Fast Startup made much more sense when Windows PCs relied on slow mechanical hard drives, and booting could take forever. Saving part of the system state was a clever way to make computers feel faster.

But modern PCs are different. Most now use SSDs, and many can boot Windows in seconds anyway. So I have to wonder: is saving a few seconds really worth making the Shut Down button behave differently than most people expect?

Personally, I’d rather wait a few extra seconds and get a genuinely fresh start. Fast Startup isn’t useless, but on modern hardware, I don’t think it’s as essential as it once was.

How to check whether Fast Startup is enabled on your Windows PC

The funny thing about Fast Startup is that many Windows users probably have no idea whether it’s enabled on their PC. I certainly didn’t.

Checking it is relatively easy, although Microsoft has buried the setting in the older Control Panel rather than placing it prominently inside the modern Windows 11 Settings app.

Here’s how I checked:

  1. Open the Control Panel and Click Hardware and Sound.
  2. Then click on Power Options.
  3. Click Choose what the power button does from the left sidebar.
  4. Now look at the Shutdown settings section and check if Fast Startup is selected and greyed out.

If the checkbox is selected, Fast Startup is enabled. It determines whether a normal shutdown uses the faster hybrid shutdown behavior.

How to make Windows 11 actually shut down completely

If you prefer a traditional full shutdown, you have a few options.

Method 1: Disable Fast Startup permanently

This is the simplest option if you want your Windows 11 PC to perform a complete shutdown every time.

  1. Go back to Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do.
  2. Click Change settings that are currently unavailable at the top.
  3. Uncheck Turn on fast startup (recommended).
  4. Click Save changes.

From that point on, Windows won’t save the kernel session during shutdown. That means every time I click Shut Down, my PC gets a more traditional, complete shutdown.

Method 2: Hold Shift while clicking Shut Down

If you don’t want to disable Fast Startup permanently, there’s a quick workaround.

  1. Open the Start menu.
  2. Click the Power button.
  3. Hold down the Shift key.
  4. Click Shut Down.

This gives you a convenient way to bypass Fast Startup when you want a full shutdown without permanently changing the setting.

Method 3: Use a full shutdown command

If you’re comfortable using Windows commands, you can also perform a full shutdown directly.

  1. Press Win + X and select Terminal (Admin).
  2. Write this command: shutdown /s /f /t 0
  3. Press the Enter key.

This tells Windows to force-close running applications and shut down immediately.

Optional: Use Restart when troubleshooting

If you don’t want to disable Fast Startup permanently, this is probably the best compromise.

Leave Fast Startup enabled for normal use. But whenever your Windows 11 PC is acting strangely, choose Restart instead of Shut Down.

Before restarting, save your work, close anything important, and then deliberately select Restart.

Should you disable Fast Startup? My honest take

After learning what Fast Startup actually does, I don’t think there’s one universal answer.

I would keep Fast Startup enabled if:

  • Your PC uses an older mechanical hard drive.
  • Windows takes a noticeably long time to boot.
  • You’ve never experienced problems related to drivers or hardware.
  • Faster startup matters more to you than having a completely fresh boot.

You may consider disabling Fast Startup if you:

  • Have a modern PC that already boots from an SSD.
  • Regularly troubleshoot Windows issues.
  • Frequently experience USB, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or driver problems.
  • Want a genuine full shutdown every time.

Personally, I lean toward disabling it on a modern SSD-equipped PC.

Would you keep Fast Startup enabled for quicker boot times, or disable it so Shut Down actually means Shut Down? Let me know in the comments.

title.rendered: Will GTA 6 Have a First-Person Mode? Everything we know so far

content.rendered:
There are now fewer than 100 days until GTA 6’s release, but one question that many in the community continue to ask is: Will GTA 6 have a first-person mode? With this highly anticipated entry, developer Rockstar Games is taking players to the stunning state of Leonida, and a first-person perspective will undoubtedly be the most immersive way to experience the world. ​

However, Rockstar hasn’t uttered a word about the first-person mode or shown any gameplay footage of it through the various trailer releases so far. Fortunately, a select group of YouTubers has had the opportunity to watch exclusive GTA 6 gameplay, and their experiences contain many clues as to whether the mode will be available. Let’s take a look.

Is there a first-person mode in GTA 6?

Spanish YouTuber El Rubius was among the many creators invited by Rockstar Games to Rockstar North for an exclusive look at GTA 6 gameplay. After his visit, Rubius shared many details about the gameplay footage in a YouTube video, dropping all sorts of details on how the game has evolved compared to previous entries. These included things such as dynamic world events, denser traffic, advanced vehicle crash physics, gore and dismemberment, robberies, and several other brand-new additions.

During the preview, Rubius also directly asked co-lead developer Rob Nelson whether GTA 6 will have a first-person mode. According to a translation provided by a Reddit user u/El_Pintor64, it was revealed that a first-person mode had not been implemented in the game at the time Rubius saw the game. While Rockstar hasn’t exactly confirmed that the feature won’t be available at launch, it’s likely that the game won’t debut with this particular perspective.

However, there’s always a chance that Rockstar could decide to change things in the future. Rubius speculated that a GTA 6 first-person mode could arrive alongside the PC version or the game’s eventual release on the next-generation consoles, which include the likes of PlayStation 6 and Xbox Project Helix. So, if you’re planning to pre-order GTA 6, it’s crucial to keep this detail in mind.

Why GTA 6 needs a first-person mode

The last couple of weeks have been an absolute treat for the GTA 6 community in terms of news about the game, especially after such a long period of silence from Rockstar. Whether it’s through the GTA 6 leaks or the official extended look that premiered on Netflix, players now have a better idea of what the developer plans to bring to the state of Leonida. While there’s still plenty we don’t know about the game, these reveals have made one thing clear: Rockstar is pushing the level of detail in GTA 6 to a completely new level.

Just take a look at the gameplay footage, and you’ll see how Leonida is shaping up to be a dynamic world. Not only will you be able to explore the streets of Vice City, but you’ll also be able to go through highways, beaches, islands, wetlands, and tons of other environments. These areas are being filled with life, with NPCs that follow routines and react to the world around them. You can see cars with detailed interiors, visible crash damage, and deformation, and the in-game world is packed with places you can enter and explore. It’s expected that hotels, shops, clubs, houses, and other locations will feature their very own interiors.

When Rockstar is going out of its way to create a game that mimics the real world, players should have a way to experience those details right up close. A GTA 6 first-person view will allow players to view the streets of Vice City, NPC animations, buildings, cars, and even the smallest of environmental touches that might get overlooked in a third-person angle. Just going around Leonida from behind the wheel could feel like a completely unreal experience.

Rockstar already has a track record of proving that first-person mode works great in its open worlds. With GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, the developer showed how much immersion can change with a simple switch of the camera angle. There’s no reason to abandon the feature in an extremely detailed game like GTA 6.

title.rendered: GTA 6 vehicle customization: Every detail revealed so far

content.rendered:
GTA 6 Extended Look finally hit Netflix last week and gave fans a plethora of different reasons to be excited about the highly anticipated title, scheduled to come out on November 19, 2026. From the stupefyingly lively world of Vice City to the highly detailed and highly customized vehicles, the nearly half-hour-long showcase contained lots of intriguing new visuals.

Speaking of vehicle customization, cars turned out to be one of the more notable highlights from the first look at GTA 6’s gameplay. Things such as heavily modded cars and race cars were given a short but prominent place in the video. Below, we have compiled all the details about GTA 6’s cars, car customization, and car-related side missions that you may have missed.

All car customization features in GTA 6

  1. Cars have a wide variety of decals that can be put on spots like the back glass.
  2. There is the option to mod underglow onto the car’s bottom surface.
  3. Various liveries are available in mod shops, including liveries that glow in the dark.
  4. The flames coming out of the exhaust pipes can be color-customized.
  5. The lighting on the number plate is customizable with different colors.
  6. Lug nuts on the rim of a wheel can be changed in terms of color.
  7. An interior LED strip can be placed on the inside of the back glass.
  8. The interior lighting of cars can be customized.

Through the GTA 6 leaks we saw last month, we already had received a good look at cars and driving in the game. However, the Extended Look has shown the true level of detail and customization that will be possible when you set foot in Vice City.

Besides the gas stations being able to repair your vehicle, you can also take them to Pay N’ Spray, a series staple, to do certain modifications such as a new paint job. However, extensive modifications would be available through dedicated mod shops, some of which are controversially exclusive to those who order GTA 6’s Ultimate Edition.

Cars in GTA 6: What changed since GTA 5

  1. The driving in GTA 6 appears to feel heavier than in GTA 5, with the car weight substantially coming into play during turns and quick movements.
  2. The car interior is highly detailed, complete with buttons on the car door, backseat armrest strap and even the airbag warning sticker.
  3. On the outside, the headlights of cars now have daytime running lights (DRLs).
  4. The underside of the chassis also has 3D details instead of 2D textures, as was the case in GTA 5.
  5. Car damage is apparently more specific, with individual parts showing signs of damage.
  6. The indicator on the rear lights now works according to the turns you take.
  7. NPC cars can also sport a heavily customized look more often than usual.
  8. Apart from acting as your transport, cars now also double up as storage, with the trunk being used to store items such as firearms in GTA 6.

These changes are understandably being implemented to enhance the realism in the GTA sequel. With that said, fans can expect the days of arcade-y car handling and physics-defying car jumps in the franchise to be numbered as the game’s launch draws near.

Vehicle-based activities in GTA 6

The Extended Look revealed a variety of different side activities in GTA 6, ranging from basketball to base jumping. In addition, there were a few vehicle-based activities on display as well. The video confirmed that illegal street racing, car racing, and off-road racing are set to be part of the forthcoming title.

Since past GTA titles have included racing as a significant part of its side content, it’s not surprising that the new GTA is also following in the footsteps and doing the same. It will be interesting to see how these activities increase in difficulty with the new car handling and weightiness incorporated into Rockstar’s title.

Rounding up

Fans are certainly thrilled by what GTA 6 Extended Look had to show them, as evident by the video on Rockstar’s official YouTube channel amassing 1.5 million likes, at the time of writing, in about 11 days. It not only gave the community a long-awaited deeper look at GTA 6’s gameplay but also injected more hype into it by giving a glimpse at the level of meticulous work Rockstar Games devs have once again done this time around.

After shipping two monumental open-world action-adventure titles in 2013’s GTA 5 and 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, it will be exciting to see all that the GTA makers have prepared for fans to experience this year. Overtaking those two behemoths of a hit might generally be considered a tall order for any game, but judging by what experts have been saying, GTA 6 seems to be fairly up to the task.

  • Every GTA protagonist, ranked from worst to best
  • Why GTA 6 needs a first-person mode

title.rendered: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 leak points to four new features

content.rendered:
Code in the watchOS 27 and iOS 27 betas may have revealed four changes coming to Apple’s next watches. A MacRumors forum post from user pdfu points to a new Readiness app, more detailed strength-workout tracking, a revised optical-sensing system, and possible 128GB storage.

Apple has not confirmed any of them. The clues also do not prove that every feature will arrive on both the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.

A new Readiness app may sit beside Workout

The beta code refers to a separate Apple Watch app called Readiness. It appears in the watchOS launcher logic and in the iPhone Watch app’s code for arranging the default Home Screen, where it sits next to Workout.

That name suggests a broader recovery or wellness view, separate from the existing Vitals app. The code does not explain what data Readiness would show or whether it would be exclusive to the new watches.

Strength workouts could track each set

Apple is also preparing health data structures that can store more detail about strength training. The fields include individual sets, repetitions, weight, equipment, body side, and workout duration.

That would give the Workout app a better record of how a session was performed instead of treating strength training as one broad activity. The code points to the data model, not a finished screen or a confirmed watchOS 27 feature.

The optical sensor may get a hardware update

Another clue is a sensor family called "Sunstone4p0." The code describes lower noise coefficients and channel selection based on the watch’s position and orientation.

In plain terms, that could help the watch choose a better sensing path when the reflected pulse signal is weak or when the watch sits differently on the wrist. It may point to revised heart-sensing hardware, but the code does not identify the final component or the model that will use it.

128GB storage is possible, not guaranteed

The code also contains a NAND storage profile tied to the T8320 chip that is associated with the Series 12 and Ultra 4. That has led to speculation that Apple could double Apple Watch storage from 64GB to 128GB.

The benefit would be more room for music, offline content, apps, and future on-device features. Most buyers probably will not need that much space, though, and the storage profile does not prove that Apple will offer 128GB on every configuration. A current Apple Watch buying guide shows how the existing lineup is positioned today.

The launch is still unconfirmed

Apple’s September 9 event is the likely place to learn whether these features are real. Separate reporting has also tied the event to the Series 12 and Ultra 4, including another Apple Watch Ultra 4 rumor about sensors and health alerts.

Until Apple shows the watches or publishes their specifications, the safest read is that the beta code reveals what the company is testing, not what every customer will get.

excerpt.rendered: Code in watchOS 27 and iOS 27 betas points to four possible Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 upgrades, but Apple has not confirmed them for launch.

title.rendered: WhatsApp may let users connect up to five third-party AI agents

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is testing a way to let users connect outside AI agents directly to chats in the app. The feature, spotted by WABetaInfo, lets users create a dedicated conversation for an agent, send it instructions, and receive replies without opening another app.

The feature is still limited to some Android beta users. WhatsApp has not announced a public rollout or an iPhone release.

How the agent chats would work

Users can add an agent from WhatsApp’s settings, give it a name, and choose a profile photo. WhatsApp then generates an API key that the user pastes into the service hosting the agent. Compatible services can use that connection to send messages back into the new WhatsApp chat.

WABetaInfo says the feature supports up to five agents per account. They could be AI agents, but the system also supports simpler bots that carry out specific commands. Each one appears as its own conversation, so users can keep different tools separate.

The agent only gets access to what the user shares in its chat. It cannot read other WhatsApp conversations, contacts, or media, and the current implementation does not support group chats or communities. Removing an agent disconnects it, but WhatsApp keeps the existing chat history visible.

These chats are not end-to-end encrypted

The privacy detail matters more than the five-agent limit. WhatsApp’s Help Center says chats with third-party agents are not considered end-to-end encrypted because a Meta service manages the conversation for the agent developer.

That does not give an agent access to the rest of your WhatsApp account. It does mean users should treat the dedicated chat differently from a normal conversation with another person. The agent developer can access the messages as part of the service, so sensitive information does not belong there unless the user trusts that provider.

WhatsApp also warns that AI responses may be inaccurate. That is worth keeping in mind when an agent is asked to make decisions or carry out tasks based on incomplete information.

The company has been adding more AI features to WhatsApp, including Incognito Chat for Meta AI and testing AI summaries for unread messages. Third-party agents take that shift a step further by letting people bring their own tools into the messaging app.

The rollout is still small

The feature appeared in WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.35.3 and is rolling out to a limited number of accounts in select countries. Most users will not see an Agents section in WhatsApp’s settings yet.

WhatsApp has not said when the feature will reach more Android accounts, group chats, or iPhone users. Until then, the useful takeaway is simple: agent chats may soon be easier to set up, but they will have a different privacy model from regular WhatsApp messages.

title.rendered: Five iPhone 18 Pro camera features may be hidden in iOS 27 code

content.rendered:
Apple may be preparing five camera controls that have not appeared in the iOS 27 betas yet. A MacRumors forum post from user pdfu points to new Camera code for exposure scopes, focus tools, repeated self-timer shots, manual focus, and aperture-based image correction.

The code does not confirm that these features are coming to the iPhone 18 Pro. None is available in the current beta, and Apple could hold some back for a later update.

Five camera changes appear in the leak

The reported features cover both photo controls and the processing that happens after the shutter is pressed:

  1. Exposure scopes: The Camera app may add waveform and histogram views to help users judge brightness while shooting. The code includes luminance, RGB Composite, and RGB Parade options.
  2. Focus peaking and highlight warnings: Colored edges could show which parts of a scene are in focus. A separate overlay could warn when bright areas are losing detail, using solid colors, pulses, diagonal stripes, or a checkerboard pattern.
  3. Repeated self-timer shots: A timer could take several photos in a row, restarting the countdown without waiting for each image to finish processing. That would be useful for group photos and moving into position without running back to the phone after every shot.
  4. Manual focus: A slider could let users set and lock focus instead of leaving the job entirely to autofocus. Apple already offers a similar control in Final Cut Camera.
  5. Aperture-based image correction: iOS 27 could choose different lens-correction data depending on the camera’s aperture setting, then blend between nearby calibration points.

The aperture code is the clearest iPhone 18 Pro clue

The last feature fits a separate iPhone 18 Pro rumor. Apple is widely expected to add a variable-aperture main camera, which would let the lens opening change instead of staying fixed. If that hardware arrives, the new processing code could help the Camera app compensate for how the lens behaves at different settings.

The forum post says the system can use up to four calibration references. That does not mean the iPhone will have four physical aperture stops. It only describes how iOS can select and blend correction data.

The same product cycle has already produced leaks about the lineup and chip. iOS 27 beta code is believed to reference the fall iPhone 18 Pro models and Apple’s foldable, while a separate A20 Pro leak points to a possible seven-core GPU. Those reports are also unconfirmed.

Apple may reveal more this week

Apple’s September 9 event is the first obvious chance to show the iPhone 18 Pro camera system. Still, a feature appearing in beta code does not guarantee a launch-day release. The controls could remain hidden, be limited to new hardware, or arrive in a later iOS 27 update.

For now, the leak suggests Apple is working on more serious camera controls for the iPhone. It does not yet tell us which of them will actually ship.
