title.rendered: OpenAI’s Admin plugin lets ChatGPT Work and Codex manage teams

content.rendered:
OpenAI has launched an Admin plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex that lets workspace admins inspect usage, manage access, and make supported account changes from a conversation.

The plugin puts routine Admin Console work inside ChatGPT. An admin can ask which teams are using the most credits, check why someone cannot access a model, approve a spending request, or update a group without jumping between settings and reports.

What the Admin plugin can do

The first release covers four common parts of workspace administration:

  • Review activity, adoption, and credit use across ChatGPT Work and Codex
  • Add or remove members and update groups
  • Check effective permissions and control access to features or models
  • Change usage limits and approve or deny spending requests

Admins can ask follow-up questions before taking action. For example, they could compare credit use across teams, create a chart for a monthly review, then adjust a limit after seeing the underlying data.

That fits the broader idea behind ChatGPT Work, which is meant to complete multi-step jobs across tools rather than return a single answer.

Existing permissions still apply

The plugin does not create a shortcut around workspace controls. OpenAI says it works within the admin’s existing role and permissions, while respecting workspace policies and approval requirements.

It also returns a structured result for each request, so admins can see whether an action completed and what changed. Actions with wider impact can be reviewed before the plugin applies them.

That permission model matters more here than it does for a read-only report. Removing a member or changing model access has real consequences, and a conversational interface should not make those changes invisible.

It can automate recurring admin work

OpenAI says the plugin can monitor recurring conditions and route requests to Slack or Microsoft Teams. A company could send pending credit requests to an authorized reviewer or automatically grant feature access when a request meets predefined rules.

The Admin plugin joins tools such as the recent Apple Messages plugin for ChatGPT on Mac, but it targets the people running the workspace rather than the members using it.

Workspace admins can enable the plugin in ChatGPT settings, then install it from the Plugins directory in ChatGPT Work on the web or desktop app. OpenAI has not published a plan-by-plan availability list in the announcement.

mainEntity.name: Has Lilith appeared in Fortnite before?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, this is the first time a Lilith-inspired outfit has made its way into the game. Contrarily, the Mad Moxxi and Psycho Bandit skins have previously appeared in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Borderlands bundle that includes all three skins?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, there is no such bundle. The only bundle on offer, in the Borderlands section, is the Mad Moxxi Bundle, which contains the Mad Moxxi skin along with her themed pickaxe and back bling.

mainEntity.name: Which other video game cosmetics are available in the Fortnite Shop right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, you can also purchase cosmetics related to the Crash Bandicoot and Spyro franchises.

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, you can also purchase cosmetics related to the Crash Bandicoot and Spyro franchises.

mainEntity.name: 1. When did Master Chief first land in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Master Chief was first released in the game in December 2020 during Chapter 2 Season 5.

mainEntity.name: 2. Which other Xbox franchises have appeared in Fortnite besides Halo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Xbox-owned IPs, including Gears of War, Doom, Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Overwatch, have previously been featured as in-game cosmetics in Fortnite.

mainEntity.name: 3. Which other FPS protagonists, other than Master Chief, have been added to Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Other FPS heroes in Fortnite's skins catalog include popular characters such as Doom Slayer from Doom, V from Cyberpunk 2077, and Tracer, Genji, & D.Va from Overwatch.

mainEntity.name: 1. How many Sonic The Hedgehog character skins are available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, there are four different Sonic franchise characters up for grabs, namely Sonic, Dr Eggman, Knuckles, and Shadow.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: 3. Is Tails available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: While Tails is not available in Fortnite as a skin, you can still unlock his sidekick version by purchasing the Battle Pass for Chapter 7 Season 4 and reaching Level 2.

title.rendered: Mac Processor History: How Apple Transformed Computing

content.rendered:
When you think of a Mac today, you probably imagine a fast, powerful machine powered by Apple’s latest M6 chip. But Macs weren’t always this advanced. Their journey began in the 1980s with the Motorola 68K series—a much simpler processor. Over the years, Apple transitioned to PowerPC, then Intel, and finally, its own Apple Silicon chips.

In this article, we’ll explore how Mac processors have evolved over time. You’ll see how each new chip improved speed, graphics, and memory, shaping the powerful Macs we use today.

Table of Contents
  • 2020–Present: Apple Silicon
    • M6 Chip Family: M6
    • M5 Chip Family: M5, M5 Pro, M5 Max, and M5 Ultra
    • M4 Chip family: M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max
    • M3 Chip Family: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra
    • M2 Chip Family: M2, M2 Pro, M2 Max, and M2 Ultra
    • M1 Chip family: M1, M1 Pro, M1 Max, and M1 Ultra
  • 2006-2020: Intel x86
  • 1994-2005: Power PC
  • 1984-1995: Motorola 68 K

2020–Present: Apple Silicon

On June 22, 2020, Apple CEO Tim Cook announced a two-year transition plan to move from Intel processors to Apple Silicon. The goal was to create an all-Apple ecosystem by replacing Intel’s x86-64 architecture with Apple’s native ARM64-based chips.

Staying true to its timeline, Apple introduced its first Apple-designed chip, M1, in November 2020. This was followed by more powerful M1 variants in 2021. Apple then launched the M2, M3, M4, M5, and M6 chipsets, further pushing the boundaries of performance.

Here’s a detailed table outlining the evolution of Mac processors, from the latest Apple M4 Max back to the M1:

M6 Chip Family: M6

M6 (August 2026)

Apple’s M6 is the company’s first chip built using a state-of-the-art 2-nanometer process, bringing major improvements in CPU, GPU, storage and AI performance. It features a 12-core CPU, delivering up to 40 percent faster CPU performance, and a 12-core GPU, with two additional cores compared with M4.

AI is one of the biggest focuses of M6. The chip features an all-new Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says delivers up to 2x faster performance than the previous generation. Combined with the Neural Accelerators in the GPU, M6 is built to handle local AI workloads and next-generation Apple Intelligence features more efficiently.

Memory and storage performance have also been upgraded. Mac mini with M6 starts with 16GB of unified memory, configurable up to 32GB, while memory bandwidth reaches up to 170GB/s. Apple also claims up to 2x faster storage compared with the previous generation.

M5 Chip Family: M5, M5 Pro, M5 Max, and M5 Ultra

M5 (October 2025)

The M5 is the base chip in the M5 family and is created using  TSMC’s third-generation 3-nanometer process for mainstream laptops and tablets. It’s the first Apple Silicon chip to feature a dedicated Neural Engine in the GPU core, focusing on AI-driven tasks.

The chip features a 10-core CPU made up of 6 performance and 4 efficiency cores and up to a 10-core GPU, which provides solid graphics performance for tasks like photo editing and light 3D work. You can also configure it up to 32 GB of unified memory.

In Geekbench Single-Core scores, the M5 base model outperforms the whole M4 series and has the highest scores of any Apple silicon chip. Overall, it delivers a strong balance of performance, efficiency, and affordability for most users.

M5 Pro (March 2026)

The M5 Pro is designed for professionals who need more processing power than the base M5. Apple has designed a new Fusion Architecture specifically for AI tasks in this chip. It includes an 18-core CPU (6 super and 12 performance cores), offering 30% faster processing of intensive workloads. Apple has stated it as “the world’s fastest single-core performance.”

The GPU can scale up to around 20 cores with a dedicated Neural Accelerator in each core, delivering much stronger graphics performance. One of the major improvements in the M5 Pro is higher memory bandwidth up to 307GBps and up to 64 GB of unified memory, enabling large projects and datasets to run smoothly without slowdowns.

M5 Max (March 2026)

The M5 Max sits at the top of the M5 chip lineup and is built for users who need maximum performance. It is targeted at professionals working in fields such as 3D rendering, medical imaging, advanced video production, machine learning, and large-scale creative projects.

This chip features the same high-performance CPU architecture as the M5 Pro but dramatically expands the GPU capabilities. The GPU can scale up to 40 cores, making it one of the most powerful graphics systems available in a laptop.

The M5 Max also offers up to 614GBps memory bandwidth and supports up to 128 GB of unified memory. So, it can run large professional projects efficiently without relying heavily on external storage.

M5 Ultra (August 2026)

Apple’s M5 Ultra, introduced in August 2026, is designed specifically for demanding professional workflows and advanced AI workloads. The biggest change is Apple’s move to a quad-die architecture using next-generation UltraFusion technology, giving M5 Ultra the scale needed for extreme CPU, GPU and AI workloads.

You can configure it with up to a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU. For AI, Apple has added Neural Accelerators to the GPU for the first time on an Ultra chip, delivering up to 4.3x the peak AI compute performance of M3 Ultra. The chip also supports up to 512GB of unified memory and an enormous 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth.

Apple says M5 Ultra delivers up to 1.3x faster multithreaded CPU performance and up to 1.8x faster graphics performance than M3 Ultra. These improvements target workloads such as 3D rendering, video production, software development, scientific computing and AI inference.

M4 Chip family: M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max

Apple’s M4 chip family represents the latest advancements in silicon technology, delivering enhanced performance and efficiency across various devices. Each chip—M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max—is designed to meet different user needs.

M4 (May 2024)

The standard M4 chip is built using second-generation 3-nanometer technology, enhancing power efficiency and performance. It features a 10-core CPU with four performance cores and six efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.8 times faster performance than the M1 chip.

The 10-core GPU provides graphics performance up to twice as fast as the M1, making tasks like photo editing and gaming smoother. The 16-core Neural Engine, capable of performing up to 38 trillion operations per second, significantly boosts AI-related tasks and features like Apple Intelligence.

M4 Pro (October 2024)

The M4 Pro chip is designed for users with more demanding workflows. It boasts a 14-core CPU, comprising ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, offering up to 1.9 times faster performance than the M1 Pro.

The GPU includes up to 20 cores, providing graphics performance twice that of the standard M4. This makes it ideal for professionals engaged in tasks like app development, video editing, and complex simulations.

M4 Max (October 2024)

The M4 Max chip is the most powerful in the M4 family, targeting users requiring extreme performance. It features a 14-core CPU with ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, similar to the M4 Pro.

However, its GPU scales up to 32 cores, delivering exceptional graphics capabilities suitable for high-end tasks such as 3D rendering and large-scale data processing. The M4 Max also supports higher unified memory bandwidth, enhancing data-intensive operations.

All M4 chips support advanced features like hardware-accelerated ray tracing and mesh shading, enhancing graphics rendering and gaming experiences. They also enable Thunderbolt 5 connectivity, offering faster data transfer speeds and improved peripheral support.

M3 Chip Family: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra

Apple’s M3 chipset family includes four powerful processors: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra. Each is designed to meet different performance needs, from everyday tasks to demanding professional workloads.​

M3 (October 2023)

The M3 chip is built using advanced 3-nanometer technology, making it faster and more efficient. It features an 8-core CPU with four performance cores and four efficiency cores, delivering up to 30% faster performance than the M1.

The 10-core GPU provides enhanced graphics performance, making tasks like photo editing and gaming smoother. The 16-core Neural Engine, capable of performing up to 15.8 trillion operations per second, significantly boosts AI-related tasks.

M3 Pro (October 2023)

The M3 Pro chip is designed for users with more demanding workflows. It boasts a 12-core CPU, comprising six performance cores and six efficiency cores, offering up to 40% faster performance than the M1 Pro.

The GPU features up to 18 cores, delivering graphics performance ideal for professionals in video editing, programming, and other demanding tasks. Apple has also integrated 37 billion transistors to enhance the overall performance of Mac machines.

M3 Max (October 2023)

The M3 Max chip is one of the most powerful in the M3 family, targeting users requiring extreme performance. It features a 14-core CPU with ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, similar to the M3 Pro.

However, its GPU scales up to 38 cores, delivering exceptional graphics capabilities suitable for high-end tasks such as 3D rendering and large-scale data processing. The M3 Max also has 92 billion transistors to enhance data-intensive operations.

M3 Ultra (March 2025)

The M3 Ultra chip is Apple’s most powerful processor to date. It features a 32-core CPU with 24 performance cores and eight efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.8 times the performance of the M1 Ultra.

Its GPU includes up to 80 cores, providing up to 2.6 times faster graphics performance than the M1 Ultra. The M3 Ultra also supports up to 512GB of unified memory—the highest ever in a personal computer—making it ideal for tasks like visual effects and AI development.

M2 Chip Family: M2, M2 Pro, M2 Max, and M2 Ultra

M2 (June 2022)

The M2 processor in the MacBook houses an 8-core CPU with a configuration of 4 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores. Apple claims that M2’s CPU gives twice the performance of the latest 10-core PC laptop processor.   

In addition, the M2 processor offers unparalleled work performance with an 8—or 10-core GPU, 16-core neural engine, and 100GBps bandwidth. M2 chips have different RAM variations: 8GB, 16GB, and 24 GB. 

M2 Pro (January 2023) 

M2 Pro has a robust 10-core or 12-core CPU, including 6 or 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores. Like the M1 Pro, the M2 Pro has an inbuilt media engine that accelerates H.264, HEVC, and ProRes video encoding and decoding. Besides, the chip provides improved power efficiency when playing 4K and 8K ProRes streams thanks to the 16- or 19-core GPU.

Further, the M2 Pro has a 16-core neural engine, 200 GBps memory bandwidth, and 16 GB or 32 GB RAM variants. Apple claimed the M2 Pro offered exceptional image processing capabilities. However, it is only equipped with a MacBook Pro to handle its high efficiency.   

M2 Max (January 2023) 

M2 Max added another layer of efficiency to the Apple Silicon range. Its core specifications included a 12-core CPU with 8 performance and 4 efficiency cores. Like its predecessor, the M2 Max comes with two ProRes and video-encoding engines.   

Regarding graphics, it supports a 30- or 38-core GPU to give you the most detailed output. While the GPU support is better than M1 Max, the 16-core neural engine remains the same for both variants. In addition, Apple introduced the chip in 3 RAM variants- 32 GB, 64 GB, and 96 GB.   

Moreover, Apple asserted that the M2 Max was 30% better than the M1 version when using color grading in DaVinci Resolve. It also offers 400 GB of memory bandwidth, ensuring quick processing.   

M2 Ultra (June 2023) 

At the recent WWDC 2023, Apple launched its most efficient iteration of the Apple Silicon series: M2 Ultra. It offers the power of two M2 Max chips interwoven using the robust UltraFusion architecture. Regarding specifications, M2 Ultra features a 24-core CPU and a maximum of 76-core GPU support.

It also carries 134 billion transistors, up to 192GB of unified memory, and an impressive 800 GB of memory bandwidth. You can experience this beast in the latest Mac Studio and Mac Pro. According to Apple, Mac Studio with M2 Ultra is 3x faster than its earlier version.

Besides, it can run 22 streams of 8K ProRes video together. The M2 Ultra chip enables the Mac Pro to deliver 3D simulations and video transcoding up to 3x faster. Moreover, the processor can simultaneously consume 24 inputs from 4K cameras and encode them to ProRes. 

M1 Chip family: M1, M1 Pro, M1 Max, and M1 Ultra

M1 (November 2020)

The M1 processor was Apple’s first venture into chip design for the Mac. Indeed, it was a big blow for Intel! Regarding specs, M1 chips offer an 8-core CPU with 4 performance and 4 efficiency cores and a 7- or 8-core GPU support.

Besides, the 16-core Neural Engine embedded in the M1 series accelerates and optimizes machine learning operations on Mac. In addition, the chip offered 68.25 GB of memory bandwidth. However, it only supported two RAM variations—8GB and 16GB. The small storage capacity didn’t go down well with many Mac users.  

M1 Pro (October 2021)

Next in line in the M1 series was M1 Pro. This chipset supported 8-or-10-core CPUs, configured as 6 or 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores. Besides, Apple included a 14-or-16-core GPU, which is 2x faster than M1. Also, the new GPU was up to 7x more quickly than the integrated graphics on the 8-core laptop chip.

Besides, it featured a ProRes accelerator in the media engine for faster video processing. Its memory bandwidth of up to 200 GB is nearly 3x better than the M1. This time, Apple expanded its storage capacity with M2, introducing 16GB and 32GB chips. 

M1 Max (October 2021)

The M1 Max and M1 Pro chips were launched together. They had a 10-core CPU with 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores, a 24- or 32-core GPU, and a 16-core Neural Engine. The graphics performance of the 32GB GPU is up to 4x faster than that of the M1 chip.   

Its two ProRes accelerators can deliver up to 2x faster video encoding than M1 Pro. Moreover, the processor offers up to 400 GB of memory bandwidth, two times more than the M1 Pro and 6x improved than the M1. Besides, the 64GB RAM adds some extra credit points.   

Apple introduced the M1 Max chip only for the MacBook Pro and Mac Studio.   

M1 Ultra (March 2022)

The M1 Ultra was launched as a standard option for the Mac Studio. This powerful processor has UltraFusion architecture connecting the two M1 Max chips. It houses a 20-core CPU with 16 performance and 4 efficiency cores. For graphics, Apple added a massive 48- or 64-core GPU support.

So, you get improved latency, reduced bandwidth, and better power consumption. Furthermore, the chip has up to 128GB of unified memory built, offering twice the media engine performance of the M1 Max.   

2006-2020: Intel x86

At WWDC 2005, Apple announced its transition to Intel chips, and the first Intel Macs were announced in early 2006. These included an iMac and the MacBook Pro, which boasted almost four-fold enhanced performance from their predecessors. 

Further, from Mac OS X 10.4.4, Apple included an advanced emulation technology called Rosetta. It helped maintain software compatibility between generations. Soon, Apple introduced programs with universal binaries that could run on both PowerPC and Intel Macs.

As the transition to x86 eventually came a full circle, Rosetta was removed from Mac OS X 10.7 Lion going forward. So far, about 80 Mac models have featured Intel CPUs. This changed with the introduction of ARM-based Macs.

1994-2005: Power PC

In the late 1980s, new trends began taking over the computing industry, overshadowing the legacy CPU architectures. Apple partnered with IBM and Motorola to design a common CPU platform that could rival the “Wintel” (Microsoft-Intel) domination. 

The Power Macintosh 6100 used the PowerPC architecture, following which around 87 different Mac models were launched. Clock speeds increased from 60 MHz to 2.7 GHz, which was remarkable for that era. The final Apple PowerPC model was released in November 2005. 

1984-1995: Motorola 68 K 

The 1984 Apple Macintosh computer had an 8 MHz Motorola 68000 CPU. While in development, an early Mac prototype used an 8/16-bit Motorola 6809 CPU. But after a designer noticed the impressive graphics routines that were being created for the 68000-based Apple Lisa, the more expensive 16/32-bit 68000 was chosen. 

While the Apple Lisa used only a 5 MHz 68000, the new Mac prototype could run at 8 MHz. This appealed to Steve Jobs, who was eager to upstage the Lisa team. 

Over the following decade, every Macintosh used successors of the 68000, including the pure 32-bit 68020, 68030, and 68040 chips. These got faster and more complex over time. Overall, at least 72 different Macs used 68k CPUs, the last of which was the PowerBook 190 in 1995. 

The best is yet to come! 

The history of Apple processors beautifully captures the tech giant’s true ideology. The Mac has witnessed everything from laptop size to its architecture. I hope you enjoyed reading this article as much as we enjoyed traveling the Mac timeline while penning it.

Please share your reviews in the comments section. Till then, enjoy reading.  

FAQs

What is the oldest Mac software?

The oldest Mac software is Mac OS X Server 1.0.

What is the full form of Mac?

The complete form of the Mac is Macintosh.

mainEntity.name: 2. Can I get the Sonic the Hedgehog skin from the Item Shop?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you must purchase the Fortnite Override Battle Pass to get the Sonic skin as it isn't available in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: 3. Is Tails available in Fortnite?

acceptedAnswer.text: While Tails is not available in Fortnite as a skin, you can still unlock his sidekick version by purchasing the Battle Pass for Chapter 7 Season 4 and reaching Level 2.

title.rendered: I changed these Windows Search settings, and finding files got much easier

content.rendered:
Windows Search is useful out of the box, but it seems inefficient in certain situations. If I couldn’t remember the exact filename, I would go to the search bar, try a few variations, and eventually wonder why finding a document on my own PC felt so hard.

The problem wasn’t really Windows Search. It was how Windows was indexing my files. Once I customized a handful of Windows Search indexing settings, search became much more predictable. If you also want to improve Windows Search in Windows 11 to find files faster, here are the best settings you should change right now.

Why Windows Search can feel inefficient

Windows Search relies heavily on a system called the index: a catalog of file names, paths, properties, and, when configured to do so, the text inside files. Instead of scanning each drive on your PC every time you search, Windows can simply use the index to provide you with the necessary results quickly.

That sounds simple, but there is an obvious catch: Windows can only search efficiently for what it has actually indexed.

By default, Windows 11’s Classic search mode indexes common locations such as Documents, Pictures, Music, and the Desktop. You need to enable Enhanced Search to index the entire PC, but Microsoft notes that this can consume more system resources.

That explains a lot of the “Windows Search is broken” complaints I’ve had. Sometimes the file wasn’t missing. Search simply wasn’t looking in the folder where I’d saved it. And sometimes the file was indexed, but Windows only knew about its properties, not the words inside it. So instead of accepting Windows Search as-is, I started optimizing it to search files faster.

5 tips that improved my Windows search

1. Making Windows index the folders I actually use

This was the first change I made, and arguably the most important. I organize my files differently from the way Windows expects me to do it. Some folders that I need to access regularly are not located in the standard Documents folder, and that’s where the search problem started.

If Windows doesn’t index a location, using the Search bar won’t necessarily give you the fast, reliable results you expect.

In Windows 11, follow these steps:

  1. Launch Settings on your PC.
  2. Click Privacy & security on the left sidebar. Now, scroll and select Search.
  3. Under Find my files, choose Enhanced search.
  4. Now, Windows will scan and index the entire PC. Keep it plugged in to finish the process, as it will take some time.

You can also customize which locations are indexed and exclude unimportant folders to speed up the process. Click Add an excluded file and select temporary folders, old archives, development files, large collections of documents you never search, and application data.

But I like to be more methodical about it: index the folders I actually search, rather than blindly indexing everything. If you have a dedicated work folder, downloads directory, or external folder and want to save resources, keep the Search settings set to Classic and add the drive or folder to your indexed locations.

Simply click Customize search location under Classic > Modify in the dialog box, then choose a drive or a specific folder. Click Ok to save the location. That’s much more useful than assuming every folder on my PC is important.

One important caveat: indexing can take time initially. Microsoft says the first indexing pass can take up to a couple of hours, depending on the amount of data. After that, Windows updates the index as files change.

2. I enabled file-content searching for the documents I need

This setting made Windows Search feel dramatically smarter. Searching by filename is useful when you remember the filename. However, most of the time I forget the name and usually remember something inside the file.

For example, you may remember that a document mentioned “Q4 budget,” “client onboarding,” or “backup strategy,” but you can’t be sure about its name. In such cases, enable Windows to index file contents along with the default file names and properties.

  1. Go to Settings > Privacy & security > Search.
  2. Scroll down and click Advanced indexing options.
  3. It will open the indexing options control panel. Here, click Advanced at the bottom. Ensure you have administrative access.
  4. Move to the File Types tab. Select Index Properties & File Contents.
  5. Click Ok to apply the changes.
  6. Now, search for a sentence or keywords, and the Search bar will actually pull up documents containing them.

Content indexing makes the search index more useful, but it can also make the index larger. For me, searchable documents are worth it. That’s why I deselected the file types I don’t usually use and then enabled content indexing to minimize the process load.

If you regularly search PDFs, Word documents, text files, spreadsheets, or similar files by words contained inside them, this is one of the first settings I’d check.

And on supported Copilot+ PCs, Windows 11 can go beyond traditional keyword indexing with semantic indexing, which is designed to surface results based on the meaning of a query rather than matching only exact terms.

3. Clean up search results with better filters

Sometimes Windows Search isn’t failing. You’re just asking it a question that’s too vague. I learned to use search terms that give Windows more context, rather than typing a single generic word and scrolling through a mountain of results.

If you’re looking for a spreadsheet about a particular project, search using several useful terms rather than just the project name.

Instead of searching report“, try narrowing it with a search operator at the end like report kind:document datemodified:last week. Now, Windows will find the document file type named report that you accessed last week. If you type “size:>10MB, the search result returns files sized more than 10 MB.

You can also use multiple search operators together or access the search options to find files faster by file type, date, name, and other properties.

  1. Open File Explorer and click the search bar in the top-right corner.
  2. Enter the file name or keyword.
  3. Now, select Search options. Here, you will find different filters.

The less irrelevant material Windows has to return, the less time you spend scanning the results.

4. Use filename extensions when you know the format

If you know you’re looking for a PDF, don’t make Windows sift through Word documents, spreadsheets, images, and everything else.

For example: *.pdf Or combine the extension with a keyword: budget *.pdf

Likewise:

  • *.docx
  • *.xlsx
  • *.pptx

This is particularly useful when several files have similar names.

Moreover, when I know the file is somewhere inside Documents\Projects I open that folder first and search there. Don’t search the entire PC to get faster results.

5. Rebuild the Search Index when the search is broken

This is the nuclear option, but sometimes it’s exactly what you need.

If Windows Search suddenly stops finding files that it previously found, returns obviously incomplete results, or behaves inconsistently even after you’ve checked your indexed locations and file types, it may be time to take care of the Search index itself.

Windows 11 lets you rebuild the index to troubleshoot search problems.

  1. Go to Search settings in Privacy & security.
  2. Click Advanced indexing options and select Advanced at the bottom.
  3. Finally, click Rebuild.

Now, Windows will remove the old index, crawl your entire PC according to your configuration, and create a new search directory. It gives Windows a fresh catalog to work from. However, remember that rebuilding doesn’t automatically mean that your files will become more searchable.

And yes, the process can take hours to complete and bump your CPU usage. That’s why I wouldn’t rebuild the index every time Search feels slightly slow. Check your indexing settings and rebuild only when the index itself appears to be the problem.

What I wouldn’t change

I’m deliberately not recommending that everyone turn on every search option.

Indexing more locations can increase the amount of data Windows has to catalog. Searching the entire PC can also have resource implications. If you have a relatively clean file structure and rarely search outside your normal user folders, Classic search may be perfectly adequate.

I also wouldn’t enable content indexing for every obscure file type simply because the option exists. My approach is more practical:

  • Index what I use.
  • Make the important documents searchable by content.
  • Exclude what I never search.
  • Ensure specific file types are selected in search settings.

That’s enough.

Final takeaway

Windows Search doesn’t need a dramatic overhaul. It needs a little direction.

The biggest improvement I made was realizing that the search box doesn’t determine what Windows can find. The search index, indexed locations, file types, and search scope determine what information Windows has available when I ask it a question.

Once you change those settings around the way you actually store and search for files, Windows Search finds files way faster.

In case you missed:

  • Windows was reserving my RAM. Here’s how I got my usable memory back
  • How to screen record on Windows
  • The Windows Clipboard shortcut I wish I started using years ago
  • How to use Snap Layouts in seconds

acceptedAnswer.text: No, there is no such bundle. The only bundle on offer, in the Borderlands section, is the Mad Moxxi Bundle, which contains the Mad Moxxi skin along with her themed pickaxe and back bling.

title.rendered: New shows and movies coming to Apple TV in September 2026

content.rendered:
Apple TV is going all in this September with a stacked lineup of new shows and movies. Whether you’re into thrillers, heartfelt dramas, wild adventures, or documentaries that make you think, there’s something worth adding to your watchlist.

It can be hard to keep up with everything dropping each month, so I’ve done the digging for you. Here’s your no-nonsense guide to all the official Apple TV releases in September 2026, plus a quick peek at what’s coming up next.

Apple TV shows and movies releasing in September 2026 

Are you missing new Apple TV content? No more! Dive into the September lineup, featuring popular genres like comedy, drama, thriller, and even a documentary for TV geeks. Get ready to fill your popcorn bucket soon!

1. Mayday 

  • Cast: Ryan Reynolds, Kenneth Branagh, Maria Bakalova, and many more
  • Director: John Francis Daley, Jonathan Goldstein
  • Genre: Action, Adventure
  • Release Date: September 4, 2026

If you love adventure movies, Mayday will grab your attention instantly. The moment the mission goes wrong, the film shifts from high-tech military precision to pure, unpredictable human instinct, and that contrast is where it really shines. 

What I like here is how the film flips the spy genre on its head. Instead of focusing purely on espionage or action, Mayday leans into the awkward, often hilarious dynamic between two completely opposite personalities stuck in the same impossible situation. 

Check out on Apple TV 

2. Last Seen 

  • Cast: Patrick Brammall, Maxine Peake, Brendan Cowell, and more
  • Director: Kris Mrksa, Christian Schwochow
  • Genre: Crime Thriller
  • Release Date: September 9, 2026

If you enjoy edge-of-your-seat mystery thrillers, don’t miss Last Seen on Apple TV. The series starts with every parent’s worst nightmare and one phone call that changes everything.

Eleven years after his daughter mysteriously disappeared, former detective Ian Ridley receives a desperate call from a teenage girl claiming to be the child he lost. With hope reignited and time running out, he dives into a dark web of secrets, lies, and danger.

Check out the Apple TV Press

3. Slow Horses Season 6 

  • Cast: Gary Oldman, Jack Lowden, Kristin Scott Thomas, and more
  • Creator: Will Smith
  • Genre: Spy Thriller, Drama, Dark Comedy
  • Release Date: September 16, 2026

Apple is back with its most acclaimed espionage thriller, Slow Horses. The upcoming Season 6 follows the team at Slough House as they face one of their most dangerous missions yet.

When a series of revenge attacks puts them in the middle of a deadly conspiracy, Jackson Lamb and his misfit MI5 agents must work together to uncover the truth before it’s too late. So, get ready for even bigger risks, shocking betrayals, and high-stakes spy action.

Check out on Apple TV

4. Brothers 

  • Cast: Matthew McConaughey, Woody Harrelson, Holland Taylor, and more
  • Director: David West Read
  • Genre: Comedy
  • Release Date: September 23, 2026

Brothers brings together Hollywood stars Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson in a hilarious comedy inspired by a real-life rumor that they might actually be brothers.

When Woody and his family move into Matthew’s Texas ranch, an unexpected family secret turns their peaceful getaway into total chaos. Packed with laughs, awkward moments, and heartwarming friendship, this comedy is all about family, fame, and the surprises life throws your way.

Check out on Apple TV

What’s coming to Apple TV after September 2026 

Apple isn’t slowing down in September and beyond. Here are a few titles already making waves:

1. The Last First: Winter K2 

  • Cast: Nirmal Purja (Nims), Muhammad Ali Sadpara, Sajid Sadpara, John Snorri Sigurjónsson.
  • Director: Amir Bar-Lev
  • Genre: Documentary, Adventure
  • Release date: October 2, 2026

If you are waiting for Tenzing, here’s another tense, emotional mountaineering documentary. The Last First: Winter K2 takes you into the heart of the 2021 race to achieve the first-ever winter ascent of the world’s second-highest mountain.

What begins as a story of extraordinary courage and endurance gradually becomes an intimate look at ambition, ego, money, power, and the price of glory. I am excited to watch the spectacular mountain and the real drama that lies in the people trying to conquer it.

Check out on Apple TV 

2. Matchbox The Movie 

  • Cast: John Cena, Jessica Biel, Sam Richardson, and many more
  • Director: Sam Hargrave
  • Genre: Action, Comedy
  • Release Date: October 9, 2026

Matchbox: The Movie feels like a mix of Fast & Furious energy with a classic “friends reunited” story at its core. The story follows a group of childhood friends whose lives are thrown into chaos when their long-lost leader, Sean, suddenly returns. 

What starts as a reunion quickly spirals into a high-stakes chase across countries. There are explosive car chases, global locations, and intense action sequences, but underneath all that, it’s really about friendship, trust, and unfinished pasts.  

Check out on Apple TV 

3. Tenzing 

  • Cast: Genden Phuntsok, Tom Hiddleston, Willem Dafoe, Caitríona Balfe, and many more 
  • Director: Jennifer Peedom 
  • Genre: Drama, Adventure 
  • Release Date: October 16, 2026 

Tenzing tells the inspiring true story of Tenzing Norgay, the Nepalese-Indian mountaineer, aka Sherpa, who made history by becoming one of the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1953.  

The film does not just revolve around the climb, but highlights Tenzing’s bravery, perseverance and all the sacrifices required for accomplishing one of the most difficult things ever done by humans. If you enjoy true stories about overcoming impossible odds, this is one to add to your watchlist. 

Check out on Apple TV 

4. Where’s Wanda? Season 2 

  • Cast: Heike Makatsch, Axel Stein, Lea Drinda, Leo Simon, and many more  
  • Director: Tobi Baumann, Christian Ditter  
  • Genre: Drama, Comedy 
  • Release Date: October 21, 2026  

When the Klatt family thought that things were finally settling down, once again things went out of control for them. In Where’s Wanda? Season 2, Wanda becomes a suspect in a murder case, and her family once again finds themselves in the midst of chaos and investigations.  

Packed with dark humor, unexpected twists, and plenty of family drama, I am waiting to see the new mystery unfold while laughing along the way. 

Check out on Apple TV 

5. Nocturne 

  • Cast: Liev Schreiber, Zazie Beetz, Stephen Graham, and more 
  • Director: Tim Van Patten
  • Genre: Crime, Thriller
  • Release Date: October 30, 2026  

Nocturne is a gripping crime thriller that starts off with an unexpected turn of events. A victim believed to be dead in a serial killing suddenly reappears, completely disrupting the whole investigation.  

The show then goes on how a detective and FBI agent uncover the truth and hunt down the ruthless criminal. If you enjoy dark mysteries, clever cat-and-mouse games, and suspense that keeps you guessing until the end, Nocturne looks like one to watch. 

Check out on Apple TV 

6. Stick Season 2 

  • Cast: Owen Wilson, Peter Dager, Marc Maron, Rhea Seehorn, and more.
  • Created by: Jason Keller
  • Genre: Sports, Comedy
  • Release date: November 4, 2026

After finding an unlikely second chance through golf, Pryce Cahill is back, and this time, the stakes are bigger. Stick Season 2 continues the heartfelt sports comedy beyond golf and into ambition, friendship, and family.

The new season promises more laughs, emotional turns, and new characters as Pryce and Santi face the next stage of their journey.

Check out on Apple TV

7. Being Heumann 

  • Cast: Ruth Madeley, Mark Ruffalo, Dylan O’Brien, Madeline Delp, and more
  • Director: Siân Heder  
  • Genre: Drama, Comedy
  • Release Date: November 13, 2026 

Another interesting true story set for release in 2026 on Apple TV is Being Heumann. It is about Judy Heumann, one of the most influential disability rights activists in American history.  

In 1977, together with hundreds of other protesters, she occupied a federal building demanding equal rights and accessibility to people with disabilities. It’s a powerful, uplifting film that shows how one person’s determination can spark a movement and change millions of lives. 

Check out on Apple TV 

8. Way of Warrior Kid

  • Cast: Chris Pratt, Jude Hill, Linda Cardellini, and many more
  • Director: McG
  • Genre: Action, Drama
  • Release Date: November 25, 2026

Way of the Warrior Kid is Based on the bestselling book by Jocko Willink. You will get a story of Marc, an introverted 11-year-old boy who lacks self-confidence, has trouble at school, and even with physical activities. It’s designed to inspire younger audiences while still hitting adults with a strong message about discipline and personal growth.

Check out on Apple

9. Bad Monkey Season 2

  • Cast: Vince Vaughn, Natalie Martinez, John Malkovich, and more
  • Director: Marcos Siega, Colin Bucksey, and more
  • Genre: Comedy, Drama
  • Release date: December 2, 2026

Andrew Yancy is back in the Florida Keys, and somehow his life is about to get even more complicated. After the wildly eccentric mystery of Season 1, Bad Monkey Season 2 brings an entirely new case. This time, Yancy witnesses the murder of Florida’s finest fixer and gets pulled into an investigation.

I am excited about season 2 because it’s an original story rather than a direct adaptation of another Carl Hiaasen novel. So, get ready for sun-soaked Florida, eccentric criminals, dark comedy, bizarre situations, and Vince Vaughn’s effortless sarcasm at the centre of it all.

Check out on Apple TV

10. Neuromancer

  • Cast: Callum Turner, Briana Middleton, Joseph Lee, Mark Strong, and more
  • Director: J.D. Dillard and Graham Roland
  • Genre: Sci-fi, Thriller
  • Release Date: January 22, 2027

Based on William Gibson’s legendary cyberpunk novel, Neuromancer drops you into a futuristic world where hackers, powerful corporations, and cutting-edge technology collide.  

The story follows a disgraced super-hacker and deadly assassin as they team up for a dangerous heist. I have high hopes for its promised smart sci-fi with high-stakes action, futuristic tech, and plenty of twists. 

Check out on Apple TV 

Final take: Must-watch Apple TV releases this September 

Apple TV is clearly on a roll. Whether you’re up for a globe-trotting docuseries, a heartfelt thriller, or a sci-fi robot with emotional baggage, September  2026 is loaded with good stuff.

So grab your snacks, make room in your watch queue, and don’t forget to explore the immersive Vision Pro experience if you’re lucky enough to own one.

title.rendered: How to get the Kernel Hearts Fernet skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Kernel Hearts, a forthcoming anime-inspired action-RPG, is scheduled to launch on September 17, 2026, across PC, Xbox Series X/S, PS5, and Switch 2. Ahead of its release, Epic Games Store announced a collab with the game that brings its protagonist Fernet to Fortnite as an in-game skin.

On August 17, the Epic Games Store x Kernel Hearts collab was first announced to mark the occasion of pre-orders opening for the indie title. What separates getting the game via Epic’s storefront from others is that this particular option, which costs $19.99 (₹719), also comes with the Fernet Fortnite skin as a freebie. This bundled item offer is redeemable at any point (not just the pre-order phase).

Steps to claim the Kernel Hearts Fernet skin in Fortnite

  1. Go to the Epic Games Store, enter “Kernel Hearts” in the search bar at the top of the screen, and select the game when it appears in search suggestions.
  2. Then, once you are on the product page for the game, click on “Pre-Purchase“.
  3. Finally, choose your desired payment option, fill in the required details, and click on “Pay Now.”

Other Epic Games Store games that come with free Fortnite skins

Kernel Hearts is just one of the many games that Epic Games Store has partnered with to offer its buyers a free bundled Fortnite skin. In cases where these games are free-to-play, an eligible in-game purchase unlocks their respective cosmetic freebie(s).

1. Resident Evil: Requiem

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Grace Ashcroft
Price: $69.99
Release status: Available

2. Cyberpunk 2077

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Adam Smasher
Price: $59.99
Release status: Available

3. Borderlands 4

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Mad Moxxi
Price: $69.99
Release status: Available

4. Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Dr Eggman (along with Dr Eggman Bundle items)
Price: $69.99
Release status: Available

5. Warframe

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Excalibur
Price: Free
Release status: Available

6. Control Resonant

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Dylan Faden
Price: $59.99
Release status: Coming out on September 24, 2026

7. Honkai Star Rail

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Stellaron Hunter Blade
Price: Free
Release status: Available

8. Crimson Desert

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Kliff
Price: $69.99
Release status: Available

9. Dave The Diver

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Dave
Price: $19.99
Release status: Available

10. Phantom Blade Zero

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Soul
Price: $59.99
Release status: Coming out on October 29, 2026

11. Cronos: The New Dawn

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Traveler
Price: $59.99
Release status: Available

12. Arknights: Endfield

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Perlica
Price: Free
Release status: Available

13. Rematch

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Coach Gabi
Price: $29.99
Release status: Available

14. Goals

Redeemable Fortnite skin: Goal Getter
Price: Free
Release status: Available

Wrapping up

For the past several years, Fortnite has added to its catalog of video game cosmetics, with big-name franchises such as Sonic the Hedgehog, Tomb Raider, God of War, and more joining the lineup. This run is only bolstered by developer Epic Games’ gift-with-purchase offers that have bundled a free themed skin with certain game purchases on its store.

Given the ongoing season, Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 Override, has a gaming-focused theme at its core, we can expect even more new video game character skins to be incorporated into the game. While memorable fictional figures such as Persona’s Joker are already confirmed to arrive, it is yet to be known when exactly fans can grab them and which other related cosmetics will go on sale simultaneously.

  • How to get Spyro the Dragon sidekick in Fortnite

title.rendered: I compared the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8: Here’s the foldable I’d buy

content.rendered:
Google has launched the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, its latest foldable phone, and it goes head-to-head with Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8. I’ve always found foldable phones exciting, but spending nearly $2,000 on one makes the choice a lot harder.

Both flagships offer a large internal display, flagship processors, sophisticated AI, premium cameras, and years of software support. On paper, they look like two variations of the same idea. They aren’t. After comparing the two, one stands out as the foldable I’d actually buy.

Here I’ll break down the Pixel 11 Pro Fold vs Galaxy Z Fold 8 based on their display, camera, performance, battery life, software, and price to see which premium foldable is better and actually feels worth the money.

Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8: Quick specs comparison

The two phones start at essentially the same price in the U.S., but their philosophies are very different.

Design and build quality: Samsung redefined foldable phones

This is where Samsung surprised me. The old criticism of Galaxy Z Fold phones was simple: they were technologically impressive but physically awkward. The Z Fold 8 finally feels like Samsung listened.

At 201 grams, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is dramatically lighter than the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which weighs 238 grams. Samsung also gave its foldable lineup the biggest design makeover, with a wider cover screen, and honestly, it makes my content-watching more fun. Moreover, I can unfold it smoothly thanks to the Armor FlexHinge and a widened gap in the inner bezel.

This time, Samsung focused on durability as well. Dual-layer Flex Titanium beneath the inner display strengthens it. In addition, the frame uses Armor Aluminum, while Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 is used on the folded front and Gorilla Glass Victus 2 on the back. Galaxy Z Fold 8 comes in Pistachio, Lavender, Graphite, and Cream, and they truly look beautiful in person.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold takes a different approach. Google says it is almost 10% lighter and about 1mm thinner than its predecessor, with a new gearless hinge, a more compact camera bar with the HiLight notification system, a redesigned hinge, and a lighter, 3x more durable body.

The exterior combines glass-ceramic cover glass, Gorilla Glass Victus 2 on the back, an aluminum frame, and an ultra-durable composite matte back in only two colors. It also carries an IP68 rating.

For me, Samsung wins on the new design. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 feels noticeably more refined and compact, with a reassuringly premium construction. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is still the one I’d consider if a taller form factor and a more understated matte finish matter more to you.

My pick: Galaxy Z Fold 8 if you like a compact design; Pixel 11 Pro Fold for a bigger, more understated feel.

Displays: Bigger isn’t everything

The display is probably the first thing I noticed when comparing the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8. Both have excellent screens, but Google and Samsung are clearly taking different approaches.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold goes big. Its inner display measures 8 inches and uses a foldable LTPO OLED Super Actual Flex panel with a 120Hz refresh rate, HDR10+, and up to 3,600 nits peak brightness. The square-ish 1:1 aspect ratio also gives me plenty of room for reading, browsing, and working on two apps side by side.

I particularly like the 6.5-inch Super Actua cover display. With a 1080 x 2342 resolution, 120 Hz, and 3,600 nits peak brightness, it feels much closer to using a regular flagship phone when the Pixel is folded.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8, meanwhile, is smaller at 7.6 inches, while the cover display is only 5.5 inches. But Samsung’s trick is the aspect ratio. The Fold 8’s outer display uses a wider 10:16 ratio, while the unfolded display uses a 4:3 ratio. The cover screen feels more like a small tablet, which I find particularly useful for multitasking, gaming, and reading.

Although smaller, the Dynamic LTPO AMOLED 2X display, with a 120Hz refresh rate, HDR10+, and up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness, makes text and images look incredibly sharp. In addition, the Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 protection and anti-reflective treatment are also nice touches for everyday use.

For me, the Pixel wins if you want the biggest screen, while the Galaxy wins for the more polished foldable display experience.

My pick: Pixel 11 Pro Fold for size, Galaxy Z Fold 8 for overall display experience.

Performance and everyday speed

Performance is where I think the Galaxy Z Fold 8 has the clear advantage. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold uses Google’s new Tensor G6, built on a 3nm process, while Samsung’s foldable runs on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, also built on 3nm.

The Pixel’s Tensor G6 uses a 7-core CPU configuration with 50% more TPU compute power, 20% greater power efficiency, and around 15% faster app launch speeds. Graphics are handled by the PowerVR CXTP-48-1536 GPU. Google’s focus here is on powering AI features and making everyday tasks feel smarter, rather than chasing benchmark numbers.

And honestly, for normal use, that’s sufficient. Apps open quickly, switching between apps feels smooth, and Google’s on-device AI features truly shine in day-to-day life. If you are mostly browsing, messaging, taking photos, and using Gemini, I don’t think you’ll feel shortchanged.

But the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the phone I’d choose when performance really matters. Its Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 uses an octa-core CPU with two Oryon V3 Phoenix L cores and six Oryon V3 Phoenix M cores. It also gets the Adreno 840 GPU running at 1.3GHz.

That extra performance headroom makes a difference for demanding games, video editing, and heavy multitasking, especially when I’m using the large inner display with several apps open. For me, the Pixel is fast enough, but the Galaxy feels more future-proof.

My pick: Galaxy Z Fold 8. If you’re spending this much on a foldable, I’d rather have the extra performance available when I need it.

Cameras: Pixel processing vs. Samsung versatility

This is where I would hesitate before declaring a winner.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold has a 48MP main camera with an f/1.7 aperture, dual-pixel autofocus and OIS. But the camera I find most exciting is the 10.8MP telephoto, which provides true optical zoom rather than digital cropping. There’s also a 10.5MP ultrawide camera with a 127-degree field of view.

Google is known for its computational photography, and the Pixel 11 Pro Fold is no exception. I really liked Magic Capture, which automatically captures, crops, and edits photos and videos. Its new 30x Super Zoom keeps distant subjects sharper, while the larger sensor captures 56% more light for better Night Sight photos and clearer low-light video.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a 50MP f/1.8 main camera and a surprisingly capable 50MP ultrawide with a 120-degree field of view and multi-directional autofocus. However, there’s no dedicated telephoto camera, so Samsung relies on digital zoom for longer-range shots. That sounds like a clear Pixel victory, and for still photography, I think it is.

Where Samsung pulls ahead is video. The Fold 8 can record up to 8K at 30fps, while the Pixel tops out at 4K at 60fps. Samsung also offers My FanCam to track a subject in group videos and Dual Recording from the front and main cameras, making the Galaxy a more appealing option if I plan to shoot a lot of video.

Overall, if I were taking travel photos, family photos, or spontaneous night shots, I would choose the Pixel, whereas for creating social media content, filming other people, or even editing video footage on the phone, I would go for the Galaxy.

Winner: Pixel 11 Pro Fold for photography; Galaxy Z Fold 8 for video versatility.

Software, AI, and foldable features

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold runs Android 17 with Google’s Pixel software and Gemini Intelligence deeply integrated into the experience. Google has added foldable-specific features such as Split Screen, Drag and Drop, Instant View, tabletop mode to watch content, and optimized app bubbles. I love its proactive assistance in daily tasks and improved Circle to Search.

There are also smart privacy and security features. Call Screen and Scam Detection have saved me multiple times, whereas the built-in VPN and emergency services via satellite come in handy in critical situations. The Pixel approach is simple: Make the phone understand what I am trying to do.

Samsung’s approach is more like: Give me every tool I could possibly need. One UI 9 on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is built around Multi Window, App Continuity, Taskbar functionality and three-way split-screen workflows. I also tried DeX mode, which effectively lets the Fold 8 behave more like a lightweight desktop computer when connected to the right setup.

Then there is Galaxy AI. The Fold 8 gets Now Nudge, Photo Assist, and My FanCam, along with Gemini-powered features. Both bundles a six-month Google AI Pro trial with expanded Gemini access and 5TB of cloud storage.

Winner: Galaxy Z Fold 8 for power users, Pixel 11 Pro Fold for everyday use.

Battery life and charging

The batteries are almost identical on paper.

  • Pixel 11 Pro Fold: 4,806mAh.
  • Galaxy Z Fold 8: 4,800mAh.

But charging is where Samsung pulls away.

The Pixel supports 30W wired charging and up to 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging. Google says it can reach 50% in around 30 minutes and offers more than 24 hours of battery life. Whenever I needed an ultra-fast battery boost, I enabled Extreme Charging Mode, which pauses background activity and non-essential apps.

Samsung supports 45W wired charging, 20W wireless charging, and Wireless PowerShare. Samsung’s charging architecture is designed to distribute power more efficiently across the battery system while managing heat. The Galaxy is also rated for up to 26 hours of video playback.

However, note that foldable phones are screen-hungry devices. When testing the inner display heavily, I had to charge both phones frequently. And being able to top up quickly matters more than winning a theoretical battery-capacity contest.

Winner: Galaxy Z Fold 8

Software support and long-term ownership

This is one category where neither phone gives me a reason to worry.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold gets seven years of OS, security, and Pixel Drop updates. Samsung matches it with seven generations of Android OS upgrades and seven years of security updates for the Galaxy Z Fold 8. That’s excellent news for a $1,800-plus smartphone.

But long-term ownership isn’t only about software updates. It’s also about durability, repairability, accessories, and the cost of replacing the device.

Samsung’s foldable ecosystem is more mature, and its new Fold 8 design benefits from years of hinge and foldable-display development. Google has made impressive durability improvements with the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, including its gearless hinge and IP68 protection.

I’d still give Samsung the slight edge simply because the Fold line has been evolving for longer.

Winner: Galaxy Z Fold 8

Price and value

Both phones start at about $1,900. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 starts at $1,899.99, with 512GB at $2,099.99 and 1TB at $2,499.99. Only the top-tier 1TB option comes with 16GB RAM. And Samsung’s trade-in, financing programs, $200 store credit, and free app subscription bundles can make the effective price even more attractive.

On the other hand, you will get the Pixel 11 Pro Fold 256GB for $ 1,899 and 512 GB for $2,019. Google also offers up to $1,000 off eligible trade-ins and the Pixel Watch 5 for free until 27/08.

Winner: Galaxy Z Fold 8 for most buyers; Pixel 11 Pro Fold for Pixel loyalists and photography fans.

Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8: Which foldable should you buy?

Here is the part where I stop comparing spec sheets.

I’d buy the Galaxy Z Fold 8.

Not because the Pixel 11 Pro Fold is bad. Quite the opposite. The Pixel might actually be the more exciting phone. Its displays are bigger, the camera system is more interesting, AI feels more naturally integrated into every task, better Qi2 wireless charging, and IP68 protection plus seven years of updates make it a seriously compelling long-term device.

But the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the better foldable.

The wider cover screen makes the phone more interesting. The 201g weight makes it easier to carry. Snapdragon performance gives it more headroom. One UI 9 is packed with foldable-specific multitasking tools. DeX gives power users another dimension. Samsung’s 45W charging is faster. And the camera system is more versatile for video creation.

Most importantly, Samsung has spent years learning what people actually do with a foldable. The Fold 8 feels like the product of those lessons.

Buy the Pixel 11 Pro Fold if you:

  • Want the best Pixel camera experience in a foldable.
  • Prefer clean, Google-first Android.
  • Care about Gemini and Google’s AI ecosystem.
  • Love the larger 8-inch inner screen.
  • Want a 5x optical telephoto camera.
  • Use wireless charging frequently.
  • Like to have IP68 durability.
  • Plan to keep the phone for many years.

Buy the Galaxy Z Fold 8 if you:

  • Want the best all-around foldable.
  • Care about raw performance and gaming.
  • Multitask constantly.
  • Prefer a wider, more usable cover display.
  • Enjoy faster wired charging.
  • Create a lot of video content.
  • Want a lighter foldable that’s easier to carry.

And if you are asking me, should you buy the Pixel 11 Pro Fold or the Galaxy Z Fold 8? Galaxy Z Fold 8. No hesitation.

Final takeaway

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8 are proof that foldable phones are finally becoming less about surviving the engineering challenge and more about perfecting the experience.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is the phone I’d choose if I wanted the camera, AI, and Google software experience above everything else. Its 6.5-inch outer display, 8-inch inner screen, 5x telephoto, and 3,600-nit displays make it an unusually strong alternative to Samsung’s formula.

However, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the phone I would actually purchase, as it is lighter, faster, charges faster, has a more functional cover display, offers better multitasking options, and its software is built around the idea that you’re holding a phone that can become a tablet. And that’s ultimately what I want from a foldable.

When not typing, you can find her exploring the latest Apple releases or pondering the future of tech innovation."

About Ava Biswas

  • Ava is a die-hard Apple aficionado and loves testing the latest tech gadgets.
  • She is always on the lookout for issues Apple users are facing, finds solutions, and crafts troubleshooting guides.
  • Her goal to make tech easy for everyone encouraged her to break down complex concepts into easily digestible content.

Experience

Ava has been employing her professional writing and editing skills for over 4 years at renowned media houses like TechBurner and iGeeksBlog. Using her expertise, she crafts informative and engaging How-To's, troubleshooting guides, product reviews, and editorials. When not typing, you can find her exploring the latest Apple releases or pondering new tech innovations.

title.rendered: How to get Shadow the Hedgehog skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
The Sonic the Hedgehog franchise has raced into Fortnite, making famed characters such as Sonic, Shadow, and more available as in-game skins. As a consequence, the Shadow The Hedgehog skin in particular has been a trending cosmetic in the Item Shop since its introduction.

Unlike the Sonic skin, which is part of Fortnite Override’s Battle Pass and hence available throughout the entirety of the season, the Shadow skin is on sale for a limited time until August 30, 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET. The latter outfit is available for 1,800 V-Bucks in the Shop and comes bundled with the Super Shadow Transformation emote and Doom’s Eye back bling.

Steps to claim Shadow the Hedgehog skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab.
  2. After that, scroll to the “Sonic the Hedgehog” section and select your desired skin.
  3. Finally, press the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

Apart from purchasing the Shadow the Hedgehog skin separately, you can also buy it as part of the Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle for 3,600 V-Bucks. This particular offer additionally throws in the Knuckles the Echidna skin and nine other related cosmetics at a discount of 4,700 V-Bucks.

Other Sonic the Hedgehog cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Knuckles the Echidna

Price: 1,500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle

2. Knuckles’ Gloves (pickaxe)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Knuckles the Echidna skin, Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle

3. Chao Egg (back bling)

Price: 600 V-Bucks
Also available with: Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle

4. Chaos Crasher (pickaxe and back bling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle

5. Doom’s Eye (back bling)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available with: Shadow the Hedgehog skin, Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle

6. Doom’s Scythe (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle

7. Super Shadow Transformation (emote)

Available with: Shadow the Hedgehog skin, Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle

8. Dr Eggman

Price: 1,500 V-Bucks

9. Egg Hammer (pickaxe)

Price: 600 V-Bucks
Also available with: Dr Eggman Bundle

10. Orbot and Cubot (back bling)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available with: Dr Eggman skin, Dr Eggman Bundle

11. Egg Mobile (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Dr Eggman Bundle

12. Eggman’s E-TAR (pickaxe and back bling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Dr Eggman Bundle

13. Shadow Slip-Ons (kicks)

Price: 1,000 V-Bucks
Also available with: Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle

14. Sonic Grind Shoes (kicks)

Price: 1,000 V-Bucks
Also available with: Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle

15. Shadow’s ARK Angel (pickaxe and back bling)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Shadow the Hedgehog & Knuckles the Echidna Bundle

16. Porsche 918 Spyder (car body)

Price: 2,800 V-Bucks

Wrapping up

Thanks to Sonic the Hedgehog headlining Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4, its characters have been among the first to be rolled out in the Item Shop. At the time of writing, Lara Croft from Tomb Raider has been confirmed to land in the game this week, whereas Crash Bandicoot and Spyro have also been teased, albeit with no specific timeline.

As the season continues, it is fair to expect several more video game franchises to become part of Fortnite Override. That’s because the promotional images and videos for the new season have already revealed that IPs such as Street Fighter, Persona, The Witcher, and more are set to appear in some capacity.

You may like to read:

  • How to get the Dr Eggman skin in Fortnite
  • Fortnite x Sonic the Hedgehog crossover
  • What happens to your sprites in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4
  • How to get the Lilith skin and Borderlands bundle

title.rendered: Apple may launch two AirPods 5 models at its September event

content.rendered:
Apple’s next entry-level AirPods may arrive as soon as next month. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is preparing two AirPods 5 models for its expected September product event, likely on September 9. One version would be a standard model, while the other would add active noise cancellation.

That would give Apple a direct refresh to the AirPods 4 lineup. The current earbuds launched in September 2024, and U.S. pricing runs from $129 to $179. If Apple keeps the same split, buyers may get a cheaper open-fit option and an ANC version without moving up to AirPods Pro.

Two AirPods 5 versions are reportedly planned

Gurman’s report does not include design, battery, chip, or pricing details. For now, the clearest expectation is a regular AirPods 5 and a second version with active noise cancellation, following the way Apple separated the AirPods 4 models.

There is one software clue behind the rumor. AirPods 5 references in macOS 26.7 code appeared last week, although the code does not explain how the new earbuds will differ from the current generation.

Camera-equipped AirPods are a separate project

The AirPods 5 should not be confused with Apple’s more ambitious camera-equipped earbuds. Gurman now expects those to arrive in 2027. An Apple demo video showing camera AirPods using Visual Intelligence offers a look at that project, but it does not change the simpler AirPods 5 report.

The split matters because the next AirPods launch may be a familiar audio update rather than Apple’s first move into camera-based wearables. Apple appears to be keeping those products on separate timelines.

What the report means for AirPods buyers

The current AirPods 4 and AirPods Pro 2 comparison still explains Apple’s basic choice between an open fit and a sealed Pro design. If you are considering AirPods 4 mainly for the ANC model, waiting for Apple’s September event could make sense. Apple has not confirmed the AirPods 5 name, specifications, price, or release date, so there is no guarantee the reported update will arrive on schedule.

excerpt.rendered: Apple may introduce two AirPods 5 models as early as its September iPhone event. The report points to regular and active noise cancellation versions.

title.rendered: New Mac mini could launch before Apple’s September event, report says

content.rendered:
Apple may update the Mac mini within days, before its main iPhone event. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple is preparing a new model after nearly two years, potentially ahead of the September 9 event the company is expected to hold.

Apple has not announced the Mac mini or confirmed an event date. The timing is notable because Tim Cook is scheduled to become Apple’s executive chairman on September 1, with John Ternus taking over as CEO. If Gurman’s timing is right, the Mac mini could be the last new product introduced before that transition.

M5 and M6 Mac mini versions are both in testing

Gurman says Apple has tested Mac mini versions with both M5 and M6 generations of Apple silicon. That does not mean Apple plans to ship two chips, or that the final model will use the newer generation. The report leaves the decision open.

The current Mac mini lineup uses M4 and M4 Pro chips and launched in 2024. A new model would arrive as Apple is trying to keep up with demand from people using compact Macs to run AI models locally.

Supply trouble is part of the story

Mac mini delivery times have stretched for weeks or months on some configurations. Earlier this year, Mac mini and Mac Studio shortages were expected to last for several months as demand moved faster than supply.

Apple is also preparing to make Mac mini units in Houston later this year. Apple’s Houston manufacturing plan says the new facility will produce the computer in the United States for the first time. It remains unclear whether the model that may launch in the coming days is the same version intended for that factory.

The launch could happen outside Apple’s main event

If Apple does announce the Mac mini before September 1, that would put it outside the expected September event. Gurman’s report gives a short window, not a confirmed launch plan.

For buyers, the safest move is to wait if a Mac mini purchase is not urgent. Apple has not confirmed the chip, design, price, or exact date, and the current Mac mini versus Mac Studio comparison remains useful for anyone choosing between the models already available.

excerpt.rendered: Apple may unveil a new Mac mini in the coming days, ahead of its September event. The report points to M5 and M6 versions but no final chip choice.

mainEntity.name: Has Lilith appeared in Fortnite before?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, this is the first time a Lilith-inspired outfit has made its way into the game. Contrarily, the Mad Moxxi and Psycho Bandit skins have previously appeared in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Borderlands bundle that includes all three skins?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, there is no such bundle. The only bundle on offer, in the Borderlands section, is the Mad Moxxi Bundle, which contains the Mad Moxxi skin along with her themed pickaxe and back bling.

acceptedAnswer.text: Xbox-owned IPs, including Gears of War, Doom, Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Overwatch, have previously been featured as in-game cosmetics in Fortnite.

title.rendered: iOS 27 beta 7 is out as Apple polishes its biggest Siri update

content.rendered:
Apple has released iOS 27 developer beta 7 as the fall launch gets closer. Apple’s developer release page lists build 24A5424a, dated August 24. Developers enrolled in the beta program can install it from Settings > General > Software Update > Beta Updates.

The release entry confirms the build but does not call out a major new feature. Beta 7 follows beta 6 from August 17, so this looks like a stability-focused release before the public version arrives.

Siri AI remains the main reason to watch iOS 27

Apple’s iOS 27 preview puts Siri AI at the center of the update. The rebuilt assistant is designed to handle richer conversations, personal context, onscreen awareness, and actions across apps. Apple is also testing a new Siri interface connected to the Dynamic Island, a dedicated Siri app, and tighter links between Siri, Visual Intelligence, and the Camera app.

The broader Apple Intelligence changes in iOS 27 cover Photos, Safari, Passwords, Mail, Messages, Shortcuts, and other parts of the system. Those are the features that make beta 7 worth following, even if this particular build does not introduce a headline addition.

More iOS 27 changes are still being refined

The wider iOS 27 beta cycle also includes a transparency control for Liquid Glass, faster app and Photos launches, smoother Camera behavior, continuous sending in Messages, Dual Capture in FaceTime, custom EQ for AirPods, easier Apple Pay card switching, new recovery options, and AI-generated wallpapers.

These features belong to the wider iOS 27 release, not necessarily to beta 7 alone. Apple says iOS 27 is coming this fall, while Siri AI will arrive in English later this year. Availability can also vary by iPhone model, language, and region. A Siri AI availability guide explains why installing the beta does not automatically unlock every Siri feature.

Beta testers should expect rough edges

Developer beta 7 is meant for testing, not everyday reliability. Bugs, battery drain, app compatibility problems, and unfinished Siri behavior are still possible. If you are not testing an app or building for iOS 27, waiting for the public release is the safer choice.

mainEntity.name: Has Lilith appeared in Fortnite before?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, this is the first time a Lilith-inspired outfit has made its way into the game. Contrarily, the Mad Moxxi and Psycho Bandit skins have previously appeared in the Shop.

mainEntity.name: Is there a Borderlands bundle that includes all three skins?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, there is no such bundle. The only bundle on offer, in the Borderlands section, is the Mad Moxxi Bundle, which contains the Mad Moxxi skin along with her themed pickaxe and back bling.

acceptedAnswer.text: At the time of writing, you can also purchase cosmetics related to the Crash Bandicoot and Spyro franchises.

acceptedAnswer.text: Master Chief was first released in the game in December 2020 during Chapter 2 Season 5.

mainEntity.name: 2. Which other Xbox franchises have appeared in Fortnite besides Halo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Xbox-owned IPs, including Gears of War, Doom, Fallout, The Elder Scrolls, and Overwatch, have previously been featured as in-game cosmetics in Fortnite.

title.rendered: ChatGPT can now turn your photos into iMessage and WhatsApp stickers

content.rendered:
OpenAI has added a sticker tool to ChatGPT Images. According to OpenAI’s announcement, you can upload a photo, describe the result you want, and export the finished sticker to iMessage or WhatsApp. ChatGPT can also create a transparent background, so the subject is ready to place in a message without a manual cutout.

ChatGPT can build a sticker pack from your images

The tool lives inside Images > Stickers in the ChatGPT sidebar. You can start with one image or several, then ask ChatGPT to turn each one into a sticker or remix them into a set. You can also add or remove parts of the image, or borrow a style from another picture or a text prompt.

The export step comes after you finish editing:

  1. Open ChatGPT and select Images, then Stickers.
  2. Upload one or more images and describe the sticker or changes you want.
  3. Tap Add to chat apps after ChatGPT generates the result.

That makes the tool useful for more than cutting a person or pet out of a photo. You can turn a few pictures into a matching pack, change the mood of the artwork, or create a sticker from an idea instead of a saved image.

WhatsApp has one export requirement

The Add to chat apps menu currently supports iMessage, WhatsApp, and Save to Photos. WhatsApp exports need at least three stickers at a time. 9to5Mac notes that Meta sets this requirement, rather than ChatGPT itself.

In the same test, the finished sticker appeared in a dedicated ChatGPT section inside the Messages sticker carousel. A simple prompt could also create a transparent asset and extend a subject that was cropped in the original photo.

ChatGPT takes a different route from Apple’s built-in stickers

The iPhone already lets you create Live Stickers from photos by lifting the subject in the Photos app or Messages. ChatGPT’s approach is more flexible when you want to change the source image, combine several photos, or create a consistent style across a pack.

If the original photo needs a quick cleanup before you upload it, these iPhone photo editing tools can handle the basic crop, color, and background work. ChatGPT then takes over for the sticker-specific edits and export.

excerpt.rendered: ChatGPT Images now lets you turn photos or ideas into custom sticker packs and export them to iMessage or WhatsApp, with one WhatsApp requirement.
