title.rendered: Meta AI gets a Mac app that can see your screen and read your Instagram stats

content.rendered:
Meta AI now has a native Mac app in beta. Meta announced it on August 19 as part of a push toward small businesses and creators. The desktop app can read a shared window, type dictated text into any app, and pull engagement data from your Facebook and Instagram accounts.

The beta is free and downloads directly from the Meta AI site, not the Mac App Store.

The Mac app can read a shared window and dictate anywhere

Two features are desktop-only. You can attach a Mac window to a conversation, and Meta AI reads the visible text and captures a screenshot so it can answer questions about what you are working on. That requires Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions. The app also offers systemwide dictation: hold a shortcut, speak, and the words land in Mail, a document, or any other app.

Pressing Option-Space opens a compact Meta AI composer over your current app. You can also hide the Dock icon so the assistant stays behind the keyboard shortcut. According to a 9to5Mac hands-on, the app is a native build using AppKit and SwiftUI, weighs about 16MB installed, and needs an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 15 or later. Meta has not published official requirements.

Meta is positioning it around business data

The main differentiator is access to business data. If you connect a professional Facebook or Instagram account, Meta AI can answer questions about reach, saves, shares, comments, and profile visits, analyze ad campaign performance, and benchmark your results against similar brands using public data. Most rival chatbots can help write a caption, but Meta AI can also work from the account’s own performance data.

It also connects to Google Workspace, so it can pull from Gmail, Docs, Sheets, and Slides. From there, it can build decks, docs, spreadsheets, and reports, or run recurring jobs like a weekly performance summary.

The app is free for now, but Meta is testing usage limits on compute-heavy features. Hit a daily or monthly cap, and you get offered a Meta One subscription for more headroom. Meta has not shared what that costs yet.

The privacy trade-off is real

Meta’s generative AI privacy policy says your interactions with Meta AI can be used to train its models. That matters more when the Mac app can read your screen and connected Google Workspace files. Incognito Mode is available for chats you want kept separate, and you can turn off Meta AI inside WhatsApp, Instagram, and Facebook if you do not want to use it there.

Meta already has Muse Code on the Mac, while the Meta AI app launched on iPhone and Android in April 2025. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini also have desktop apps with screen-aware features. Meta’s bet is that access to Instagram analytics will make its assistant more useful to creators and small businesses.

excerpt.rendered: Meta launched a native Meta AI app for Mac in beta. It can read a shared window, dictate into any app, and pull your Facebook and Instagram performance data.

title.rendered: EU welcomes Apple’s new App Store terms, Epic calls them junk fees

content.rendered:
The European Commission says it welcomes the new EU App Store business terms Apple announced on August 18. That suggests the regulator is willing to work with Apple’s revised framework, but the case is not closed. Epic Games, which has spent years challenging Apple’s fees, says the new terms still break the law.

Apple is replacing several EU fee structures with one set of terms

Apple is scrapping its patchwork of EU fee structures and moving every developer to a single set of terms from October 1, 2026. The per-install Core Technology Fee is gone, along with the Initial Acquisition Fee and the Store Services Fee.

In their place, Apple charges a flat commission based on how an app is distributed and how users pay:

  • 26% for App Store sales through Apple’s In-App Purchase, with 15% for Small Business Program developers and subscriptions after year one
  • 20% for App Store apps that use an alternative payment processor, dropping to 10% for small businesses
  • 15% for purchases made through link-outs to the web, dropping to 10% for small businesses
  • 5% Core Technology Commission for apps distributed through alternative marketplaces or the web

Developers can also offer Apple’s In-App Purchase alongside alternative payment options in the same app, something Apple never allowed before. Small marketplace operators earning under 10 million euros a year can get the 5% commission waived entirely.

The Commission will monitor the rollout

“The Commission welcomes Apple’s changes to their business terms, which follow a close dialogue between the Commission and Apple,” a European Commission spokesperson said in a statement shared with the press. The statement refers to the non-compliance decision on Apple’s steering rules and the preliminary findings on alternative distribution from April 2025.

That April 2025 decision came with a 500 million euro fine, which Apple is still fighting in court. The Commission has not formally closed its case. It will monitor how Apple implements the new terms, so the welcome is not a declaration that the dispute is over.

Epic says the fees still break the DMA

Epic Games rejected the new terms within hours, calling the new tiers “junk fees” that do nothing to open up iOS to real competition.

Epic’s argument is simple: the DMA says developers must be able to steer users to the web “free of charge” and make “effective use” of competing stores. In Epic’s reading, any commission above zero on those transactions violates the law, so a 15% link-out fee and a 5% cut on Epic Games Store purchases are just the old tax with new labels.

The Commission’s welcome suggests it considers the framework workable for now. Regulators spent more than a year in talks with Apple after the fine, and the fee levels Epic objects to are the ones that came out of that dialogue.

The new terms start October 1

The new terms kick in across the EU on October 1. Apple, which has long argued the DMA delays features and creates security risks for European users, gets regulatory breathing room just as its App Store model faces pressure everywhere else. EU developers finally get one rulebook instead of three overlapping ones.

Epic has no path to veto the deal, but it can keep lobbying the Commission and challenging Apple in court, which it has never been shy about. And if Apple’s implementation falls short of what regulators expect, the monitoring phase gives Brussels an easy way to reopen the fight.

title.rendered: Apple fires back at OpenAI’s bid to dismiss its trade secret lawsuit

content.rendered:
Apple is asking a federal judge to keep its trade secret case against OpenAI alive. In an opposition filed on August 19 in federal court in San Jose, Apple says OpenAI’s motion to dismiss “relies on distortion, speculation, and improper extrinsic evidence” and asks the court to deny it in full.

The filing answers the motion OpenAI, io Products, and former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan filed on August 5. That motion called Apple’s July lawsuit meritless and asked the court to end the case before discovery begins.

Apple repeats its core allegations

Apple’s response revisits the allegations in its original complaint. It says Liu, a senior system electrical engineer who spent eight years at Apple, exploited an authentication bug to access Apple’s confidential network repository for weeks after joining OpenAI. Apple alleges that he downloaded dozens of engineering files, including a presentation on how Apple builds and tests its main logic boards, and reacted to his own access in writing with “LOL … so funny.”

The filing also alleges that Tan, now OpenAI’s chief hardware officer, used Apple’s internal project codenames to quiz job candidates about unreleased products. Apple says he asked a then-current employee to bring “some parts” she worked on, including batteries and logic boards, to interviews for “show and tell.”

Apple also accuses OpenAI and io Products of building the behavior into their hiring process: structuring interviews to pull out engineering and supplier details, encouraging candidates to bring prototypes and CAD files, coaching new hires to dodge Apple’s exit procedures, and getting one of Apple’s manufacturing partners to perform a proprietary metal-finishing technique on OpenAI products.

Apple challenges OpenAI’s defenses

OpenAI’s motion says Apple never identified real trade secrets, showed actual misappropriation, or explained how it was harmed. It portrays Liu as an ex-employee helping a former colleague at an Apple manager’s request, and says Tan kept an Apple offboarding document for legitimate compliance reasons.

Apple’s answer to the Liu defense is the sharpest line in the filing: “A manager’s transition question is not authorization to raid Apple’s confidential repository.” It adds that the defendants cite nothing suggesting anyone at Apple knew about or approved the downloads.

Apple also objects to how OpenAI built its motion, saying the company leaned on outside messages, third-party websites, and attorney claims about Apple’s security practices. That kind of extrinsic evidence, Apple argues, has no place at the dismissal stage, where the court must accept the complaint’s allegations as true.

OpenAI’s public response remains firm. In a blog post titled “Apple is getting this wrong,” the company says it does not have and does not want any Apple trade secrets, and calls the lawsuit “careless, aggressive and oddly personal.”

What happens next

OpenAI’s reply is due August 26, and Judge Edward J. Davila hears arguments on the motion to dismiss on October 1 in San Jose. Apple’s separate push for a preliminary injunction, which could restrict OpenAI’s hardware work while the case plays out, runs on its own schedule: opposition briefs are due August 31, with replies by September 14.

If the motion fails, OpenAI faces discovery into its hardware program as it works toward its first devices. If it succeeds, Apple may get a chance to amend its complaint, a possibility Apple’s filing acknowledges.

title.rendered: What happens to your sprites in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 | Sprite Garden explained

content.rendered:
Fortnite recently announced a big change coming to your existing collection of sprites. Not only did they confirm a new set of sprites will replace the existing ones in Chapter 7 Season 4, but they also shared future plans for what happens to those critters you collected in Fortnite Runners.

On August 7, Fortnite officially gave the green light for the sprites gameplay feature to carry over into Fortnite Override. This was met positively by many sections of fans, as this particular aspect of the game has turned out to be very popular among players. Below, you can learn more about how the transition from Season 3 to Season 4 will affect your sprites. You can also find out everything you need to know about the newly revealed Sprite Garden map.

What happens to Chapter 7 Season 3 sprites in Season 4

Fortnite Runners brought a whopping 117 sprites (including variants) for players to catch. Courtesy of the various Sprite Hours, where the spawn rate of a particular sprite or variant is temporarily boosted, which took place at different points throughout the season, many players have put together a long lineup of their own extracted sprites.

Now, apparently, all the sprites from Chapter 7 Season 3 will be restricted to a new Fortnite map called Sprite Garden. For the Season 4 Battle Royale modes, a new set of sprites will be released, which will consist of a mix of fan-made sprites and those made by the devs. It’s worth paying attention that the devs also shared that certain previously added sprites may even be re-released, allowing them to be used beyond the Sprite Garden.

The inclusion of fan-made sprites came about after a public “Design a Sprite” contest was organized by Epic Games. Some of these sprites have already been unveiled and offer benefits as shared below.

  • Bullet Sprite: Ammo boxes grant slightly more ammunition than usual.
  • Dumpster Dive Sprite: Jumping into dumpsters will provide loot.
  • Honey Sprite: When attacked, a beehive spawns, releasing a swarm of bees onto your enemy, which will inflict light damage for a span of time.
  • Pond Sprite: Your movement speed in water increases with each level, offering boosted jump height and reduced fall damage at level 5.
  • X-Ray Sprite: Offers the ability to see through walls and other obstacles for a limited time.

Moreover, it was also noted that Fortnite Override will bring more ways to “discover” sprites, both in and out of the game. Even though it isn’t clear what this statement entails, it does suggest that sprite extraction during matches may not be the only way you can add sprites to your collection in Chapter 7 Season 4. Additionally, it was further revealed that owned gizmos, such as the Portable Extractor, and Sprite Dust will be reset for the new season.

Sprite Garden in Fortnite, explained

Sprite Garden is the island map where you would be able to equip and showcase Fortnite Runners season sprites, while also being able to visit your friends’ garden sanctuaries, possibly to take a look at their respective sprite collections. Additionally, the sprites you obtain in the Fortnite Override season will also appear in this mode as you grow your collection.

Besides the Sprite Garden, you can further display the Season 3 sprites as part of your cosmetics via the Sprite Mastery Pod Back Bling and via the Guardian Outfit. These old sprites will also still appear in the Sprites tab, together with the new sprites that will join the game eventually.

Wrapping up

With how popular sprites have turned out to be among Fortnite players, it’s no doubt that Epic Games has decided to continue this feature. The novelty of fan-made sprites in Chapter 7 Season 4 could certainly feel like a breath of fresh air.

Based on what we know so far, the incoming fleet of sprites seems to offer exciting variety. From IP-inspired sprites such as Sonic the Hedgehog Sprite to community-powered ones such as the Bullet Sprite, there is no dearth of distinct boosts provided by these backpack-like companions. However, whether or not this variety translates into another successful season for Sprite is something only time will tell.

  • Confirmed game characters in Fortnite Override
  • How to get Calm Capy sidekick in Fortnite

title.rendered: GTA 6 leak analysis: All revealed gameplay details and map locations

content.rendered:
GTA 6 has once again fallen victim to a massive leak, revealing several key gameplay features that have not been officially confirmed before. Interestingly, the latest batch of leaked details comes just days before Rockstar Games is scheduled to premiere an extended look at the hotly anticipated game on Netflix on August 27.

Throughout the course of its development, GTA 6 has suffered from multiple major leaks, which arguably also played a role in its decision to go discless with the game. In 2022, a big pile of confidential clips was shared on the internet, irking the American publisher. Right before its debut trailer in December 2023, a recording of the same was published ahead of time in another instance of a leak. Given the sheer scale of the latest leaks, it is comparable in seriousness to those that surfaced four years prior.

The freshest set of leaks is reportedly a developing situation, as the leaker behind it, Cyberleek, has said that they have more footage to spill online. Below, we have collated all the leaked unofficial information about GTA 6 that is now in the public domain.

GTA 6 latest leak explained

On August 18, a new round of GTA 6 leaks bearing the watermark “Cyberleek” started spreading on social media. Among them, two gameplay videos and an image being touted as the official in-game map gained a lot of traction and roused discussions on the internet. While one video showed GTA 6 protagonist Jason playing basketball at his safehouse, the other showed him beating down an NPC and trying to make a run for it from law enforcement in his car.

Almost as soon as the leaks began propagating online, Rockstar Games launched its offense by sending DMCA takedown notices, pulling down these clips from the sites where they were hosted. As new uploads of the footage take place, the company is quickly reacting to the same by getting those pulled down as well. Such prompt action by the gaming giant implicitly confirms the legitimacy of the leaked content.

In the immediate aftermath, Cyberleaks’ apparent motive behind the GTA 6 leak also came to the fore. Mainly, the hacker announced three “commandments” that showed their disapproval of digital pre-orders and “fake” single-player DLC, alongside their support for preservation of single-player content. Importantly, it was mentioned that any publisher breaking one of these conditions would be targeted consistently until the latter shared a public apology.

All new GTA 6 gameplay and map details revealed

Changes to Wanted System in GTA 6

The leaked footage shows Jason assaulting an NPC with a wrench and attaining a wanted level for his actions. From that sequence, we saw certain noteworthy details in the game’s Wanted System.

  1. 6-star wanted level returns for the first time since GTA 4 (2008).
  2. Police will remember distinct details about the player, including appearance, clothing, and vehicle.
  3. When you gain a wanted level, incoming police won’t be marked on the map, like in GTA 5, but instead a flashing circular zone will appear centered at your position.
  4. Directional markers indicating detection, like the ones seen in Ubisoft games such as Watch Dogs: Legion, appear when a police officer is nearby.

Driving gameplay and cars in GTA 6

One of the leaked videos shows Jason driving a Vapid ’70 Ganado rather recklessly. The short driving sequence unraveled quite a few intriguing tidbits for players to chew on.

  1. Cars will have a fuel indicator, suggesting there may be an in-game mechanic that requires refueling gas in cars before you can drive them again.
  2. The player character automatically adjusts the rear-view mirror, according to the situation.
  3. Cars can be used to store weapons and more in GTA 6. You can also close/open the trunk manually.

GTA 6 HUD details and changes

  1. The health bar doesn’t show up at all times but only when there is a change in the meter, such as when you take damage.
  2. There is a stamina bar that also shows up when there is a change. In the case of the leaked clip, repeatedly striking an NPC depleted Jason’s stamina bar.
  3. The equipped weapon in the HUD now has color and isn’t grayscale like in GTA 5.
  4. There are two money indicators, one showing money carried in the wallet and the other showing money kept at the safehouse/bank.

NPC relations in GTA 6

  1. When Jason, in the leaked clip, beat down the NPC, a purple devil emoji showed up with a minus symbol adjacent to it. This strongly hints at the incorporation of an honor system akin to the one featured in Red Dead Redemption 2, where the player’s in-game actions define how the NPCs perceive him.
  2. A split-second frame, right before the NPC fight, shows the options “Defuse” and “Warn”. This makes it very likely that RDR 2-like NPC interactions will make their way into GTA 6 as well.

Minigame in GTA 6

  1. The basketball minigame returns to GTA for the first time since GTA San Andreas (2004).
  2. A basketball backboard is apparently available right at Jason’s safehouse.

GTA 6 map locations

Alongside gameplay stuff, the entire map of Leonida was also present among the leaks. Given below are all the major map locations within Leonida, arriving in the GTA sequel.

  • Vice-Dale County
  • Leonard County
  • Lummox County
  • Kelly County
  • Mariana Country

Further, the Leonida map in GTA 6 is surrounded by three distinct water bodies, namely the Gulf of Leonida, the Leonida Straits, and the Atlantic Ocean.

Author’s take

The latest GTA 6 leak right ahead of the game’s high-profile Netflix video feature is undoubtedly an unfortunate setback for Rockstar’s marketing team. However, it seems like the problem is far from over at this point, with Cyberleaks threatening with two to four more leaks pertaining to GTA 6 in the pipeline.

Once the saga is over and the dust settles, it will be interesting to see how it impacts Rockstar Games’ plan for the August 27 premiere and GTA 6’s eventual launch on November 19. Fans would certainly hope that the fiasco Rockstar finds itself in the midst of, despite rigorously locking down their offices and communication channels, doesn’t affect the twice-delayed game’s release timeline.

title.rendered: I tried Spotify’s new Playlist Notes: Here’s how to add your own and why they’re useful

content.rendered:
Spotify has launched a new feature called Playlist Notes, and honestly, it’s one of those small updates I didn’t know I needed until I saw it.

According to Spotify’s official Newsroom, Playlist Notes lets you add your own thoughts, memories, recommendations, or little explanations to songs, podcast episodes, and audiobooks in your playlists.

For me, the best part is that it makes a playlist feel a little more personal. Instead of just adding a song and moving on, I can now leave a note explaining why it’s there. Here’s how the Spotify Playlist Notes feature works and how you can add one.

What are Spotify Playlist Notes?

Spotify Playlist Notes let you attach a written note to individual tracks, podcast episodes, or audiobooks inside a playlist you created or collaborated on. Think of them as tiny captions attached to the things you listen to.

You can use a note to explain:

  • Why you added a song
  • Where you discovered it
  • What memory it reminds you of
  • Why you think someone else should listen
  • What mood it is supposed to create
  • Why it belongs in that particular playlist
  • What makes the track special to you

A normal playlist tells someone what to listen to. A playlist with notes can tell them why. And I think that makes a huge difference.

Spotify says the feature is designed to let listeners capture memories, share recommendations, and explain why particular picks made the cut. Notes are visible to anyone who can view the playlist, and the note author’s name links to their Spotify profile.

Note: Playlist Notes are different from playlist descriptions, which tell you about the playlist. Notes are about the individual song.

How to add notes to a Spotify Playlist

The good news: Spotify hasn’t buried this feature behind menus and a settings page. Writing a custom user note to your Spotify Playlist takes just a few taps.

Here’s how I use Spotify Playlist Notes:

  1. Open a playlist you own or collaborate on.
  2. Find the song, podcast episode, or audiobook you want to annotate.
  3. Tap the three dots (…) next to it.
  4. Select Add note from the menu.
  5. Write your note and tap Save.

That’s it. Your note will appear underneath the item in the playlist.

If you don’t see the Add Note feature yet, don’t immediately assume you’re doing something wrong. It may simply not have reached your account.

Spotify says Playlist Notes are currently rolling out to iOS and Android users in more than 100 markets globally, although availability can vary as the rollout continues. I recommend updating the app to get the latest features as they become available.

My favorite thing about Spotify Playlist Notes

The obvious use for Playlist Notes is writing something like: “This was my favorite song of the summer.” And that’s fine. But honestly, I think you’re underselling the feature if that’s all you use it for.

The more interesting notes are the ones that give the listener a reason to stop and care. For example, I added: “Play this one when you’re driving home after midnight.” That’s better than writing “Great song.”

Even better if you write: “Added this after hearing it at that tiny club in Berlin. The live version was even better.” Now you’ve created context. The song isn’t just audio anymore. It’s attached to a place, a moment, and a story. That’s where Spotify Playlist Notes become genuinely interesting.

4 actually useful ways to use Spotify Playlist Notes

If you’re wondering what you’re supposed to write in these little notes, don’t overthink it.

Here are the uses I think are genuinely worth trying.

1. Turn a playlist into a personal time capsule

This is probably the most meaningful use.

Create a playlist for a particular period of your life and use notes to preserve the details that you’ll forget later.

Try notes like:

  • “I found this during my first month at the new job.”
  • “Played this constantly during the summer of 2026.”
  • “This was on repeat during our Paris trip.”
  • “First heard this at 2 a.m. and immediately added it.”

Six months from now, the playlist will be more than music. It becomes evidence of who you were.

2. Explain why a song is there

We’ve all received a playlist from someone containing one completely baffling song.

Now there’s an easy solution. Write: “Trust me. Wait until the chorus.” Or: “This doesn’t make sense until track 7.”

Suddenly, the listener has a reason to keep going. I think it will finally make the carefully sequenced playlists, where every track is supposed to lead into the next, easy to understand.

3. Make better shared playlists

This is where I think Playlist Notes could become surprisingly useful.

Spotify allows people to collaborate on playlists, so multiple people can contribute tracks. But collaboration can also create musical chaos. One person adds indie rock, another adds Bollywood, and others add a 12-minute experimental jazz track.

A note can provide some context: “Added this for the late-night section.” Or: “This is the song I meant when I said something dreamy.” It gives collaborators a little more communication without having to leave Spotify.

4. Create a playlist for someone else

It helps me more when making a playlist for a friend and adding a short personal note to every few songs.

For example: “You said you wanted something upbeat for your morning commute. Start here.” Then: “This one reminded me of you immediately.” Or: “As you like K-Pop, listen to this one”

It’s like I am giving them a guided tour through my taste. And don’t write reviews; only add context for the emotional touch.

6. Remember why you saved a Podcast or Audiobook

This is an underrated part of the update. Spotify isn’t limiting Playlist Notes to music. You can also add notes to podcast episodes and audiobooks you’ve added to playlists.

That opens up a completely different use case. I have added: “Listen to this episode before the interview.” Or: “The section around 32 minutes is the part I want to revisit.” It made my saved audio easier to navigate and remember.

Note: Notes are visible to people who can view your playlist, so don’t treat them like private diary entries. Additionally, Spotify says Playlist Notes must comply with its Platform Rules and Terms of Use. So, be careful!

Spotify is also giving its editors a voice

There is another side to Playlist Notes that I find even more interesting. Spotify isn’t only giving listeners the ability to add notes. Spotify’s editors are getting them too.

According to Spotify, editors can use Playlist Notes to explain why a track matters, why it is culturally relevant, or why it belongs in a particular playlist. The company is also introducing Editor Profiles, where listeners can see an editor’s top tracks and albums, as well as the playlists they contribute to.

Initially, editor notes are appearing on major playlists, including:

  • Today’s Top Hits
  • RapCaviar
  • Hot Country
  • All New Pop
  • mint
  • Fresh Finds Hip-Hop

Simply open the Playlist, tap the Notes button above the tracks, and the editor’s notes will appear.

The editorial rollout is currently aimed at Free and Premium users aged 16 and older in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand.

And this is where Spotify is making a subtle but important shift. For years, editorial playlists have largely been a black box. A song appears, you listen, and move on. Now Spotify can potentially give you a little more of the human reasoning behind that choice.

Your Spotify playlists just got a memory

Spotify has spent years getting better at predicting what we want to hear next. Playlist Notes add something the algorithm can’t manufacture quite as convincingly: personal meaning.

So the next time you create a playlist, don’t just add the song. Add the reason, memory, joke, warning, or tiny piece of context that turns a random track into your track.

What do you think about the new Spotify feature? Let me know in the comments below!

  • How to Transfer Spotify Playlists to Apple Music on iPhone

title.rendered: How to see sensitive content on X (Twitter): The settings that actually worked for me

content.rendered:
If you have ever searched for something on X (formerly Twitter), clicked a post, and found yourself facing a “This media may contain sensitive material” warning, then you are not alone. The frustrating part is that X makes this sound more complicated than it really is.

I went looking for the setting that actually controls sensitive media, expecting to find one obvious switch. Instead, there are two controls that matter: one for media in your X feed and another for sensitive content in search results.

So if you are trying to see sensitive content on X (Twitter), including NSFW, adult, graphic, violent, or other sensitive media that X has placed behind a warning, here is the setup that matters. I have shared the steps for iPhone, Android, and browser.

Before you start: What X calls “sensitive content”

First, a quick clarification: sensitive content on X doesn’t always mean violence or NSFW material.

X automatically applies sensitive-media labels to material that some users may reasonably prefer not to encounter unexpectedly. That can include things such as:

  1. Graphic Content: Posts showing excessive violence, death, medical procedures, or abuse involving people or animals.
  2. Gratuitous Gore: Extremely graphic scenes like mutilation, torture, or corpses, way beyond typical horror.
  3. Adult Nudity & Sexual Behavior: Consensual sexual acts or nudity (real or animated) meant for arousal.
  4. Violent Sexual Conduct: Any sexual act involving violence or non-consent, real or simulated.
  5. Sensitive Topics: Mentions of suicide, self-harm, or abuse that aren’t graphic but are emotionally heavy.
  6. Emotionally Charged Content: Posts about political conflicts, global issues, or divisive topics likely to spark fights.

Note: Content involving sexual violence, bestiality, or necrophilia is never allowed on X, not even with sensitive content settings enabled.

X’s policies specifically allow some consensually produced adult content when it is appropriately marked as sensitive. But remember that turning on sensitive content does not mean X suddenly removes its other rules.

You are changing what your account is willing to display. You are not disabling the platform’s content policies. And that is the first mistake I see people make: they assume there is one universal “show everything” button.

Who can actually view sensitive content on X?

This is where things get important. Changing your settings does not guarantee that every piece of sensitive or adult content will become visible.

X restricts certain adult content for users who are under 18 or who have not provided a birth date on their profile when signing up. So, if you are over 18 and still cannot see sensitive posts, do not immediately assume the account is broken.

Check these things first:

  1. Is your date of birth on your X profile?
  2. Is sensitive media enabled in your media settings?
  3. Is X’s safe search filtering sensitive posts?
  4. Are you using the iOS app, where some sensitive-content behavior differs from the web?
  5. Is the specific post restricted for another reason?

That last point is important. A sensitive-content setting cannot override an age restriction, deleted post, protected account, suspended account, or content that X has removed. In other words, the setting gives you permission to see eligible sensitive media; it does not make unavailable posts magically reappear.

The main fix: Turn on sensitive media on feed and search results

This is the part that actually solved the problem for me.

I found two settings worth checking. The first controls sensitive media displayed in posts. It controls whether you see a warning blur over potentially sensitive media. The second controls Safe Search, which can hide sensitive content from your search results entirely.

If you only change the first one, you can still wonder why sensitive posts are missing from search. That is because feed visibility and search filtering are not the same thing.

On iPhone and iPad

Here’s the annoying part: iPhone and iPad users need to use the X/Twitter website rather than the iOS app to change this preference.

  1. Launch Safari or any other browser on your iPhone and go to x.com.
  2. Tap Sign in and use the credentials to log into your account.
  3. Now, tap your profile picture at the top, then scroll down and select Settings and privacy.
  4. Then go to Privacy and safety and tap the Content you see option.
  5. Check the box next to Display media that may contain sensitive content. It will remove the X/Twitter sensitive content warning from your feed.
  6. Next, select Search settings and untick the Hide sensitive content box.

While testing the feature, I noticed that some sensitive posts behind an interstitial still can’t be clicked through in the iOS app, even though the sensitive-media preference is managed on the website. So, you need to use the web version to access content that the iOS app doesn’t show.

On Android

The good news is that the X app on Android offers sensitive content settings. Follow these steps below:

  1. Open the X app and tap your profile picture.
  2. Select Settings and privacy on the left sidebar.
  3. Tap Privacy and safety from the menu.
  4. Go to Content you see and select Sensitive media.
  5. Tick the box for Display media that may contain sensitive content.

However, it doesn’t include the Safe Search settings. You need to go to the X website to disable the filter on your account.

On the web (Mac and PC)

I prefer the web version as it includes all the relevant settings in one place. And once I change the settings, it syncs my choices across the platforms.

  1. Log in to your account on X.com.
  2. Click More (three-dot button) and select Settings and privacy
  3. Now, click Privacy and safety on the left side, then go to Content you see.
  4. Select the box for Display media that may contain sensitive content.
  5. Then click Search settings and uncheck Hide sensitive content to enable it.

What the setting does and what it doesn’t do

Turning on the sensitive-media preference tells X that you are willing to see media that it has identified as potentially sensitive rather than automatically hiding it behind the default warning.

X describes these controls as a way for users to decide whether they want to see warnings over potentially sensitive media. Disabling Hide sensitive content in Search settings also allows potentially sensitive posts to be included in search results.

It does not:

  • Make deleted posts visible
  • Bypass private/protected accounts
  • Override age restrictions
  • Guarantee every sensitive post appears in search
  • Remove X’s content rules
  • Make prohibited content available

X explicitly notes that search results are filtered for quality and relevance, and that not every post will necessarily appear in search. That’s why I would not describe this as a “show everything” setting.

How to mark your own posts as sensitive on X (Twitter)

If you’re looking for the sensitive content rules on X because you post such media yourself, the process is slightly different. X provides a setting called Mark media you post as containing material that may be sensitive

  1. On the X web version, go to Settings and privacy > Privacy and safety.
  2. Select Your posts from the menu, and you will find the sensitive-media option.
  3. Turn this ON if you regularly post graphic, mature, or potentially sensitive material.

When I enabled it, people visiting my profile saw a notice indicating that my account may include potentially sensitive content. If your posts are generally safe-for-work, leave this OFF to ensure your content remains visible without warnings.

You can also mark individual photos and videos when attaching them to a post. This option is available across Android, iOS, and the web.

  1. Start a new post and attach an image or video.
  2. Tap on the attached media.
  3. Select the paintbrush or edit icon.
  4. Then use these steps according to your device:
    • On iPhone: Tap the three-dot icon > Content settings and toggle on Nudity, Violence, or Sensitive. Tap Done to save.
    • On Android: Tap the three-dot icon > Content settings and toggle on Adult content, Graphic violence, or Other.
    • On web: Move to the flag icon and choose the appropriate tag: Nudity, Violence, or Sensitive.

This lets you tag specific content without affecting your entire account. When in doubt, it’s safer to flag it—it helps avoid moderation issues. Keep in mind that marking content as sensitive may reduce its visibility. Some people might not see it, depending on their settings.

Sensitive content warning still appearing? Try these fixes

If you enabled the setting and nothing changed, work through these in order.

  • Check your birthday: If you are trying to access adult content, make sure your X account has an accurate date of birth. X restricts adult content for users under 18 and for accounts without a listed birth date.
  • Check Safe Search separately: When sensitive posts appear normally on profiles or in your feed but disappear when you search, make sure Hide sensitive content is disabled.
  • Try X.com instead of the app: The web version can be the easiest way to find sensitive media control settings that are unavailable in the app.
  • Give the setting a little time: X notes that some search-setting changes may take several minutes to take effect. So if you switch the setting and immediately test it, don’t assume it failed.
  • Remember that some posts are simply unavailable: A post may have been deleted, an account may be protected or suspended, or X may have restricted the content for another policy reason. No sensitive-content toggle can override that.

I advise being cautious about accessing sensitive material because it may trigger emotional distress or impact your mental well-being. In addition, interacting with posts that do not comply with X’s guidelines could result in account restrictions.

Wrapping up

There you go. Getting your sensitive content settings unlocked isn’t that complicated once you know the little-known requirements. I get it if you’re curious or just want more control over what shows up in your feed; same here. Just keep in mind it’s a bit of a wild ride once it’s all turned on.

Also, if you use X on multiple devices, it is also worth checking the settings on each one instead of assuming everything has synced correctly. Once those are sorted, you should have a much easier time finding the content you’re looking for.

Also read:

  • How to pin a post on X (Twitter) on iPhone, iPad, or desktop
  • How to delete your Twitter account permanently
  • How to Turn ON Twitter Lights Out Dark Mode on iPhone and iPad

@graph.name: How to View Sensitive Content on X (Twitter) On iPhone, iPad, and Android
@graph.description: Learn how to enable sensitive content on the X (formerly Twitter) app using your iPhone, iPad, or Android device to see all media without restrictions.

step.name: Open the X app and log in
step.text: Launch the X app on your device and sign in to your account.

itemListElement.text: Open the X app on your iPhone, iPad, or Android.
Log in using your username and password if you're not already signed in.

step.name: Go to Settings and Privacy
step.text: Tap your profile icon at the top-left, scroll down, and select Settings & Support, then tap Settings and Privacy.

itemListElement.text: Tap your profile picture in the top-left corner of the screen.
Scroll down and tap Settings & Support.

step.name: Enable sensitive content
step.text: Navigate to Privacy and Safety, then tap Content you see, and switch on Display media that may contain sensitive content.

itemListElement.text: Turn on Display media that may contain sensitive content.

@graph.name: How to View Sensitive Content on X (Twitter) On the Web (Mac or PC)
@graph.description: Learn how to enable sensitive content on the X (formerly Twitter) website using a Mac or Windows PC to view all types of media.

step.name: Sign in on X.com
step.text: Visit X.com in your web browser and log in to your account.

itemListElement.text: Go to X.com on your browser.
Sign in using your account credentials.

step.name: Access Settings and Privacy
step.text: Click the More option in the left sidebar, then choose Settings and Privacy.

itemListElement.text: Click More in the sidebar menu.

step.name: Open Content Settings
step.text: Go into Privacy and Safety, tap Content you see, and check the box to allow sensitive content.

itemListElement.text: Check the box for Display media that may contain sensitive content.

@graph.name: How to Show Sensitive Content in X Search Results (On iPhone, iPad, or Android)
@graph.description: Here's how you can adjust your settings in the X (formerly Twitter) app on mobile devices to allow sensitive content to appear in your search results.

step.name: Open the X app and sign in
step.text: Launch the X app on your mobile device and log in to your account if needed.

itemListElement.text: Open the X app on your iPhone, iPad, or Android device.
Sign in with your credentials if you're not already logged in.

step.name: Navigate to Search Settings
step.text: Tap your profile icon, go to Settings & Support > Settings and Privacy > Privacy and Safety > Content you see, and then enter Search settings.

itemListElement.text: Tap your profile picture in the top-left corner.
Scroll to Settings & Support, then tap Settings and Privacy.

step.name: Disable Hide Sensitive Content
step.text: Toggle off the option labeled Hide sensitive content so search results will include sensitive media.

itemListElement.text: Find the setting labeled Hide sensitive content.
Toggle it off to allow sensitive content in search results.

@graph.name: How to Show Sensitive Content in X Search Results On the Web (Mac or PC)
@graph.description: Enable sensitive content in X.com search results on your Mac or PC browser by adjusting your account settings.

step.name: Log in to X.com
step.text: Open X.com in a browser on your computer and sign in to your account.

itemListElement.text: Head to X.com in your preferred web browser.
Log in using your username and password.

step.name: Go to Search Settings
step.text: Click More in the sidebar, then go to Settings and Privacy > Privacy and Safety > Content you see > Search settings.

itemListElement.text: Click More in the sidebar menu.

step.name: Show sensitive content
step.text: Uncheck the box next to Hide sensitive content so it shows in search results.

itemListElement.text: Find the option labeled Hide sensitive content.
Uncheck the box to allow sensitive content in search results.

keyPoints.title: Understanding Sensitive Content on X
keyPoints.explanation: Sensitive content on X includes a range of material from graphic violence to serious topics like abuse, which the platform flags to protect users and adhere to legal standards.

keyPoints.title: Why X Flags Content as Sensitive
keyPoints.explanation: X flags content as sensitive to prevent chaos, safeguard minors, and respect international laws, using evolving guidelines that can include blocking certain content.

keyPoints.title: Deciding What Counts as Sensitive
keyPoints.explanation: Content is flagged through community reports, algorithms, and policy reviews, with some topics like bestiality or necrophilia being permanently banned regardless of user settings.

keyPoints.title: Viewing Sensitive Content Settings
keyPoints.explanation: Users must verify they are over 18, have their profile birth date set, and may need to adjust settings on web or desktop to view sensitive content in their feed and search results.

keyPoints.title: Differences Between Feed and Search Content Rules
keyPoints.explanation: Sensitive media display rules differ for the main feed and search results, requiring separate toggles to control content visibility in each section.

title.rendered: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens with Study Hours, homework nudges, and stricter safety rules

content.rendered:
OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT for Teens, a version of ChatGPT that under-18 accounts get automatically. It leans on Study Mode for schoolwork, adds new Study Hours and homework reminders, and turns on stricter content protections and parental notifications by default. Anyone who says they are 13 to 17, or who OpenAI’s age-prediction system estimates is under 18, is placed in it without creating a new account.

The rollout started on August 18 for eligible teen accounts on Free and paid personal plans, and OpenAI says availability will expand over the coming weeks. Australia is expected to get full access on September 8.

Study Mode becomes the default for homework

The biggest change is how ChatGPT handles schoolwork. Study Mode, which walks students through a problem with guiding questions and step-by-step hints instead of handing over the answer, is the centerpiece of the teen experience. New responsible homework reminders try to spot when a teen appears to be shortcutting an assignment and steer them into Study Mode.

Two other pieces round it out:

  • Study Hours let a teen, or a linked parent, pick times when new chats start in Study Mode by default. It does not block ChatGPT; it just changes how ChatGPT answers during those hours.
  • Quizzes and Learning Visualizations give teens ways to test themselves and see tricky math or science concepts drawn out.

Teens also get onboarding that walks through these tools, learning-focused starter prompts, and simple customization like accent colors and voice options.

Stronger protections and more parent alerts

ChatGPT for Teens applies OpenAI’s under-18 model rules by default, with extra protections in higher-risk areas such as self-harm, violence, eating disorders, dangerous activities, and explicit or graphic content. The model is also told not to use romantic language, encourage emotional dependence, or suggest it has feelings or consciousness. That goes beyond blocking romantic roleplay, which OpenAI restricted for teens earlier.

The break reminders ChatGPT added last year show up more often for teens during long sessions, and ChatGPT will nudge teens to check a photo for private details before uploading it, even something as ordinary as a photo of handwritten notes.

Parents with linked accounts keep the tools that came with ChatGPT’s parental controls last September: Quiet Hours that limit access at set times, control over selected settings, and safety notifications in limited high-risk situations. OpenAI is now adding notifications related to eating disorders on top of the existing alerts for signs of acute distress. Parents still cannot read a teen’s conversations, and OpenAI says it shares only what is needed to help in a safety situation.

The move follows Meta AI’s parent alerts for self-harm conversations, so parent notifications are becoming the norm across the big AI assistants rather than an OpenAI-only feature.

What happens if you land in it by mistake

Because placement relies partly on age prediction, some adults will end up in ChatGPT for Teens. OpenAI’s fix is the same as before: verify your age with OpenAI to have the teen protections removed. Going the other way, when ChatGPT decides an account holder has turned 18, the account may move out of the teen experience, which can also end a linked parental-controls connection.

OpenAI is also starting to publish under-18 evaluations in its system cards, showing how its models handle teen-specific tests around self-harm, eating disorders, violence, age-restricted goods, and sexual content. That is a small step toward outside scrutiny of claims that have so far been hard to check.

The company still faces lawsuits from families who say ChatGPT contributed to harm to their children, and critics such as Common Sense Media maintain that social AI companions are not safe for kids at all. ChatGPT for Teens is OpenAI’s answer to that pressure: keep teens on the platform, but change what the platform does for them.

title.rendered: Apple pulls an AI “nudify” app after Meta ran ads for it with a deepfake of a US politician

content.rendered:
Apple has removed an App Store app called Kromix that let paying users drop real people’s photos into AI-generated pornographic videos, after WIRED reported that Meta had been running Facebook and Instagram ads for it. One of those ads showed a woman closely resembling a prominent female US politician standing in front of a US flag, then cut to a pornographic deepfake with the same face. Meta pulled the ads and Apple pulled the app, both after WIRED asked about them.

Kromix listed itself as an “AI image styler.” The ads were less subtle: a voice-over promised “no restrictions,” said “all the characters are real people,” and called it “the AI that men actually use.”

What Meta’s ad system missed

The ads were found by the Tech Transparency Project, a watchdog group. According to Meta’s own ad library, they were targeted only at male users. Meta says the account behind them ran 32 ads, each live for between five and 46 hours, and most were seen ten times or fewer. The Facebook page that ran them was created on August 3 and had no followers, two signals that should have looked suspicious to Meta.

Most of the video ads opened with a harmless cover image, like a beach or a waterfall, before switching to the explicit content. Meta says it knows this trick and blocks many ads that use it, but “no system is perfect,” and it is still investigating how these got through. Meta’s rules already ban sexual content in ads and specifically prohibit promoting “nudify” apps. By its own count, Meta removed more than 340,000 nudify ads between November and January and has sued at least one nudify developer, yet researchers keep finding new ones.

Apple says the app changed after review

Apple told WIRED that Kromix appeared to have added the prohibited features after it passed initial App Review. Its statement repeats the usual line: Apple has “always strictly prohibited apps designed to generate, distribute, or consume pornography,” nudification apps break the App Review Guidelines, and it goes after both the apps and the developer accounts behind them.

That bait-and-switch pattern is the hard part for Apple. An app can look like a generic photo tool on submission day and turn into something very different after an update or a server-side change, and App Review does not catch every version. Apple ran into a similar problem with Grok earlier this year. After users generated millions of sexualized images and senators pushed Apple and Google to drop X and Grok, Apple warned xAI to fix the chatbot’s deepfake output or risk removal rather than pulling it outright.

Kromix was not the only removal. Apple also pulled MaskAI, a face-swap app that let users put people into sexual scenes. Some of the Meta ads pointing to MaskAI were among the more than 50 ads containing AI-generated child sexual abuse imagery that the same researchers surfaced earlier this month.

This lands a month after San Francisco’s warning

In July, San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu sent Apple and Google cease-and-desist letters over 13 nudify and face-swap apps, eight of them on the App Store, and gave both companies 28 days to respond. Apple said at the time it had removed three of the named apps and was shutting down their developer accounts. Kromix and MaskAI show that new ones keep arriving through the front door, and that Meta’s ad network is helping them find customers.

If you run into an app or ad like this, you can report it from the App Store listing or from the ad’s menu on Facebook and Instagram. The bigger fix, catching these before they go live, is on Apple and Meta.

title.rendered: How to get the Phantom Blade Zero skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Phantom Blade Zero, one of 2026’s most promising games, has collaborated with Epic Games to make its protagonist, Soul, available as a Fortnite skin. This team-up comes just a couple of months ahead of the action-RPG title’s release on October 29, 2026.

The Phantom Blade Zero x Fortnite collab was first revealed on August 11, the same day on which the wuxia game’s pre-orders kicked off for PC and PS5 users. Unlike other platforms and storefronts, if you buy the forthcoming game on the Epic Games Store at any point of time, you also instantly get the Soul outfit for Fortnite. Importantly, the game is priced at $59.99 (₹4,299), with its Digital Deluxe Edition variant retailing for $69.99 (₹5,199).

Steps to claim the Phantom Blade skin in Fortnite

  1. Open the Epic Games Store, type “Phantom Blade Zero” in the search bar at the top and select the game when it appears.
  2. On the game’s store page, click on the Pre-Purchase button.
  3. Then, select your preferred payment method, enter the required details, and click on “Pay Now.”

After you complete the purchase, besides the Soul outfit, you will get two additional themed cosmetics in Fortnite. These are the Sanguine pickaxe and the Sanguine back bling, which round out the Phantom Blade Zero set.

Moreover, those who prefer to buy the game on a different platform or don’t want to buy the game at all can also get the Soul outfit. From October 29 to November 5 (Phantom Blade Zero launch week), the game’s cosmetics will go live in the Item Shop for players to buy using V-Bucks.

Other free skins bundled with Epic Games Store purchases

Similar to Phantom Blade Zero, Epic has partnered with some of the most popular games in 2026 to bring more game characters to Fortnite as skins. These titles include widely acclaimed AAA hits such as Resident Evil: Requiem and indie darlings such as Dave the Diver.

Following are some of the skins emerging from a newer lineup of such collabs that the Tim Sweeney-led company has announced in 2026 so far. All these items are bundled bonuses that are unlocked once you purchase the respective game on the Epic Games Store or make a qualifying in-game purchase in the case of free-to-play live-service titles available on the client.

Grace Ashcroft (Resident Evil: Requiem)

Adam Smasher (Cyberpunk 2077)

Dave (Dave The Diver)

Mad Moxxi (Borderlands 4)

Kliff (Crimson Desert)

Excalibur (Warframe)

The Traveler (Cronos: The New Dawn)

Fernet (Kernel Hearts)

Coach Gabi (Rematch)

Goal Getter (Goals)

Wrapping up

While the Epic Games Store still trails Steam by a sizable margin when it comes to total user base, the special perks the storefront provides, such as free Fortnite outfits with partner titles, are something worth praising. Not only do they provide a fair amount of incentive for players to make purchases on Epic’s client, but they also act as a way to promote partnered games via Fortnite, one of the most played games in the world.

FAQs

Which cosmetics do I get after purchasing Phantom Blade Zero on the Epic Games Store?

Upon purchasing Phantom Blade Zero via the store, you will automatically unlock the Soul outfit, the Sanguine pickaxe, and the Sanguine back bling.

Which platforms will the Phantom Blade Zero cosmetics be available on?

As long as you are using the same Epic Games Store account that you used to pre-order the game, you will be able to use the skin across all platforms where Fortnite is available.

Until when is the Phantom Blade Zero skin available with the game’s purchase on the Epic Games Store?

The Soul outfit can be claimed in Fortnite as a freebie with Phantom Blade Zero’s purchase as long as the latter game is still available on the PC storefront. Hence, it can be interpreted as a permanent offer.

  • How to get Calm Capy sidekick in Fortnite
  • How to get the Lilith skin and Borderlands bundle

title.rendered: Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 Override: All confirmed game characters, sprites, and mythics

content.rendered:
With only a few days to go until Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 Override rolls out, devs have been sharing glimpses of what’s coming via teaser images and videos. This ongoing hype build-up also saw the release of two full-fledged trailers that shed light on the various game characters slated to appear in the next season.

Apart from its video game IP-centric theme, Fortnite Override also has players keen because it’s going to retain the sprite gameplay feature from the previous season and build on it with a fresh set of these critters. Fortunately, a few fleeting seconds of these forthcoming sprites were also revealed in the recent media released for the new season.

Below, you can find a detailed breakdown of such images and clips, bringing forth the characters and sprites that are now basically confirmed to be a part of Fortnite Override.

Confirmed game characters in Fortnite Override

A variety of characters from various game franchises, ranging from classic IPs such as Pac-Man to newer hits such as Peak, are scattered throughout Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4’s key art and trailer. These characters shall be introduced in the next season as skins, sidekicks, and other cosmetic items.

1. Sonic The Hedgehog

2. Shadow The Hedgehog

3. Tails (from Sonic The Hedgehog)

4. Eggman (from Sonic The Hedgehog)

5. Ryu (from Street Fighter)

6. Blanka (from Street Fighter)

7. Scorpion, Raiden, Kitana (from Mortal Kombat)

8. Joker (from Persona)

9. Morgana (from Persona)

10. Mega Man

11. Rush (from Mega Man)

12. Spyro

13. Crash Bandicoot

14. Pac-Man

15. Lara Croft (from Tomb Raider)

16. Master Chief (from Halo)

17. Sora (from Kingdom Hearts)

18. Scout (from Peak)

19. Geralt Of Rivia (from The Witcher)

20. Deer (from 99 Nights In The Forest/Roblox)

Confirmed sprites in Fortnite Override

Besides video game characters appearing as Fortnite skins, there is another way they are clearly set to be used, which is as a sprite. As a matter of fact, some game-inspired sprites even appear in the Fortnite Override trailer, along with some other sprites apparently based on original characters created by Epic Games.

1. Sonic The Hedgehog Sprite

Ability: As seen in the trailer, equipping this sprite enables players to sprint very fast, akin to Sonic.

2. Tails Sprite

Ability: This sprite allows you to hover in the air and cover distances.

3. Jazz Jackrabbit Sprite

Ability: There was one benefit of equipping the Jazz Jackrabbit Sprite shown in the video, which was an increased jump height.

4. Klombo Sprite

Ability: The few seconds of Jonesy using it in the trailer show what might be a boosted slide, but nothing concrete about its ability has been revealed yet.

5. Killswitch Sprite

Ability: This sprite’s power-up has to do with gun damage; however, the exact benefit isn’t known as of now.

6. Victory Crown Sprite

Ability: There are few to no leads that tell more about this particular sprite’s benefit.

7. Adventurer Sprite

Ability: This critter apparently grants the power to see through walls, as can be seen in the Fortnite Override trailer.

Confirmed mythic weapons

In addition to game characters and their sprite versions, a couple of different mythic weapons were also showcased in the minute-and-a-half-long trailer. These items belong to the Mega Man and Cyberpunk 2077 IPs and are listed below.

1. Mega Man Mythic

Usage: This item is essentially like having Mega Man’s iconic Mega Buster attached to your character’s hand. It allows you to shoot rounds from it.

2. Arasaka guns

Usage: There is a split-second glimpse of HJSH-18 Masamune and TKI-20 Shingen guns in the trailer, which are Arasaka-manufactured weapons in the Cyberpunk 2077 lore.

Rounding up

Fortnite Override is shaping up to be a promising new season, not just for the game’s fans but also those invested in other game franchises that have made an appearance in the media released thus far. It will be interesting to see if this excitement and hype can translate into strong engagement numbers for the online multiplayer title.

While the aforementioned video game brands are set to have some sort of role to play in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4, more could be joining the lineup sooner rather than later. In the newest development, Nintendo also teased partnering with Epic Games for Fortnite’s new season. As a result, fans have been hoping for more popular characters from the Japanese gaming giant, such as Mario and Link, to be eventually unveiled for Epic’s live-service game.

mainEntity.name: Which cosmetics do I get after purchasing Phantom Blade Zero on the Epic Games Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Upon purchasing Phantom Blade Zero via the store, you will automatically unlock the Soul outfit, the Sanguine pickaxe, and the Sanguine back bling.

mainEntity.name: Which platforms will the Phantom Blade Zero cosmetics be available on?

acceptedAnswer.text: As long as you are using the same Epic Games Store account that you used to pre-order the game, you will be able to use the skin across all platforms where Fortnite is available.

mainEntity.name: Until when is the Phantom Blade Zero skin available with the game's purchase on the Epic Games Store?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Soul outfit can be claimed in Fortnite as a freebie with Phantom Blade Zero's purchase as long as the latter game is still available on the PC storefront. Hence, it can be interpreted as a permanent offer.

title.rendered: Download official macOS 27 Golden Gate wallpapers (4K light & dark versions)

content.rendered:
Apple has expanded the macOS 27 Golden Gate wallpaper collection once again. With the sixth beta, Apple has added two new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers called Golden Gate Day and Golden Gate Evening.

These new designs join the Golden Gate Sunset, Golden Gate Night, and abstract Celosia wallpapers introduced in earlier betas. The latest additions give you more options to enjoy the iconic bridge across different times of the day.

The best part is you don’t need to install the macOS 27 beta to enjoy the new look. Below is the official macOS 27 Golden Gate wallpaper collection in high resolution, available to download for free. We have shared both Light and Dark variants.

Get new Golden Gate Day and Evening wallpapers 

The Golden Gate Bridge has always been one of San Francisco’s most recognizable landmarks, and Apple is using it as the visual centerpiece of macOS 27.

The latest macOS 27 beta 6 wallpapers take a more scenic approach compared to the original abstract design. They showcase the Golden Gate Bridge in different lighting conditions, adding more variety to Apple’s growing wallpaper collection.

Like the Sunset and Night wallpapers, the new designs are more than static backgrounds. They animate when you unlock your Mac and can also be used as screen savers. When used as a screen saver, both wallpapers feature cars slowly driving across the Golden Gate Bridge, adding a subtle sense of motion to the desktop experience.

Apple has now included four scenic Golden Gate wallpapers across the recent beta releases:

  • Golden Gate Day
  • Golden Gate Evening
  • Golden Gate Sunset
  • Golden Gate Night

macOS 27 also continues to offer the abstract Golden Gate Celosia wallpaper for users who prefer a cleaner, less scenic desktop background. The design resembles the sculpted, organic forms of the celosia flower, subtly forming the number 27. I liked how the overall composition feels premium, refined, and timeless while avoiding visual clutter.

Download official macOS 27 Golden Gate wallpapers 

The original Golden Gate wallpapers are available in two versions. In the Light edition, the wallpaper blends warm sandy gold tones into subtle purples, whereas Dark mode transitions into deep indigo hues accented by silvery-blue highlights. The color scheme resembles iOS 27 official wallpapers.

Additionally, the newer Day, Evening, Sunset, and Night designs complement these original wallpapers while giving you more ways to customize your Mac’s desktop. All are available in a resolution of 4480 × 3088 pixels, making them suitable for all Mac models, including iMac, Studio Display XDR, and even high-resolution external monitors.

Download Golden Gate wallpapers: Day | Evening | Sunset | Night | Light | Dark

Note: The dynamic switching, animated versions, and screen saver behavior are part of macOS 27. If you download the wallpapers as regular image files, they will work as static desktop backgrounds. 

Why do these wallpapers work so well? 

One reason the official macOS 27 wallpapers stand out is their balance between aesthetics and usability.

The design provides:

  • Great visibility for icons
  • Limited visual distractions
  • Strong contrast in both light and dark modes
  • Consistent appearance across different display sizes
  • A premium look on Retina displays

Apple clearly designed these wallpapers to enhance the desktop experience with the refined Liquid Glass look.

Final thoughts 

The new Golden Gate Day and Golden Gate Evening wallpapers make Apple’s macOS 27 wallpaper collection even more impressive. Along with the Sunset and Night versions, they offer a nice mix of scenic and abstract designs without making the desktop feel overly busy.

If you don’t want to install the macOS 27 beta, downloading the wallpapers is an easy way to bring a little of the Golden Gate look to your Mac right now. For the full experience, you need to wait for the public release expected in September.

In case you missed:

  • Download the official MacBook Neo wallpapers
  • Download the official Apple wallpapers for the Year of the Horse
  • Apple’s new iPhone Mirroring features in macOS 27
