title.rendered: Gem sprites in Fortnite: Where to find them and what they do

content.rendered:
Throughout Chapter 7 Season 3, sprites have made Fortnite even more engaging by adding a unique gameplay twist to its unranked modes. Courtesy of weekly sprite additions, this engagement has regularly peaked at the time of a new update, the latest of which added gem sprites to the mix.

Sprite variants in Fortnite have aided players in combining two different gameplay bonuses into a single sprite. With the release of gem sprites, the number of these variants has also increased to eight. As of now, the current lineup of sprite variants includes base, gold, gummy, galaxy, gem, holofoil, cube, and quack.

What does a gem sprite do in Fortnite?

When you equip a gem sprite, it offers you a 30% reduction in fall damage. It’s worth paying attention here that even though the fall damage goes down with this sprite, it doesn’t make you invincible to being knocked out after a big fall, especially if you were already low on health.

Courtesy of the boost it provides, the gem sprite variant is quite useful for traversal in Fortnite. In particular, the Gem Aura Sprite is a great pick for those who want to scour the map with as much ease of traversal as equipping a sprite could offer. That’s because, combined with the Aura Sprite, it also gives you Shock Rock charge when you deal sufficient damage to your opponents, unlocking maneuvers such as double jumps.

Where to find gem sprites in Fortnite

To be able to find rare sprites such as the gem variants quicker, it’s highly beneficial to extract and equip a holofoil variant sprite first. The latter boosts your chances of finding rare sprites by 5% during a Fortnite match, cutting short the amount of effort you have to put in. Below, you can find the marked locations where Fortnite streamers and creators have previously found gem sprites.

Island between Chopped Shop and The Battlewoods

In the north-west of the Battle Royale map, sandwiched between Chopped Shop and The Battlewoods, there is a leaf-shaped island with a few red cliffs. Once you are there, go to the top of the highest cliff where you can find a special chest adjacent to the red shack. Opening this particular one has rewarded a player with a gem sprite before.

Extraction site between Zero Point and Sinister Strip

Right above Sinister Strip on the map, close to the Zero Point, there is an extraction site where you need to go. There, you will find a standard chest that is known to have spawned a gem sprite in the past.

Frosted Flats

Frosted Flats has turned out to be one of the more common sources of gem sprites in Fortnite. There are at least a few different locations from which players have obtained these sprites to add to their collection.

First off, head to the north-west direction from Frosted Flats. About a five-second sprint away from the bridge, there is a tree adjacent to a rock where you will find a chest that can provide a gem sprite.

To proceed with the second location, go to the ‘frosted’ part of Frosted Flats, the spot with the snow-capped buildings and hills. There, inside a small brick-and-mortar structure, there are a couple of chests, one of which has previously spawned the sought-after gem sprite.

Other ways to get gem sprites in Fortnite

Indexing it from a friend

If you are struggling to get your hands on a gem sprite the traditional way, you can simply recruit a friendly player who already has it to share the sprite with you. For this, you can go to the official Fortnite Discord and visit the “sprite-runners-network” channel. Once you find someone willing to help, enter a Fortnite match together with him. Let him drop the desired sprite for you to extract.

Then, partake in another match with him and return the sprite to the original owner. While doing this removes the sprite from your collection, since it has already been indexed, you can recall it at any time from the Sprites tab using a certain amount of Sprite Dust.

Taking it from an opponent

You don’t really have to go on a chest-hunting spree or ask for help to add gem sprites to your inventory. To be more precise, you also have the option to snatch it from another player during a match.

For this approach to work, it is advisable to go through which sprite each opponent has equipped on their back while you are still on the Spawn Island. Memorize the appearance of the opponent who has your desired sprite and then exit the Battle Bus at the same time as him. Once on the ground, chase after and eliminate him to claim the desired sprite from the dropped loot.

Rounding up

The introduction of gem sprites has added another layer of variety to what’s already available in Fortnite. In doing so, the devs also increased the sprite count in the game to 117. Importantly, this was also the last wave of sprites to be added in Chapter 7 Season 3.

While sprites are confirmed to continue into the gaming-themed Fortnite Override, those sprites will actually be a completely fresh set. On the other hand, Fortnite Runners’ sprites will be moved to the Sprite Garden island and won’t be available for use in Battle Royale matches. Regardless, the forthcoming seasonal update promises even more in this gameplay aspect, as Epic Games doubles down on its experience with sprites from this season and applies it to the next one.

  • How to get Pollo Sprite in Fortnite
  • How to get Ironmouse Sprite in Fortnite

title.rendered: ChatGPT for Mac can now remember everything you do on your computer

content.rendered:
OpenAI has added a new Computer History feature to the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS. Once you opt in, it records your activity across the apps and websites you choose and turns it into memories and a timeline that ChatGPT and Codex can use in future conversations. OpenAI announced the feature on August 13, and it replaces Chronicle, the screenshot-based research preview the company tested earlier this year.

The idea is simple: if ChatGPT knows what you were working on, you don’t have to explain it every time. OpenAI says the assistant can pick up tasks where you left off, understand how you work, and suggest skills or automations based on your habits.

No screenshots this time

Chronicle worked by capturing screenshots of your screen, which drew obvious comparisons to Microsoft’s Recall. Computer History drops that approach entirely. According to OpenAI’s Computer History documentation, it records interaction events through macOS accessibility features instead, things like clicks, typing, keyboard shortcuts, and app switching.

OpenAI is clear about what stays out: no screenshots, no screen recordings, no microphone input, no system audio, and nothing from private browsing windows.

Here’s how the data flows. Interaction events sit on your Mac for up to 48 hours. OpenAI processes those temporary event files on its servers to generate memories, then deletes them unless it’s legally required to keep them. The finished memories are stored as plain-text files on your Mac until you delete them, and none of it is used to train OpenAI’s models.

You stay in control, mostly

Computer History is off by default, and turning it on takes a deliberate trip to Settings > Integrations in the Mac app. From there, you can pause collection anytime, exclude specific apps and websites, inspect every memory file, delete individual items, or wipe the whole history. A menu bar indicator shows what’s being captured.

There’s one warning worth taking seriously: OpenAI itself says the feature increases the risk of prompt injection from content in the apps and websites you visit. The company recommends pausing collection when you’re handling confidential material. That’s an unusual caveat for a feature built to watch everything you do. If you’d rather keep AI off your activity entirely, you can still run an open-source ChatGPT model offline on your Mac, though you give up features like this.

Who gets it

Computer History is available now for ChatGPT Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. Business and Enterprise admins have to enable it for their workspace first, and even then, each person must opt in individually. It doesn’t work if you sign in with an API key or through Amazon Bedrock.

Users in the EEA, Switzerland, and the UK are excluded at launch, with access expected in the coming weeks.

The feature is another sign of how much OpenAI wants the ChatGPT app on Mac to be more than a chat window. Between Codex landing in the desktop app in July and earlier additions like Record Mode and cloud drive access, the app is steadily turning into an assistant that works across your whole Mac. Whether you want it remembering your whole workday is a question only you can answer, but at least this time, the answer starts with “off.”

title.rendered: Apple warns spyware targets in 110 countries, and the alert now hits your Lock Screen

content.rendered:
Apple sent a fresh round of mercenary spyware threat notifications on Thursday, and the company confirmed to TechCrunch that targeted users in 110 countries received them. It is one of the widest waves since Apple started sending these alerts in 2021.

The delivery changed with this round. According to Apple’s updated threat notifications support document, the warning now appears directly on the iPhone Lock Screen and in Settings, alongside the usual email from threat-notifications@email.apple.com and a banner at the top of account.apple.com after you sign in. Until now, a warning could sit unread in an inbox for days. A Lock Screen alert is hard to miss.

The push alert reads: “Apple detected a mercenary spyware attack targeted at your iPhone. There are actions you can take now to protect your data and device.”

John Scott-Railton, a senior researcher at Citizen Lab, first flagged the new round on X and called the push alerts “a big improvement.” As he told TechCrunch, “Notifications create a critical signal that a community is being targeted. People get an alert, and then some of them reach out and seek help. Often this kicks off an investigation that reveals many, many more cases.”

Who these warnings are for

Mercenary spyware is government-grade surveillance software, like NSO Group’s Pegasus, that costs millions of dollars to deploy and targets a very small number of people, usually journalists, activists, politicians, and diplomats. Almost no one reading this will ever get one of these alerts.

Apple says the notifications are high-confidence alerts based entirely on its internal threat intelligence, and it deliberately doesn’t explain what triggers them so attackers can’t adapt. It also doesn’t attribute the attacks to any country or company. Since 2021, Apple has notified users in over 150 countries across multiple waves a year.

What to do if you get one

First, confirm the alert is real. Sign in to account.apple.com, and a genuine notification will appear at the top of the page. Apple never asks you to click links, open files, install apps or profiles, or share your Apple Account password or verification code, so anything that does is a scam dressed up as a warning.

If the notification is genuine, Apple recommends turning on Lockdown Mode and getting expert help from the Digital Security Helpline at Access Now, a nonprofit that runs it around the clock. Apple says it isn’t aware of a single successful mercenary spyware attack against a device with Lockdown Mode turned on.

For everyone else, the standard advice holds: keep your iPhone updated, use two-factor authentication on your Apple Account, turn on Stolen Device Protection, and stick to the App Store for apps.

title.rendered: WhatsApp may get chat themes with animated wallpapers on iOS

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is reportedly developing new chat themes with animated wallpapers for iPhone users. The feature was spotted in the latest WhatsApp beta for iOS and appears to build on similar customization options already discovered on Android. However, there’s an important catch: the feature is still under development and isn’t available to beta testers yet.

If released, the new themes could give WhatsApp chats a more dynamic look while keeping the animations subtle enough that they don’t distract from conversations.

WhatsApp is adding subtle animations to chat themes

According to WABetaInfo, the latest WhatsApp beta available through TestFlight includes revamped chat themes organized into three categories: Featured, Doodle, and Minimal. The setup is similar to the chat customization options recently spotted in a WhatsApp beta for Android.

The Featured category is where things get more interesting. It’s expected to include wallpapers with subtle animations, giving WhatsApp conversations a sense of movement without turning every chat into a visual distraction.

Fast-moving backgrounds might look impressive in a product demo, but they could quickly become annoying when you’re trying to read a long conversation. WhatsApp’s reported approach instead uses slow, gradual animations designed to add some personality to chats while keeping messages at the center of attention.

The Doodle category will reportedly build on WhatsApp’s familiar doodle-style artwork, while Minimal will offer cleaner and simpler backgrounds. These are expected to include solid white and black options that automatically adapt depending on whether the iPhone is using light or dark mode.

Chat bubble colors could change automatically

WhatsApp is also reportedly linking chat bubble colors to individual themes. Instead of requiring users to manually choose a bubble color that matches their wallpaper, WhatsApp would automatically select a complementary color combination for each theme.

That may sound like a small detail, but it could make the entire customization experience feel much more polished. Users could simply choose a theme and get a coordinated combination of wallpaper, animation, and chat bubble colors without adjusting each visual element separately.

WhatsApp has also been experimenting with other interface animations on iPhone. A previous beta update reintroduced message animations on iOS along with a dedicated setting for controlling them.

Taken together, these changes suggest WhatsApp is moving toward more complete visual customization packages rather than treating wallpapers, bubble colors, and animations as separate options.

When will WhatsApp animated wallpapers launch?

There’s no confirmed release date for animated chat wallpapers yet. WhatsApp is still developing the feature and hasn’t announced when the revamped chat themes will become available to beta testers or roll out to everyone.

The fact that similar customization features have now been spotted on both iOS and Android suggests WhatsApp is working toward a more consistent visual experience across the two platforms.

However, features discovered during beta development can still change significantly before release, and WhatsApp could modify or remove some of these options before they reach the stable app.

Would you use animated wallpapers in your WhatsApp chats, or do you prefer keeping your conversations simple? Let us know in the comments below.

title.rendered: Google Pixel Tag vs. Apple AirTag: Has Google finally beaten Apple?

content.rendered:
Google has finally launched its own Pixel Tag, giving Android users a first-party tracker to take on Apple’s popular AirTag. It may have arrived late, but Google isn’t simply playing catch-up. With Find Hub, Ultra Wideband, Precision Finding, and a replaceable battery, Pixel Tag looks like a serious competitor from day one.

But the big question is simple: has Google finally built an AirTag killer, or is Apple still one step ahead? Here, I’ve shared a detailed comparison of the Pixel Tag vs AirTag based on their accuracy, tracking range, battery life, privacy, smart features, and price to see which Bluetooth tracker is better.

Google Pixel Tag vs. Apple AirTag: Quick comparison

What is the Google Pixel Tag?

The Pixel Tag is Google’s first-party Bluetooth item tracker, designed to work with the company’s Find Hub network. Google already had Find Hub. What it lacked was its own tracker. That’s now changing.

Unlike the AirTag, which has a circular design, the Pixel Tag comes in an oval and pill-shaped design. It is made of metal and polycarbonate, weighs around 12 grams, and measures 1.8 x 1.1 inches with a thickness of 0.2 in. It carries an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance.

It also has:

  • Bluetooth
  • Ultra Wideband (UWB)
  • A built-in speaker
  • A replaceable CR2032 battery
  • Left Behind alerts
  • Precision Finding
  • A physical button for finding your phone
  • Google Find Hub integration
  • Multi-person item sharing

Google says the battery should last more than a year.

Apple AirTag is not the same AirTag anymore

Here’s where this comparison gets interesting. If you are picturing the original 2021 AirTag, stop. Compared to AirTag 1, Apple’s current AirTag is a second-generation product with improved hardware.

Apple says the latest AirTag has a 50% louder speaker and up to 1.5× greater Precision Finding range than its predecessor. It also uses Apple’s second-generation Ultra Wideband chip and an upgraded Bluetooth chip.

The current AirTag remains:

  • Replacable battery with up to one year of life
  • IP67 rated
  • Powered by a replaceable battery
  • Integrated with Apple’s Find My network
  • Equipped with UWB 2 for Precision Finding
  • Compatible with Apple’s Find My ecosystem

In other words, Google isn’t beating up an old AirTag. It’s walking into a fight with AirTag 2.

Pixel Tag vs. AirTag: Price is a draw

Google didn’t try to win the Pixel Tag vs. AirTag battle by making its tracker cheaper. Instead, it did something much more interesting: it matched Apple dollar for dollar.

And that’s actually good news for Google. If Pixel Tag had launched at $39 or $49, I’d immediately question its value proposition. You’re asking Android users to move away from established third-party trackers while charging a premium for the privilege.

Instead, Google has effectively said: AirTag costs $29. So does Pixel Tag. Choose your ecosystem. And I think that’s the right strategy. The real battle starts when you stop looking at the price and consider what mobile you use.

Google has one feature Apple doesn’t: A phone-finding button

This is my favorite Pixel Tag feature. And it’s also the sort of feature that sounds trivial until you actually need it.

The Pixel Tag has a physical button that can make your connected phone ring, even if it’s on silent. Think about the number of times you’ve searched your house for your phone while it’s under your couch. In such situations, I now only need to press the button on the tag.

Apple’s AirTag doesn’t have an equivalent physical button.

These tiny quality-of-life features are exactly what makes Google feel less like it’s merely copying Apple.

Winner: Pixel Tag.

Design and build quality: Which feels better built?

This is where the Pixel Tag surprised me.

Google could have played it safe and simply copied the AirTag’s little disc. Instead, it went in a different direction. The Pixel Tag has a slim, elongated oval shape and measures just 5.4mm thick, giving it a noticeably thinner and different silhouette from Apple’s round AirTag. And honestly? I like it.

And don’t worry; Google assures that it is “designed to resist flexing and cracking.” There’s also a silver metal face, with Google’s familiar G logo in the center, and the speaker cutout underneath it. Flip the tracker over, and you get a Fog-colored plastic back with the battery cutout.

On the other hand, the AirTag’s circular design has become a standard. You will get lots of different types of accessories and cases designed specifically around it. The enclosure is made of 85% recycled plastic and 100% fiber-based packaging.

Both trackers have IP67 water and dust resistance ratings, ensuring they can withstand splashing water, rain, and even accidental drops. However, the only thing that doesn’t fully convince me about the design is that both tags lack an integrated keyring hole; you will need a separate holder/case to carry them with your keys or luggage.

Winner: Pixel Tag.

Pixel Tag vs. AirTag: Which has the better tracking network?

This is the battle that actually matters. A Bluetooth tracker isn’t very interesting when it’s sitting next to you. The magic happens when you leave your suitcase in an airport, forget your keys behind, or accidentally leave your backpack somewhere. That’s where the network comes in.

Apple’s AirTag uses the Find My network, leveraging nearby Apple devices to anonymously relay the approximate location of your lost item. Its upgraded second-generation Ultra Wideband chip also improves Precision Finding up to 60 meters. I like AirTag’s sharing feature that helps find lost luggage at airports.

The improved speaker makes the tag easier to hear when it is hidden nearby. Add Left Behind alerts, encrypted location sharing in the Find My app, and unwanted-tracking protections, and AirTag 2 remains one of the most capable item trackers around.

Google’s Pixel Tag uses Find Hub, which Google says taps into more than one billion Android devices. Moreover, the Pixel Tag has an accelerometer, speaker, Bluetooth, and Ultra Wideband (UWB). With Precision Finding, you get visual distance and directional cues to help locate a nearby tag up to 50 meters away.

Google also includes familiar AirTag-style features such as Left Behind alerts, playing a sound on your Google Pixel Tag, or even asking Gemini to ring it for you, as well as the ability to share a tag’s location with up to 10 people.

Winner: Tie.

Privacy and anti-stalking protection: Google finally plays by Apple’s rules

A tracker that can help you find your lost keys can also be misused to track people. So privacy and anti-stalking protections aren’t optional extras; they’re part of what makes a tracker worth trusting.

The good news is that Google has essentially matched Apple’s approach here. Android devices can alert you when an unknown tracker is detected traveling with you, helping protect against someone secretly placing a Pixel Tag in your bag, car or belongings.

Even better, the protection isn’t locked inside Google’s ecosystem. Thanks to a collaboration between Google and Apple, Tracking Notifications are cross-platform. That means an iPhone can warn you about an unfamiliar Pixel Tag, while an Android phone can alert you about an unknown AirTag traveling with you.

I genuinely think this is one of the most important parts of the Pixel Tag.

Winner: Tie.

Has Google beaten Apple with Pixel Tag?

No, but Google has beaten my expectations. And that’s actually a compliment. I expected Google’s first tracker to be a generic AirTag clone with a Pixel logo.

Instead, Google has built something that makes several thoughtful improvements:

  • A phone-finding button
  • Support for up to 10 shared users
  • UWB Precision Finding
  • Bluetooth 6.0 capabilities
  • A thin, distinctive design
  • More than one year of replaceable-battery life
  • Find Hub integration
  • A $29 price point

At the same time, Apple still has enormous advantages:

  • A mature Find My network
  • A massive AirTag accessory ecosystem
  • A proven tracking experience
  • Excellent integration across Apple’s hardware
  • A refined second-generation AirTag
  • A strong head start in consumer awareness

So no, Pixel Tag hasn’t dethroned AirTag.

My verdict: Pixel Tag wins for Android, AirTag wins for iPhone

If you forced me to choose one tracker for an Android phone today, I’d buy Pixel Tag. Not because it is dramatically more advanced. I’d choose it because Google has finally made the tracker feel like a native part of Android, rather than an accessory built by someone else for Google’s platform.

However, if you’re on iPhone, buy the AirTag and don’t overthink it.

More interesting reads:

  • Apple Wallet vs Google Wallet
  • Fitbit Air vs Whoop 5.0
  • Google Pixel Watch 5 vs. Apple Watch Series 11

title.rendered: Google Pixel 11 Pro vs. iPhone 17 Pro: Which compact flagship should you buy?

content.rendered:
Google has unveiled its next flagship, the Pixel 11 Pro, and I think it has landed at exactly the right time. With its compact 6.3-inch design, Tensor G6 chip, upgraded cameras, and deeper AI features, Google is taking direct aim at the iPhone 17 Pro.

On paper, these two phones look remarkably close. In practice, they have very different personalities. So, here I’ll share a detailed comparison of the Google Pixel 11 Pro vs. iPhone 17 Pro, covering design, display, performance, cameras, battery life, AI features, and long-term value. So you can decide which compact flagship you should buy.

Google Pixel 11 Pro vs. iPhone 17 Pro: Quick comparison

Design and size: Which phone is actually more compact?

I’m glad Google and Apple still make Pro phones in this size. The 6.3-inch form factor is the sweet spot for people who want a premium phone without carrying around a giant slab.

The Pixel 11 Pro measures about 6 x 2.8 x 0.3 in and weighs 198g, while the iPhone 17 Pro is 5.91 x 2.83 x 0.34 in and weighs 206g. In other words, the iPhone is slightly shorter, while the Pixel is fractionally narrower, thinner, and lighter. Neither is dramatically more compact, though.

Both use an aluminum frame and a glass back, with the Pixel using a polished metal frame and Corning Gorilla Glass Victus 2 with a silky matte finish, and the iPhone using an aluminum unibody and Ceramic Shield on the rear and Ceramic Shield 2 on the front. Both also carry an IP68 rating, so everyday splashes and dust aren’t something I’d worry about.

In my hand, the difference comes down more to shape and weight distribution than dimensions. The Pixel’s familiar camera bar gives it a distinctive feel, now thinner and all-glass. Moreover, the new HiLight lets you identify calls from your favorite contacts. But I felt the iPhone was marginally easier to manage one-handed because of its slightly shorter body.

My verdict: The iPhone 17 Pro wins narrowly on ergonomics, but the Pixel 11 Pro has a more distinctive design. I liked its new matte aesthetic in Obsidian color.

Display: Pixel 11 Pro is brighter than ever

This is one area where Google’s numbers are genuinely impressive.

The Pixel 11 Pro packs a 1280 × 2856 resolution, around 495 ppi, with a tall 20:9 aspect ratio. The iPhone 17 Pro uses a 2622 × 1206 resolution at 460 ppi with a 19.5:9 aspect ratio. In practice, both are incredibly sharp, but text and fine details look a little denser on the Pixel.

Where Google really pulls ahead is brightness. The Pixel 11 Pro’s Super Actua display reaches a claimed 2400 nits HDR and 3600 nits peak brightness. The iPhone 17 Pro’s 6.3-inch Super Retina XDR display reaches up to 1600 nits HDR and 3,000 nits outdoors. That difference sounds small, but I can finally see my screen under direct sunlight with Pixel.

Apple fights back with more convincing anti-reflective treatment. Its Ceramic Shield 2 includes an Apple-designed coating that improves scratch resistance and reduces glare. The Pixel also upgraded to Corning Gorilla Glass Victus 2 with a 2x stronger anti-scratch shield. However, it doesn’t give me quite the same confidence about reflections.

Both are excellent OLED displays with 1-120Hz refresh rates and support HDR and always-on functionality. But if you regularly use your phone outdoors, I would take the Pixel’s display.

My verdict: I’d give the Pixel 11 Pro the display win for its higher pixel density and exceptional brightness. But if glare reduction, color accuracy, and overall refinement matter more to you, the iPhone 17 Pro remains an outstanding screen.

Performance: Tensor G6 vs. A19 Pro

Here’s where I’m less enthusiastic about Google’s Tensor strategy.

Google’s Tensor G6 is built on TSMC’s 2nm process and uses a 7-core CPU, an upgraded TPU with 50% more compute, MediaTek’s M90 5G modem, and Titan M3 security hardware. Moreover, the advanced vapor chamber helps sustain peak performance.

This time, the focus is clearly on efficiency and on-device AI. Google claims roughly 25% faster web browsing, 15% quicker app launches, and up to 20% better power efficiency, while its TPU is designed to accelerate Gemini Intelligence’s proactive assistance and Live Translate for media.

Apple’s A19 Pro, meanwhile, uses a 6-core CPU, a 6-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a 16-core Neural Engine. Apple also adds a vapor chamber to help sustain performance under heavy loads.

In everyday use, both should feel extremely fast. But if I were gaming, editing 4K video, or running demanding apps for long sessions, I’d pick the iPhone. Apple’s GPU and hardware-accelerated Ray Tracing give the A19 Pro a clear performance advantage for AAA titles.

The Pixel doubles down where Google knows it can win. Tensor G6’s architecture is designed to make features such as Gemini-powered assistance, translation, and camera processing feel more central to the experience. I look forward to seeing how the new MediaTek modem handles connectivity issues, such as overheating and battery drain.

My verdict: iPhone 17 Pro wins raw performance and gaming; Pixel 11 Pro wins the AI argument. For longevity, I’d still trust the iPhone more for sustained heavy workloads.

Camera: This is where I would buy the Pixel

If you’re asking me where the Pixel 11 Pro starts becoming genuinely compelling, it’s the camera.

Pixel 11 Pro comes with a 50MP main camera, a 48MP ultrawide, a 48MP telephoto with OIS, and a 42MP autofocus front camera. Google also advertises up to 120x Pro Zoom, up to 50MP High-Res photos, 8K video, and Pro Stable Video. Combined with the Gemini AI assistance and editing features, that’s a serious camera system.

Camera Looks is my favorite addition. Instead of slapping a filter on a finished image, it changes how the Pixel processes the photograph at capture time. Similar to Apple’s Photographic Styles, you can choose styles such as Natural, Shadows, Vanilla, Digi, and Black Tie, then adjust elements like contrast and brightness.

Then there’s Magic Capture, which feels genuinely useful. You can record a moment and let Google’s AI automatically identify the best still images from the footage. I won’t have to worry about timing your shot perfectly anymore. Google has also added Instant Night Sight, which can capture low-light photos up to 4.5 times faster.

The iPhone 17 Pro has also stepped up its game. Apple now puts 48MP sensors across all three rear cameras. The telephoto uses a tetraprism design with a 56% larger sensor, offering a 4x optical telephoto and an 8x optical-quality option. You also get 48MP macro photography, ProRAW, and an extensive computational photography stack.

However, since I love recording videos, the iPhone 17 Pro remains my favorite. It can record 4K Dolby Vision at up to 120fps on the Fusion Main camera, supports ProRes up to 4K/120fps with external recording, ProRes RAW, Dual Capture, Cinematic mode, Audio Mix, and Spatial recording.

My verdict: The Pixel 11 Pro looks like the photographer’s phone; the iPhone 17 Pro remains the creator’s phone.

Battery life and charging: Pixel’s 30+ hour claim is hard to ignore

Battery capacity doesn’t tell the whole story, but the numbers here are interesting.

The Pixel 11 Pro packs a 4,850mAh Li-Ion battery, rated for 30+ hours of battery life. Google pairs that larger battery with 30W wired charging using PD 3.0/PPS, charging up to 55% in just 30 minutes in Extreme Charging Mode. It also supports 25W magnetic wireless charging with PixelSnap and Qi2.2 and reverse wired charging.

Meanwhile, the iPhone 17 Pro offers up to 33 hours of video playback. That gives Google a noticeable capacity advantage on paper. In terms of wired charging, it goes up to 50% in 20 minutes when paired with a compatible 40W+ AVS-supported power brick. Apple is also equipped with 25W wireless MagSafe/Qi2 and 4.5W reverse wired.

If Google has genuinely managed 30+ hours without making the phone unwieldy, that’s one of the Pixel 11 Pro’s biggest achievements.

My verdict: Pixel 11 Pro wins on battery capacity and everyday endurance potential; iPhone 17 Pro wins on charging speed.

AI and software: Android 17 vs. iOS 26

This is probably the biggest difference between the Pixel 11 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro: Google wants AI to feel like the phone itself, while Apple treats AI as a powerful layer across iOS.

The Pixel 11 Pro runs Android 17, with Gemini deeply integrated into the experience. I love how Gemini Intelligence helps me find information, take action, and automate tasks across apps. And the best part is that Pixel 11 Pro buyers get six months of Google AI Pro at no cost, which unlocks higher Gemini usage limits, deeper access to Gemini, and 5TB of cloud storage.

Apple takes a different route with iOS 26 and Apple Intelligence. Features are woven into apps and everyday tasks, including writing tools, Image Playground, Visual Intelligence, intelligent shortcuts, and Live Translation. Apple is also developing a much more capable Siri AI, with richer answers and more natural conversations coming later this year.

From my perspective, Gemini feels more ambitious, while iOS feels more controlled. Pixel gives me more reasons to actively use AI; iPhone makes AI feel like something quietly working in the background. Another major advantage of Pixel is longevity: Google promises seven years of OS and security updates, along with regular Pixel Drops.

My verdict: Pixel 11 Pro wins AI and long-term software value; iPhone 17 Pro wins software polish and ecosystem integration. If AI is genuinely part of how you use your phone, I’d take the Pixel.

Ecosystem: The decision that can matter more than specs

This is the category that can completely reverse my recommendation.

If you own a MacBook, iPad, and Apple Watch, buy the iPhone 17 Pro. Don’t overthink it. AirDrop, iCloud, FaceTime, Apple Watch integration, Continuity, and the overall Apple ecosystem create a level of frictionless interaction that is difficult to reproduce when you switch platforms.

The Pixel 11 Pro is the obvious choice if you’re already invested in Google services, Android, Pixel Buds, or Pixel Watch. All these devices work together through cross-device controls, automatic audio switching, and Gemini integration. Google is also making the transition easier, with new Tap to Share and upgraded transfer and setup tools for people switching to Pixel.

But ecosystems have gravity.

If your laptop features an Apple logo and your wrist has an Apple Watch, the iPhone 17 Pro isn’t simply another smartphone. It’s the missing piece of the ecosystem you’ve already built. That is why I wouldn’t recommend switching to Pixel, even if it wins this comparison.

My verdict: iPhone 17 Pro wins the ecosystem battle, and it’s not particularly close.

Storage, pricing, and long-term value

At this price, I don’t think storage should be an afterthought. Both phones start at 256 GB and are priced at $1,099.

The iPhone 17 Pro starts at $1,099 in the U.S. for the 256GB model, with Apple also offering 512 GB and 1 TB configurations. With Apple’s new Upgrade leasing program, you need to pay $31.99/month for 24 months, or $45.99/month for 12 months, before taxes and trade-in credits.

However, in terms of value for money, the Pixel 11 Pro stands out. Google offers the phone in 256GB with 12GB of RAM and 512GB and 1TB with 16GB of RAM. The higher configurations also use Zoned UFS storage, designed to improve storage performance and efficiency.

Google makes the launch more interesting. Buyers can choose $250 off the new Pixel Watch 5 or $200 in Google Store credit when purchasing the Pixel 11 Pro or Pro XL. There are also six months of Google AI Pro at no cost, including access to higher-level Gemini and additional AI benefits.

However, Apple has the advantage in resale value, while Google counters with long software support and a strong AI package.

My verdict: The Pixel 11 Pro offers better overall value, especially with 16 GB of RAM and the bundled Google AI Pro benefit. But if you upgrade frequently and care about resale value, the iPhone 17 Pro can make more financial sense over the long run.

Google Pixel 11 Pro vs. iPhone 17 Pro: Which one should you buy?

After spending time comparing these two, I don’t think there’s a single winner for everyone. The Pixel 11 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro are both excellent compact flagships, but they appeal to very different people.

Buy the Google Pixel 11 Pro if you want a more interesting compact flagship.

  • Better point-and-shoot photography with Google’s computational photography, Camera Looks, and Magic Capture.
  • Smarter AI experience with Gemini deeply integrated and six months of Google AI Pro included.
  • More RAM and storage flexibility with 16 GB of RAM and up to 1 TB of storage.
  • Brighter display that’s easier to see outdoors.
  • Long-term support with seven years of OS and security updates.
  • Bigger battery and strong everyday endurance.
  • Better launch value, including $250 off Pixel Watch 5 or $200 Google Store credit.

Buy the iPhone 17 Pro if you want the most dependable all-rounder.

  • Faster performance thanks to the A19 Pro chip.
  • Better for video creators with Apple’s Pro video tools and recording capabilities.
  • Best ecosystem integration if you own a Mac, iPad, Apple Watch, or AirPods.
  • Polished iOS experience with strong hardware-software integration.
  • Excellent camera system with three 48MP rear cameras and an improved telephoto.
  • Stronger resale value and attractive upgrade/leasing options.

If you’re already deep in Apple’s ecosystem, don’t switch just because the Pixel has a better camera.

But if you’re platform-neutral and simply asking me, “Which compact flagship would you spend your own money on?” I’d pick the Google Pixel 11 Pro.

  • I compared Pixel Buds Pro 2 vs. AirPods Pro 3

title.rendered: I finally tried a third-party app store from Google Play: How it works

content.rendered:
Finally, after waiting for so long, the Google Play Store is offering a way to try third-party app stores. For years, if you wanted an app outside Google Play, you had to search for the APK and sideload it yourself. Now that’s changing.

When I first saw Aptoide Games, an alternative store, available through the Play Store, it felt like Google was finally letting a competitor through its own front door. So, I decided to try it myself to see what actually happens, how the experience works, and whether having a third-party app store inside Google Play is really as big a change as it sounds.

Google Play Store now lets you install third-party app stores directly

Let’s clear up the biggest misconception first. Third-party app stores are not new to Android. Samsung has its Galaxy Store, Amazon has its own app marketplace, F-Droid has long served open-source software, and Aptoide itself has existed for years. Android has always been considerably more permissive than iOS regarding alternative software distribution.

The problem was discoverability. If you wanted a third-party app store, you generally had to find it yourself and sideload it. That meant downloading an installer from an unknown website outside the Play Store and navigating Android’s security warnings. Most users are habituated to opening the Play Store whenever they want to get a new app or game.

Google’s new system changes that equation. Starting July 22, 2026, eligible third-party US Android app and game stores could be distributed through the Play Store. Google also began making the US Play catalog available to enrolled third-party stores under its new program.

And that’s how Aptoide ended up becoming the first rival storefront to appear inside Google Play.

How the third-party app store from Google Play Store actually works

Google has created a dedicated route for users to discover third-party app stores.

You can find these stores through a dedicated landing page, links within Play, your account menu in Google Play, the apps category page, or by searching (e.g., for “App Store” or a specific store). Then download it like a normal app. No need to go through additional security measures.

Once you install an eligible third-party store from Google Play, the experience moves into that store’s own ecosystem.

  • After installing Aptoide, I could explore its storefront and catalog. It includes free and paid gaming titles and popular apps.
  • I then downloaded Genshin Impact from Aptoide.
  • Once the download was complete, a prompt appeared. Clicking Install was the final step to get the game.
  • All the app payments and updates are managed by Aptoide, not Google.

As the experience remains seamless, I expect more storefronts like the Epic Games Store, Microsoft’s Xbox mobile ambitions, the Samsung Galaxy Store, and other open-source stores to be listed sooner. That means you will get various app catalogs, regional availability, independent games, and better offers and promotions.

Note: Alternative app stores operate under their own security and privacy practices, and Google Play does not review every application distributed through them. That’s why I hesitated a bit before trying new, unknown games from Aptoide.

The part that surprised me: Google Play can feed the competition

Here’s where things get genuinely interesting. Google isn’t merely allowing an alternative app store to sit beside Play.

Under the US program, enrolled third-party Android app stores can access the Google Play catalog. Apps and games can be offered through those stores, while the actual download can still be completed through the Play Store under the applicable terms. Google says its service fee continues to apply to those downloads.

However, the participating third-party stores must meet requirements including being legitimate marketplaces, operating as organizations, targeting US users, and maintaining trust-and-safety policies.

Why this happened: Epic changed the rules

None of this appeared out of nowhere. The roots go back to Epic Games’ long-running legal battle with Google over Android’s app distribution and billing practices.

In October 2024, Judge James Donato ordered Google to make major changes to the Play Store, including allowing competitors to distribute their app stores through it and giving them access to Google’s app catalog, subject to the terms of the injunction.

Google filed an appeal, and the battle for change went on. However, by 2026, both Google and Epic withdrew from pursuing their settlement proposal, leaving Google to comply with the underlying court order. Google subsequently confirmed that third-party app stores would begin appearing in the US Play Store from July 22.

There is a downside I am concerned about

Competition isn’t automatically good just because it has the word “competition” attached to it.

Multiple app stores can also mean:

  • Multiple accounts,
  • Update systems,
  • Payment systems,
  • Privacy policies,
  • Security models,
  • And eventually, multiple versions of the same app.

Right now, Google Play manages all your subscriptions and payment details. If every third-party store starts using its own payment system, your subscriptions could end up scattered across several accounts and wallets. This increases the chances of exposing your data.

I can also see how quickly things could get messy. Imagine searching for a game on Google Play only to discover it’s exclusive to another store. Now you have to download yet another app store just to play it. Do that a few times, and your phone could end up with several app managers.

So, should you install a third-party app store?

My answer is: If you have a reason, absolutely.

If Google Play already has everything you need, there’s no reason to install another store just because you can.

But if you care about:

  • alternative game catalogs
  • apps unavailable through Google Play
  • independent developers
  • regional releases
  • open-source software
  • different pricing
  • app-store competition
  • avoiding a single distribution gatekeeper

Then alternative stores are worth understanding.

Just treat them like a separate ecosystem, because that’s exactly what they are. Don’t assume Google Play’s security model follows you everywhere.

Always check the store’s reputation, pay attention to app permissions, prefer legitimate developers, and be especially cautious with modified or suspicious APKs. I will also insist that you keep Google Play Protect enabled to identify malicious behavior on your device.

For now, I am sticking to the Play Store as I use Gemini to search for apps instead of the traditional way.

The bottom line

For years, “Android is open” was technically true but not in practice. You could install alternative software, but the mainstream path still pointed toward Google Play. Not anymore!

If Google, Epic, Aptoide, Microsoft, Samsung, and others actually turn this opening into a real marketplace rather than a legal compliance exercise, Android users could finally get something they’ve been missing for years: a genuine choice of where their apps come from.

Are you excited to explore an alternative app store on your Android? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

excerpt.rendered: Android finally gets more app store choice inside Google Play. I walked through one to see what’s inside.

title.rendered: The Terminator skins are back in Fortnite: Here’s how to get them

content.rendered:
Fortnite cosmetics inspired by The Terminator are once again back in the Item Shop. In 2026, they have been added on three different occasions before, with the previous one being in June.

Comprising the Terminator promo are three outfits modeled around Arnold Schwarzenegger’s Terminator, T-800, and Sarah Connor. While the former was first introduced in 2023, the latter two were inserted into Fortnite’s skins catalog earlier in 2021. Moreover, Terminator and T-800 skins cost 1,500 V-Bucks, whereas the Sarah Connor skin is selling for 1,800 V-Bucks. All these items belonging to the highly popular sci-fi film series are up for grabs until August 14, 2026, at 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET.

Steps to get Terminator skins in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, navigate to the Shop tab.
  2. Next, scroll down to the Terminator section and select your desired skin.
  3. Finally, press and hold the Purchase button to confirm your decision.

Besides purchasing these skins individually, you can also grab them along with other relevant in-game items for a discounted price via their respective bundles. While the Terminator Bundle, worth 2,300 V-Bucks, includes the Terminator skin, the Future War Bundle, worth 2,800 V-Bucks, offers the Sarah Connor and T-800 skins.

All Terminator cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Skynet Llama (back bling)

Available with: Terminator skin, Terminator Bundle

2. HK-Aerial (glider)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Terminator Bundle

3. HK Skynet Uplink (back bling)

Available with: T-800 skin, Future War Bundle

4. Mimetic Poly Alloy Blades (pickaxe)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Terminator Bundle

5. Tow Truck Surfer (emote)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Terminator Bundle

6. Cyberdyne Salute (emote)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available with: Future War Bundle

7. Techno-Grip Axe (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Future War Bundle

8. Combat Knife (pickaxe)

Available with: Sarah Connor skin, Future War Bundle

9. T-800 Endoskeleton Arm (back bling)

Available with: Sarah Connor skin, Future War Bundle

Wrapping up

The Terminator is undoubtedly one of the most recognizable names in the sci-fi film genre. Hence, its combination with Fortnite is something major that draws interest from both gaming fans and movie buffs alike.

Besides The Terminator, quite a few different sci-fi behemoths have also collaborated with Fortnite over the years. These names include some of the biggest in the category and range from spacefaring franchises such as Star Wars to dystopian future classics such as Robo Cop. In the coming years, it will be interesting to see which new IPs are added to the list.

In case you missed:

  • How to get the Yoruichi Bleach Wave 2 skin in Fortnite
  • How to get Addison Rae skin in Fortnite
  • How to get Stranger Things skins in Fortnite
  • How to acquire power-ups in Fortnite Override

title.rendered: Download cute Penguin wallpapers to bring Antarctic scenes to your iPhone

content.rendered:
Penguin wallpapers have a special charm that makes them stand out from ordinary nature backgrounds. The cold blue tones, snowy landscapes, and those tiny cheerful faces somehow make my screen feel calmer and playful.

So, I decided to gather some cute Penguin wallpapers to brighten up your iPhone with a little Antarctic magic. If you’re looking for a simple way to give your iPhone a cozy winter vibe, these are worth a look.

Download adorable Penguin wallpapers in 4K  

I have curated different styles of penguin wallpapers in 4K that you can download for free. For more such exclusive wallpapers and fresh designs, check out our CrestWall app.

1. Emperor Penguin in the blue hour 

The first wallpaper immediately feels like stepping outside before sunrise on a freezing Antarctic morning. And you see an emperor penguin standing against an icy landscape, surrounded by drifting snow, distant mountains, and frozen water.

Its quiet composition leaves plenty of atmospheric space above it. That gives the Lock Screen a cinematic quality without making the screen feel crowded.

Best vibe:️ Calm, cinematic, moody

Download

2. Beautiful Penguin portrait 

This close-up is all about detail. I love the emperor penguin’s dark, textured feathers, bright yellow-orange markings, and beautifully defined beak. The background is intentionally soft and snowy, allowing the penguin to dominate your Lock Screen. On iPhone, that creates an amazing Depth Effect.

Best vibe: Cozy, detailed, elegant

Download

3. Group of Penguins walking at sunset 

Instead of one, this wallpaper has a long line of emperor penguins walking across an icy landscape. Meanwhile, the sunset introduces a soft golden glow that contrasts beautifully with white snow. This is like an Antarctic way of saying “let’s survive this day together”.

Best vibe: Warm, peaceful, hopeful

Download

4. Gentoo Penguin diving through sunbeams 

Now we’re underwater. This dramatic wallpaper captures a penguin diving through deep blue water. The shafts of sunlight from the top highlight Dynamic Island beautifully. I prefer deep ocean wallpapers because they create a rich, immersive background. Overall, it has the energy of an underwater adventure waiting every time you wake your phone.

Best vibe: Adventurous, dramatic, energetic

Download

5. Mother Penguin and her cute baby 

This might be the most heartwarming wallpaper in the collection. An adult emperor penguin feeding a tiny fluffy chick. The contrast between the adult’s sleek black-and-white feathers and the baby’s soft gray fluff makes the scene incredibly charming.

If you love wallpapers that make you happy effortlessly, then this one is an excellent choice.

Best vibe: Sweet, comforting, wholesome 

Download

6. Penguin leaping from the icy ocean 

The next one is a penguin caught in a spectacular moment, launching out of the ocean water with its flippers spread wide. It feels energetic without being aggressive, more like a little reminder to jump into whatever adventure is waiting for you.

Best vibe: Playful, energetic, adventurous

Download

7. Cheerful Penguin on glimmering ice 

Well, here we have a joyful penguin wallpaper! The Pip, the cute baby penguin, is walking on reflective ice, wearing a light-blue snowflake scarf. Its closed eyes, rosy cheeks, tiny orange beak, and cheerful expression make it heartwarming.

Best vibe: Cute, cheerful, playful

Download

8. Neon minimalist Penguin 

For something completely different, there’s this futuristic low-poly penguin constructed from illuminated geometric facets. I love its dark background sprinkled with tiny glowing points of light, giving the whole scene a sci-fi atmosphere.

If you are looking for minimalist wallpapers, go for this one.

Best vibe: Futuristic, artistic, dramatic

Download

9. Penguin beneath the Aurora lights 

This may be the most cinematic wallpaper of the entire collection. A lone penguin stands under enormous curtains of Aurora light across the night sky. The galaxy reflection on the ice creates almost a mirror image, making the scene feel surreal.

Best vibe: Magical, peaceful, awe-inspiring

Download

10. Whimsical Penguin under the moonlight 

The final wallpaper brings everything back to cute. A fluffy baby penguin sits in the snow beneath a huge glowing full moon. Snow-covered mountains surround the scene, while tiny stars fill the deep blue sky. This is the wallpaper I’d choose for a cozy nighttime setup.

Best vibe: Dreamy, cozy, whimsical

Download

Which Penguin wallpaper should you choose?

If you’re having trouble choosing just one, here’s a quick personality guide: 

Give your iPhone an Antarctic look! 

After using these penguin wallpapers on my iPhone, I found that each one gives the screen a different personality. The realistic penguins make it feel calm and natural, while the cute baby penguins add a cheerful touch that is hard not to smile at. I also love how the icy blues, warm sunset colors, and glowing auroras look on the iPhone display.  

And if you are having a hard time choosing between them, that’s the fun part. Apple supports Photo Shuffle, allowing you to cycle through multiple photos at selected intervals, so you don’t have to commit to just one favorite.

  • Download cute cat wallpapers for iPhone
  • Adorable and cute stitch wallpapers for iPhone

title.rendered: Apple reportedly wants to pay news publishers every time Siri AI uses their stories

content.rendered:
Apple is negotiating with news publishers to feed current news into the new Siri AI, according to The Wall Street Journal. The company is proposing multiyear deals where publishers get paid each time Siri actually uses their content, and it has reportedly discussed a possible nine-figure budget for the program.

No publishers are named yet, and nothing is signed. The proposed payment model differs from most current AI licensing deals.

Pay per use, not a flat fee

Most AI licensing deals work like a subscription: the AI company pays a set annual fee for broad access to a publisher’s archive and gets to use it however its products need. Apple’s proposal flips that into something closer to a royalty. If Siri pulls from a publisher’s reporting to answer a question, that publisher earns money on that use.

For publishers, that could be a better deal than a flat fee if Siri takes off across Apple’s billions of devices, or a worse one if people rarely ask Siri about the news. Either way, it ties the payout to real usage instead of a number negotiated up front.

Apple already licenses publisher content through Apple News+, and some of its earlier publisher agreements included rights to use content for AI training. These new talks are about something different: live access to current reporting, so Siri can answer questions about what is happening right now instead of leaning on stale training data.

Earlier news-summary errors explain Apple’s caution

Apple has already learned what happens when its AI gets the news wrong. In late 2024, Apple Intelligence notification summaries rewrote headlines into things publishers never said, including a false BBC summary that claimed a suspect had shot himself. Apple pulled AI news summaries entirely and only brought them back with iOS 26, more than a year later, with warnings attached.

Direct access would let Siri answer news questions from licensed reporting and identify the source instead of relying only on its training data.

Siri AI arrives this fall in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 as a chat-style assistant with its own app, after repeated delays pushed the Gemini-powered overhaul back. Access to current reporting would help it answer “what happened today” questions with named sources and fewer factual errors.

title.rendered: Leaked iPhone Ultra screen protectors show square corners on one side, rounded on the other

content.rendered:
Screen protectors said to be cut for Apple’s rumored foldable “iPhone Ultra” have surfaced with square corners on one edge and rounded corners on the other. Leaker Ice Universe shared photos and a short hands-on video of the protectors on X, offering a closer look at the possible front design of Apple’s first foldable.

The screen itself is not lopsided

Ice Universe first claimed the phone “actually has an irregular screen with one side square and the other round,” but walked that back in a follow-up post. The protector covers the entire glass front panel, not just the display area, which is why its corners don’t match.

The square edge sits on the hinge side of the foldable. The display underneath is still expected to be a normal symmetrical rounded rectangle with even bezels all around, so the finished phone shouldn’t look strange from the front.

The selfie camera moves to the corner

The protector has a single punch-hole cutout near the top-right corner instead of Apple’s usual top-center placement. That fits earlier reports that the foldable drops Face ID for a Touch ID side button, which lets Apple get away with one small camera hole instead of a wider cutout.

The protector’s proportions also back up the shorter, wider cover screen seen on the iPhone Ultra dummy unit that leaked earlier this year. Rumors point to a cover display of around 5.5 inches, with a 7.8-inch inner screen when the phone is open.

The leak fits Apple’s expected September timing

Retail-style screen protectors suggest accessory makers may already be working from leaked dimensions, although they don’t prove the phone’s final design. Apple is expected to announce the foldable alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup in mid-September. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo believes pre-orders could slip to October or later because of manufacturing constraints, with a price somewhere between $2,299 and $2,499.

None of this is confirmed until Apple shows the phone, and even the “iPhone Ultra” name is still a rumor. The protectors do, however, match the shorter and wider shape seen in earlier dummy-unit leaks.

title.rendered: Google announces Pixel Tag, a $29 AirTag rival arriving November 11

content.rendered:
Google has announced the Pixel Tag, its first item tracker, at the Made by Google event alongside the Pixel 11 series. It costs $29 for a single tag or $99 for a four-pack, exactly what Apple charges for the AirTag, and goes on sale November 11 on the Google Store.

How the Pixel Tag works

The Pixel Tag runs on Find Hub, Google’s tracking network of more than a billion Android devices. When your keys or bag are out of Bluetooth range, nearby Android phones anonymously relay the tag’s location, and Google says that location data is end-to-end encrypted.

Up close, the tag supports Ultra Wideband and Bluetooth Channel Sounding for precision finding, so your phone shows distance and direction cues that walk you right to the item. You’ll need a UWB-capable Android phone for that part; basic tracking works on any phone running Android 9 or later.

There’s a built-in speaker to ring the tag, and a button on the tag itself rings your phone in reverse. A tag can be shared with up to 10 people, and Left Behind alerts warn you when you walk away without your stuff.

The familiar shape needs an accessory

The tag is a stainless steel pill, about 1.8 by 1.1 inches and 5.4mm thick, with IP67 water and dust resistance and a user-replaceable CR2032 battery rated for about a year. Like the AirTag, it has no built-in attachment hole, so you’ll need a keychain loop or holder accessory to actually clip it to anything.

Why iPhone users should still pay attention

Google says unknown tracker alerts will flag a Pixel Tag that’s traveling with someone who doesn’t own it, and those safety alerts work across both Android and iPhone. Unlike the early AirTag anti-stalking protections, Google’s alerts will cover people outside its ecosystem from launch.

Apple launched the AirTag 2 in January at the same $29 single and $99 four-pack pricing, with a second-gen UWB chip and a louder speaker. Google is matching it dollar for dollar rather than undercutting it.

Android users have so far relied on third-party options like Chipolo and Pebblebee, the same names that fill out most AirTag alternative lists. Pixel Tag gives them a first-party option from November 11.

excerpt.rendered: Google’s first item tracker matches AirTag pricing at $29, runs on a billion-device Find Hub network, and warns both Android and iPhone users about unknown tags.

title.rendered: Everything Google Announced at the Pixel 11 Event: Pixel 11 Pro, Watch 5, & Pixel Tag

content.rendered:
Google packed a lot into its Made by Google event in New York on August 12. The company announced four Pixel 11 phones, the Pixel Watch 5, and its first AirTag-style tracker, the Pixel Tag, along with a long list of Gemini features. Pre-orders are open now, and everything except the Pixel Tag hits stores on August 20.

Here’s the full keynote if you want to watch it yourself.

Pixel 11 series starts at $899 with the first 2nm phone chip

Every Pixel 11 runs on the new Tensor G6, the first smartphone chip built on a 2nm process. Google says it’s up to 20% more power efficient than the Tensor G5, loads apps 15% faster, and runs on-device AI tasks 3.5x faster while using 3.5x less energy. All four phones ship with Android 17 and 256GB of base storage, double what the Pixel 10 started with.

That extra storage comes with a price bump. Each model costs $100 more than its Pixel 10 equivalent.

The base Pixel 11 gets the biggest visible redesign: an all-glass camera bar that’s 40% thinner than before. Its new 48MP main sensor pulls in 56% more light, and the 5x telephoto now reaches 30x SuperRes Zoom. Wireless charging jumps from 15W to 25W with Qi2.2, and Google claims over 30 hours of battery. It comes in Frost, Hibiscus, Pistachio, and Obsidian.

Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL push the camera harder

The Pro models get a new 50MP main sensor and a 48MP telephoto with 30% better light sensitivity, plus Portrait Mode at 5x zoom and a 120x Pro Zoom mode. Night Sight now captures up to 4.5x faster. The Super Actua display reaches 3,600 nits and has double the scratch resistance of the Pixel 10 Pro.

There’s also a new hardware detail called HiLight, an LED ring around the camera flash that lights up for important calls and when Gemini is listening. It replaces the temperature sensor from the previous Pro models.

The Pro XL charges to 75% in 30 minutes wired, and both Pro models include six months of Google AI Pro, which normally costs $19.99 a month and bundles 5TB of storage with Google Health Premium. Colors: Canyon, Fog, Olive, and a matte Obsidian.

Pixel 11 Pro Fold is lighter, thinner, and tougher

Google’s new foldable is nearly 10% lighter and almost 1mm thinner than the Pixel 10 Pro Fold, with a glass fiber composite back that Google says makes it three times more durable. It keeps full IP68 water and dust resistance.

The outer 6.5-inch screen is 20% brighter, the inner Super Actua Flex display hits 3,600 nits with slimmer bezels, and the main camera moves up to 48MP with 30x Super Zoom. The 4,750mAh battery is rated for over 24 hours. At $1,899, it’s $100 more than last year’s Fold.

Pixel Watch 5 leans into health trends

The Pixel Watch 5 starts at $399 for the 41mm size and $429 for 45mm, with cellular adding $100. That’s up $50 from the Pixel Watch 4. It ships August 20 alongside the phones.

The headline features are two new health reports in the Google Health app. Blood Pressure Trends estimates how your blood pressure patterns change over time using existing sensor data. It’s a monthly trend report, not a blood pressure monitor, and it doesn’t give real-time readings. Insulin Resistance Trends works the same way, estimating changes from your sleep, heart rate, and activity data. Google says it trained the model on 60 million hours of data from more than 100,000 people. The watch also adds breathing emergency detection, personalized strength coaching, and bedtime automations.

Under the hood, a Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 chip makes the watch about 20% faster, RAM goes from 2GB to 3GB, and storage doubles to 64GB. Battery life is rated at 30 hours for the 41mm and 40 hours for the 45mm, and a 15-minute charge adds around 15 hours. Google also reworked GPS tracking, claiming routes are twice as accurate.

Google is also selling a $579 Stephen Curry Edition with an exclusive band and watch face.

Pixel Tag is Google’s $29 answer to the AirTag

Google finally made its own item tracker. The Pixel Tag is a stainless steel, IP67-rated tag with ultra-wideband precision finding, a built-in speaker, and a replaceable coin-cell battery rated for about a year. It runs on Android’s Find Hub network, which spans over a billion Android devices, and works with any phone on Android 9 or later. You can also locate a tagged item from a Pixel Watch or ask Gemini to find it through Pixel Buds.

It costs $29, or $99 for a four-pack, and ships November 11, nearly three months after the phones and watch. That puts it at the same price as Apple’s AirTag and in line with most AirTag alternatives already on the market. Apple, for its part, is expected to answer with an AirTag 2 featuring a new UWB chip and better precision finding.

Gemini features worth knowing about

Google also added several Gemini-powered tools across Pixel, Gboard, and Live Transcribe:

  • Task automation: Gemini can order groceries, book rides, and call businesses on your behalf, leaving you a transcript of the call.
  • Rambler: A new Gboard voice input that cleans up filler words and run-on sentences, so dictation reads like something you’d actually type.
  • Sign language transcription: Live Transcribe can now translate American Sign Language to text using the Pixel Camera, built on a DeepMind model.
  • Magic Capture: The camera analyzes around 500 frames to automatically pick the best photos and videos.
  • Camera Looks: Preset styles like Natural, Vanilla, and Black Tie for consistent color across shots.
  • Live Translate dubbing: Real-time audio translation for podcasts and YouTube videos.

Pixel Buds Pro 2 got a new Olive color and a September software update with dynamic noise cancellation, Gemini audio controls, and Live Translate support for over 70 languages. The cheaper Pixel Buds 2a picks up Gemini audio control too.

excerpt.rendered: Google’s Pixel 11 event brought four new phones on the first 2nm chip, a health-focused Pixel Watch 5, and the company’s first AirTag rival, the $29 Pixel Tag.

title.rendered: How to get the Yoruichi Bleach Wave 2 skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Fortnite and Bleach have come together once again for an in-game collab, bringing a range of cosmetics inspired by the popular anime to Epic’s multiplayer title. The Bleach Wave 2 collab importantly features skins modeled around fan-favorite characters, Yoruichi Shihoin and Kisuke Urahara. While the Yoruichi Fortnite skin is available for 1,800 V-Bucks, the Kisuke one is up for grabs for 1,500 V-Bucks.

It’s worth noting that skins and other cosmetics from the first wave of Bleach-themed Fortnite content are also back on sale during this ongoing promotion. In other words, you have another chance to claim Fortnite skins inspired by Ichigo Kurosaki, Rukia Kuchiki, Orihime Inoue, and Uryu Ishida, with the first two costing 1,800 V-Bucks and the latter two 1,500 V-Bucks. All Bleach Wave 1 & 2 cosmetics are available for a limited time only, until August 14, 2026, at 5 PM PT or 8 PM ET.

Steps to get the Yoruichi or Kisuke skin in Fortnite

  1. In Fortnite, go to the Shop tab.
  2. Then, scroll down to the Bleach section and select your pick between the Yoruichi Fortnite skin and the Kisuke Fortnite skin.
  3. Lastly, select and hold the Purchase button to complete the transaction.

Alternatively, you can get Yoruichi and Kisuke skins along with other Bleach Wave 2 items in a single purchase via the Yoruichi Shihoin & Kisuke Urahara Bundle. It is priced at 2,400 V-Bucks and saves you a staggering 2,700 V-Bucks compared to what you would have spent by purchasing all included items separately.

All Bleach Wave 2 cosmetics in Fortnite

1. Yoruichi’s Cape (back bling)

Price: 300 V-Bucks
Also available with: Yoruichi Shihoin skin, Yoruichi Shihoin & Kisuke Urahara Bundle

2. Benihime (pickaxe)

Price: 800 V-Bucks
Also available with: Kisuke Urahara skin, Yoruichi Shihoin & Kisuke Urahara Bundle

3. Soul Candy (back bling)

Price: 400 V-Bucks
Also available with: Yoruichi Shihoin & Kisuke Urahara Bundle

4. Shunko Raijin Senkei (emote)

Price: 400 V-Bucks
Also available with: Yoruichi Shihoin & Kisuke Urahara Bundle

5. Kisuke Urahara Style (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Yoruichi Shihoin & Kisuke Urahara Bundle

6. Shunko Raijin Senkei Style (wrap)

Price: 500 V-Bucks
Also available with: Yoruichi Shihoin & Kisuke Urahara Bundle

Rounding up

After days of high anticipation, the Bleach Wave 2 collab in Fortnite is finally out in the Item Shop, with the Yoruichi skin driving numbers. This Flash Goddess is, in fact, among the best-selling items in the in-game store at the time of writing.

The latest team-up with Bleach marks yet another occasion where Fortnite has partnered with an anime franchise. In the past, highly popular IPs of the same kind, such as Attack on Titan, Jujutsu Kaisen, and Naruto, have received their own cosmetics in the live-service game. Given the strong fanfare surrounding anime, it should be reasonable to expect Fortnite devs to continue this tradition going ahead.

What to read next:

  • How to get Addison Rae skin in Fortnite
  • Fortnite x Sonic the Hedgehog crossover confirmed
  • How to get Spider-Man Brand New Day skins in Fortnite
  • How to get the Phantom Blade Zero skin in Fortnite

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Ro Ghoul Codes on September 07, 2026

Ro-Ghoul is the long-running Tokyo Ghoul fighting game on Roblox, and its grind is brutal without help. Ranking up a kagune or quinque eats millions of RC cells, and good masks cost serious Yen. The working codes below hand you tens of millions of RC and Yen, plus Color Credits and Hearts, before you fight anyone. That is hours of farming skipped in one sitting. Ro-Ghoul codes used to stay valid forever, but the dated update codes now expire with each patch cycle, so redeem the newest ones first.

How to redeem Ro-Ghoul codes

Older guides tell you to type !Code in chat. That was the old method; the game now has a proper code box.

  1. Open Ro-Ghoul on Roblox.
  2. Click the <//> button on the left side of the screen.
  3. Paste a working code into the text box.
  4. Click Submit Code to collect the reward.

Why a Ro-Ghoul code may not work

  • It expired: Check the expired list above before blaming your typing.
  • You typed it wrong: Codes like 03/04/26 upd and Kuzen1-K1-K2-PK1! are typo traps. Copy and paste instead.
  • You already used it: Every code works once per Roblox account.
  • You added the old prefix: !Code belongs to the retired chat method, not the code box.
  • Your server is old: After a new code drops, join a fresh server before trying it.

If a code fails in a fresh server after a clean paste, treat it as expired and move on. And if Roblox will not let you into a server at all, fix Roblox Error Code 279 before testing any codes.

Where to find more Ro-Ghoul codes

New codes arrive with updates, boss releases, anniversaries, and holiday events. Watch these official channels:

  • Ro-Ghoul Discord
  • SushiWalrus on X
  • Official [Ro-Ghoul] Roblox community

Since Ro-Ghoul codes no longer live forever, this page is worth bookmarking; we retest the list so you do not waste time on dead strings.

If you want more free rewards, check out the latest Ninja Time codes, Dragon Soul codes, and our complete list of all Roblox game codes.

In case you missed:

  • Giant Simulator Reborn codes
  • Legacy Piece codes

title.rendered: ChatGPT desktop app is now available on Linux in preview

content.rendered:
OpenAI has launched the ChatGPT desktop app for Linux, announced on X on August 11. The app is a preview build that brings ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, and Codex together in one native desktop app, and it is available worldwide from day one.

Linux was the last major desktop platform without an official ChatGPT app after macOS and Windows. OpenAI says Linux has been one of its most-requested platforms, and this launch finally puts the desktop app on all three.

What the Linux app can do

This is the same workspace-style app OpenAI ships on other desktops, not a wrapped-up website. You can organize chats into projects, work with local files without uploading them anywhere first, and use browser workflows inside the app. Codex is built in too, so it can run directly in your local repos, and ChatGPT Work handles multi-step tasks across apps for those on work plans.

The app is free to use with an OpenAI account, though some features still depend on your plan.

Supported distros and how to get it

OpenAI has tested the app on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and 26.04 LTS, Debian 13, and Fedora 43 and 44. Distros built on those bases should generally work as well, so most popular Ubuntu and Fedora flavors are covered.

You can grab it from OpenAI’s download page as a .deb or .rpm package, with both x64 and ARM64 builds available. The installer also adds an OpenAI repository to your system, so future updates arrive through your regular package manager instead of manual downloads.

It is still a preview, so expect rough edges

OpenAI is clear that this is a preview, and early feedback backs that up. Users in the community thread have already flagged issues like broken Japanese input on Fedora KDE under Wayland, and OpenAI warns that feature integrations may not work reliably yet. If you depend on ChatGPT for real work, the browser version is still the safer option for now.

The app is also closed source, which will not sit well with everyone on Linux. But OpenAI is not alone here anymore either. Anthropic brought its Claude desktop app to Linux about a month ago, so the two biggest AI chatbots now treat Linux as a platform worth shipping for rather than an afterthought.

title.rendered: WhatsApp is building a faster way to search chats on iPhone

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is working on a search button that sits right inside the chat screen on iPhone, according to WABetaInfo. References to the feature showed up in WhatsApp beta for iOS 26.31.10.70 on TestFlight. Tap the button and you can search that conversation directly, without leaving it.

That fixes a genuinely annoying detour. Right now, searching inside a chat on iPhone means tapping the contact or group name at the top, scrolling the chat info screen, and then tapping Search. iPad users get a quicker route through the More button, but the iPhone app has never had an in-chat shortcut.

The button only shows up when you scroll back

The new search button won’t sit on the screen permanently. It appears in the bottom-right corner once you start scrolling up through older messages and disappears again when you return to the bottom of the conversation, the same way the jump-to-latest-message arrow behaves now.

That placement makes sense. Scrolling back through months of messages is exactly the moment you give up and want to search instead, and the button will be right there when it happens.

The search itself is unchanged. The button opens the same in-chat search you get from the chat info screen today, including the calendar icon for jumping to messages from a specific date. What changes is how fast you reach it: one tap instead of a trip out of the conversation.

Not available yet, even in beta

The feature is still under development. WhatsApp hasn’t enabled it for beta testers, and there’s no word on a release date, so it could take a while to reach the App Store version. Beta references also don’t guarantee a feature ships at all, though a search shortcut this small and useful seems like a safe bet.

WhatsApp has been steadily filling gaps in its iOS app lately, from testing Meta AI summaries for unread messages to a connected peripherals listing in Linked Devices. Until the search button arrives, the chat info screen remains the way in, and there are plenty of other WhatsApp tricks on iPhone that work today.

excerpt.rendered: References in WhatsApp beta for iOS 26.31.10.70 point to a floating in-chat search button on iPhone, cutting the detour through the chat info screen.

title.rendered: iOS 27 beta code references all six iPhone 18 models, including the foldable

content.rendered:
Apple’s next iPhone lineup just surfaced in Apple’s own software. Macworld found references to six unreleased iPhone models in iOS 27 beta 5, tucked inside system files that handle battery drivers and Battery Intelligence. It is the first time the full rumored 2026-2027 lineup has shown up together in a beta.

Which iPhones the identifiers point to

The code only lists identifiers, not names. The matches below come from earlier leaks and Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reporting, so treat them as well-founded guesses rather than confirmations.

The identifiers do not reveal specs, designs, or prices. Their location still makes sense: iOS has to support each new phone’s power-management setup before the hardware ships, which is why unreleased models tend to leak through battery code first.

Earlier iOS 27 betas already contained references to foldable displays and dual-battery configurations that no current iPhone uses, both of which fit the foldable expected this fall. Gurman has also said much of iOS 27 itself is being built around that foldable, with features designed for its larger inner display.

The roadmap matches the split-launch reports

The six models line up with what Gurman and analyst Ming-Chi Kuo have been reporting for months: Apple plans to break the iPhone 18 generation into two waves instead of one September event. iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the foldable arrive this fall, while the standard iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and a second-generation iPhone Air follow in spring 2027.

Apple has not confirmed any of these devices, and identifiers can shift or get shelved before launch. But Apple preparing its own operating system for six specific new phones is harder to dismiss than a supply-chain rumor. If the schedule holds, September’s event will be a Pro-and-foldable show, and anyone waiting for a cheaper iPhone 18 has about six extra months to sit out.
